statement: connection.queries is only available if the DEBUG setting is True.

statement: connection.queries is a list of dictionaries in order of query execution, each with 'sql' and 'time' keys.
source_span:
It's a list of dictionaries in order of query execution. Each dictionary has
the following:

* ``sql`` - The raw SQL statement
* ``time`` - How long the statement took to execute, in seconds.

statement: connection.queries includes all SQL statements, such as INSERTs, UPDATEs, and SELECTs.

``connection.queries`` includes all SQL statements -- INSERTs, UPDATES,
SELECTs, etc.

statement: When using multiple databases, you can access each connection's query log via connections["my_db_alias"].queries.
source_span: >>> connections["my_db_alias"].queries

statement: Calling reset_queries() from django.db clears the recorded query list manually.
source_span:
call ``reset_queries()``, like this::

    from django.db import reset_queries

    reset_queries()

a

statement: RemoteUserMiddleware must be added to the MIDDLEWARE setting after AuthenticationMiddleware.

you must add the

:class:`django.contrib.auth.middleware.AuthenticationMiddleware`

statement: ModelBackend must be replaced with RemoteUserBackend in the AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS setting.

you must replace the :class:`~django.contrib.auth.backends.ModelBackend`

statement: If the REMOTE_USER value is not set and there is no fallback backend, the user is unable to log in, even using Django's admin interface.
source_span:
if the ``REMOTE_USER`` value is not set
then the user is unable to log in, even using Django's admin interface.

statement: Adding 'django.contrib.auth.backends.ModelBackend' to AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS as a fallback allows login to work when REMOTE_USER is absent.
source_span:
Adding ``'django.contrib.auth.backends.ModelBackend'`` to the
``AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS`` list will use ``ModelBackend`` as a fallback
if ``REMOTE_USER`` is absent, which will solve these issues.

statement: Users with is_active=False won't be allowed to authenticate via RemoteUserBackend; AllowAllUsersRemoteUserBackend must be used to allow them.
source_span:
Users with :attr:`is_active=False
<django.contrib.auth.models.User.is_active>` won't be allowed to
authenticate. Use
:class:`~django.contrib.auth.backends.AllowAllUsersRemoteUserBackend` if
you want to allow them to.

statement: A custom HTTP header can be used by subclassing RemoteUserMiddleware and setting its header attribute, e.g. header = 'HTTP_AUTHUSER'.
source_span:
class CustomHeaderRemoteUserMiddleware(RemoteUserMiddleware):
        header = "HTTP_AUTHUSER"

statement: RemoteUserMiddleware must not be deployed in configurations where a client can supply the header itself, to prevent header spoofing.
source_span:
``RemoteUserMiddleware`` must not be deployed in configurations where a
client can supply the header.

statement: Under WSGI with the default header configuration (REMOTE_USER), the spoofing warning doesn't apply because only the WSGI server can set a request.META key that doesn't start with HTTP_.
source_span:
Under WSGI, this warning doesn't apply to ``RemoteUserMiddleware`` in its
default configuration with ``header = "REMOTE_USER"``, since a key that
doesn't start with ``HTTP_`` in ``request.META`` can only be set by your
WSGI server, not directly from an HTTP request header.

statement: Under ASGI, the header-spoofing warning applies in all configurations, so ASGI deployments must use a reverse proxy.
source_span:
This warning applies under ASGI in all configurations, because there is
no equivalent for a WSGI server's ability to place a trusted value in the
environ. ASGI deployments *must* use a reverse proxy as described above
when using this middleware.

statement: PersistentRemoteUserMiddleware maintains the authenticated session until explicit logout by the user.
source_span:
It will maintain the authenticated session
until explicit logout by the user.

statement: RemoteUserBackend inherits from ModelBackend, so the same permissions checking implemented in ModelBackend still applies.
source_span:
Since the ``RemoteUserBackend`` inherits from ``ModelBackend``, you will
still have all of the same permissions checking that is implemented in
``ModelBackend``.

statement: The new opt-in mechanism in React 18 is called "concurrent rendering" and lets React prepare multiple versions of the UI at the same time.

statement: Concurrent rendering is only enabled for updates triggered by one of the new features, instead of an all-or-nothing "mode".

statement: Developers will be able to adopt React 18 without rewrites and try the new features at their own pace.

statement: Adult acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is a type of cancer in which the bone marrow makes too many lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell.
source_span: Adult acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is a type of cancer in which the bone marrow makes too many lymphocytes (a type of white blood cell).

statement: Adult ALL is also called acute lymphocytic leukemia.
source_span: also called acute lymphocytic leukemia

statement: Adult ALL usually gets worse quickly if it is not treated.
source_span: This type of cancer usually gets worse quickly if it is not treated.

statement: Previous chemotherapy and exposure to radiation may increase the risk of developing adult ALL.
source_span: Previous chemotherapy and exposure to radiation may increase the risk of developing ALL.

statement: Signs and symptoms of adult ALL include fever, feeling tired, and easy bruising or bleeding.
source_span: Signs and symptoms of adult ALL include fever, feeling tired, and easy bruising or bleeding.

statement: Adult ALL can spread to the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord).
source_span: The cancer can also spread to the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord).

statement: In Philadelphia chromosome positive ALL, part of one chromosome switches places with part of another chromosome, a change called the Philadelphia chromosome.
source_span: in Philadelphia chromosome positive ALL, part of one chromosome switches places with part of another chromosome. This is called the Philadelphia chromosome.

statement: Prognosis and treatment options for adult ALL depend on the patient's age, whether the cancer has spread to the brain or spinal cord, whether there are certain gene changes including the Philadelphia chromosome, and whether the cancer has been treated before or has recurred.
source_span: The prognosis (chance of recovery) and treatment options depend on the following: - The age of the patient. - Whether the cancer has spread to the brain or spinal cord. - Whether there are certain changes in the genes, including the Philadelphia chromosome. - Whether the cancer has been treated before or has recurr

statement: Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy for diagnosing adult ALL involves removal of bone marrow, blood, and a small piece of bone by inserting a hollow needle into the hipbone or breastbone.
source_span: The removal of bone marrow, blood, and a small piece of bone by inserting a hollow needle into the hipbone or breastbone.

statement: Other symptoms of adult ALL include petechiae, shortness of breath, weight loss or loss of appetite, bone or stomach pain, painless lumps in the neck/underarm/stomach/groin, and having many infections.
source_span: Petechiae (flat, pinpoint spots under the skin, caused by bleeding). - Shortness of breath. - Weight loss or loss of appetite. ... Painless lumps in the neck, underarm, stomach, or groin. - Having many infections.

statement: Adult acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a type of cancer in which the bone marrow makes abnormal myeloblasts (a type of white blood cell), red blood cells, or platelets.
source_span: Adult acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a type of cancer in which the bone marrow makes abnormal myeloblasts (a type of white blood cell), red blood cells, or platelets.

statement: AML is the most common type of acute leukemia in adults.
source_span: It is the most common type of acute leukemia in adults.

statement: AML is also called acute myelogenous leukemia, acute myeloblastic leukemia, acute granulocytic leukemia, and acute nonlymphocytic leukemia.
source_span: AML is also called acute myelogenous leukemia, acute myeloblastic leukemia, acute granulocytic leukemia, and acute nonlymphocytic leukemia.

statement: Possible risk factors for AML include being male, smoking especially after age 60, having had treatment with chemotherapy or radiation therapy in the past, having had treatment for childhood ALL, being exposed to radiation from an atomic bomb or the chemical benzene, and having a history of a blood disorder such as myelodysplastic syndrome.
source_span: Possible risk factors for AML include the following: - Being male. - Smoking, especially after age 60. - Having had treatment with chemotherapy or radiation therapy in the past. - Having had treatment for childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) in the past. - Being exposed to radiation from an atomic bomb or to the chemical benzene. - Having a history of a blood disorder such as myelodysplastic syndrome.

statement: Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) is a subtype of AML that occurs when parts of two genes stick together, usually in middle-aged adults, with signs that may include both bleeding and forming blood clots.
source_span: Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) is a subtype of AML that occurs when parts of two genes stick together. APL usually occurs in middle-aged adults. Signs of APL may include both bleeding and forming blood clots.

statement: Signs and symptoms of adult AML include fever, shortness of breath, easy bruising or bleeding, petechiae, weakness or feeling tired, and weight loss or loss of appetite.
source_span: Fever. - Shortness of breath. - Easy bruising or bleeding. - Petechiae (flat, pinpoint spots under the skin caused by bleeding). - Weakness or feeling tired. - Weight loss or loss of appetite.

statement: Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) may be done along with cytogenetic analysis to look for certain changes in the chromosomes when diagnosing AML.
source_span: Other tests, such as fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), may also be done to look for certain changes in the chromosomes.

statement: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is a type of cancer in which the bone marrow makes too many lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell.
source_span: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia is a type of cancer in which the bone marrow makes too many lymphocytes (a type of white blood cell).

statement: CLL is a blood and bone marrow disease that usually gets worse slowly, is one of the most common types of leukemia in adults, and rarely occurs in children.
source_span: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (also called CLL) is a blood and bone marrow disease that usually gets worse slowly. CLL is one of the most common types of leukemia in adults. It often occurs during or after middle age; it rarely occurs in children.

statement: Risk factors for CLL include being middle-aged or older, male, or white; a family history of CLL or cancer of the lymph system; and having relatives who are Russian Jews or Eastern European Jews.
source_span: Risk factors for CLL include the following: - Being middle-aged or older, male, or white. - A family history of CLL or cancer of the lymph system. - Having relatives who are Russian Jews or Eastern European Jews.

statement: CLL usually does not cause any signs or symptoms and is often found during a routine blood test; its main signs and symptoms are swollen lymph nodes and tiredness.
source_span: Signs and symptoms of chronic lymphocytic leukemia include swollen lymph nodes and tiredness. Usually CLL does not cause any signs or symptoms and is found during a routine blood test.

statement: Additional symptoms of CLL include painless swelling of the lymph nodes in the neck, underarm, stomach, or groin, feeling very tired, pain or fullness below the ribs, fever and infection, and weight loss for no known reason.
source_span: Painless swelling of the lymph nodes in the neck, underarm, stomach, or groin. - Feeling very tired. - Pain or fullness below the ribs. - Fever and infection. - Weight loss for no known reason.

statement: Patients with an IgVH gene mutation have a better prognosis.
source_span: Patients with an IgVH gene mutation have a better prognosis.

statement: Diagnostic tests for CLL include immunophenotyping, FISH (fluorescence in situ hybridization), flow cytometry, the IgVH gene mutation test, and bone marrow aspiration and biopsy.
source_span: Immunophenotyping ... FISH (fluorescence in situ hybridization) ... Flow cytometry ... IgVH gene mutation test ... Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy

statement: Chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) is a disease in which the bone marrow makes too many white blood cells.
source_span: Chronic myelogenous leukemia is a disease in which the bone marrow makes too many white blood cells.

statement: CML, also called chronic granulocytic leukemia, is a slowly progressing blood and bone marrow disease that usually occurs during or after middle age and rarely occurs in children.
source_span: chronic myelogenous leukemia (also called CML or chronic granulocytic leukemia) is a slowly progressing blood and bone marrow disease that usually occurs during or after middle age, and rarely occurs in children.

statement: Signs and symptoms of CML include fever, night sweats, tiredness, weight loss, and pain or fullness below the ribs on the left side.
source_span: Signs and symptoms of chronic myelogenous leukemia include fever, night sweats, and tiredness.

statement: Most people with CML have a gene mutation called the Philadelphia chromosome.
source_span: Most people with CML have a gene mutation (change) called the Philadelphia chromosome.

statement: The Philadelphia chromosome causes the bone marrow to make an enzyme called tyrosine kinase, which causes too many stem cells to become white blood cells (granulocytes or blasts).
source_span: It results in the bone marrow making an enzyme, called tyrosine kinase, that causes too many stem cells to become white blood cells (granulocytes or blasts).

statement: The Philadelphia chromosome is not passed from parent to child.
source_span: The Philadelphia chromosome is not passed from parent to child.

statement: Prognosis and treatment options for CML depend on the patient's age, the phase of CML, the amount of blasts in blood/bone marrow, the size of the spleen at diagnosis, and the patient's general health.
source_span: The patients age. - The phase of CML. - The amount of blasts in the blood or bone marrow. - The size of the spleen at diagnosis. - The patients general health.

statement: Chronic myelogenous leukemia has 3 phases: chronic phase, accelerated phase, and blastic phase.
source_span: Chronic myelogenous leukemia has 3 phases. - Chronic phase - Accelerated phase - Blastic phase

statement: Hairy cell leukemia is a type of cancer in which the bone marrow makes too many lymphocytes.
source_span: Hairy cell leukemia is a type of cancer in which the bone marrow makes too many lymphocytes (a type of white blood cell).

statement: Hairy cell leukemia is named for how the leukemia cells look "hairy" when viewed under a microscope.
source_span: The disease is called hairy cell leukemia because the leukemia cells look "hairy" when viewed under a microscope.

statement: Hairy cell leukemia is a rare type of leukemia that gets worse slowly or does not get worse at all.
source_span: This rare type of leukemia gets worse slowly or does not get worse at all.

statement: The cause of hairy cell leukemia is unknown, and it occurs more often in older men.
source_span: The cause of hairy cell leukemia is unknown. It occurs more often in older men.

statement: Signs and symptoms of hairy cell leukemia include infections, tiredness, and pain below the ribs, as well as weakness, fever, easy bruising or bleeding, shortness of breath, weight loss, and painless lumps.
source_span: Signs and symptoms of hairy cell leukemia include infections, tiredness, and pain below the ribs.

statement: A BRAF gene mutation is often found in patients with hairy cell leukemia.
source_span: A BRAF gene mutation is often found in patients with hairy cell leukemia.

statement: Some leukemia cells in hairy cell leukemia may collect in the spleen and cause it to swell.
source_span: Some of the leukemia cells may collect in the spleen and cause it to swell.

statement: Childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is a type of cancer in which the bone marrow makes too many immature lymphocytes.
source_span: Childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is a type of cancer in which the bone marrow makes too many immature lymphocytes (a type of white blood cell).

statement: ALL is the most common type of cancer in children.
source_span: ALL is the most common type of cancer in children.

statement: Childhood ALL usually gets worse quickly if it is not treated.
source_span: This type of cancer usually gets worse quickly if it is not treated.

statement: Past treatment for cancer and certain genetic conditions affect the risk of having childhood ALL.
source_span: Past treatment for cancer and certain genetic conditions affect the risk of having childhood ALL.

statement: Signs of childhood ALL include fever, easy bruising or bleeding, petechiae, bone or joint pain, painless lumps, pain below the ribs, weakness, and loss of appetite.
source_span: Signs of childhood ALL include fever and bruising.

statement: In Philadelphia chromosome positive ALL, part of one chromosome switches places with part of another chromosome.
source_span: in Philadelphia chromosome positive ALL, part of one chromosome switches places with part of another chromosome.

statement: A lumbar puncture, also called an LP or spinal tap, collects a sample of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) to check for signs that leukemia cells have spread to the brain and spinal cord.
source_span: This procedure is also called an LP or spinal tap.

statement: Intrathecal chemotherapy is given after the CSF sample is removed to treat any leukemia cells that may have spread to the brain and spinal cord.
source_span: Intrathecal chemotherapy is given after the sample of fluid is removed to treat any leukemia cells that may have spread to the brain and spinal cord.

statement: Childhood acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a type of cancer in which the bone marrow makes a large number of abnormal blood cells.
source_span: Childhood acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a type of cancer in which the bone marrow makes a large number of abnormal blood cells.

statement: AML is also called acute myelogenous leukemia, acute myeloblastic leukemia, acute granulocytic leukemia, and acute nonlymphocytic leukemia.
source_span: AML is also called acute myelogenous leukemia, acute myeloblastic leukemia, acute granulocytic leukemia, and acute nonlymphocytic leukemia.

statement: In AML, myeloid stem cells usually become abnormal immature white blood cells called myeloblasts (myeloid blasts).
source_span: In AML, the myeloid stem cells usually become a type of immature white blood cell called myeloblasts (or myeloid blasts).

statement: Leukemia cells in AML can spread outside the blood to the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord), skin, and gums.
source_span: The leukemia cells can spread outside the blood to other parts of the body, including the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord), skin, and gums.

statement: A solid tumor formed by AML leukemia cells is called a granulocytic sarcoma or chloroma.
source_span: Sometimes leukemia cells form a solid tumor called a granulocytic sarcoma or chloroma.

statement: Treatment of AML differs when it is the subtype acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) or when the child has Down syndrome.
source_span: The treatment of AML is different when it is a subtype called acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) or when the child has Down syndrome.

statement: Chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) is rare in children.
source_span: CML is rare in children.

statement: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia (JMML) is a rare childhood cancer that occurs more often in children around age 2 and is more common in boys.
source_span: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia (JMML) is a rare childhood cancer that occurs more often in children around the age of 2 years and is more common in boys.

statement: In JMML, too many bone marrow stem cells become myelocytes and monocytes, two types of white blood cells.
source_span: In JMML, too many bone marrow stem cells become 2 types of white blood cells called myelocytes and monocytes.

statement: Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) occur less often in children than in adults, and over time MDS may become AML.
source_span: Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) occur less often in children than in adults... Over time, MDS may become AML.

statement: Transient myeloproliferative disorder (TMD), a type of MDS that can develop in newborns with Down syndrome, usually goes away on its own within the first 3 weeks of life.
source_span: This disorder of the bone marrow can develop in newborns who have Down syndrome. It usually goes away on its own within the first 3 weeks of life.

statement: Infants who have Down syndrome and TMD have an increased chance of developing AML before the age of 3 years.
source_span: Infants who have Down syndrome and TMD have an increased chance of developing AML before the age of 3 years.

statement: Therapy-related AML (t-AML) and therapy-related MDS (t-MDS) usually occur within 7 years after treatment, but are rare in children.
source_span: These therapy-related diseases usually occur within 7 years after treatment, but are rare in children.

statement: The risk of therapy-related myeloid diseases depends on the total dose of anticancer drugs used and the radiation dose and treatment field.
source_span: The risk of these therapy-related myeloid diseases depends on the total dose of the anticancer drugs used and the radiation dose and treatment field.

statement: Adult soft tissue sarcoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the soft tissues of the body.
source_span: Adult soft tissue sarcoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the soft tissues of the body.

statement: Adult soft tissue sarcomas can form almost anywhere in the body but are most common in the head, neck, arms, legs, trunk, and abdomen.
source_span: Adult soft tissue sarcomas can form almost anywhere in the body, but are most common in the head, neck, arms, legs, trunk, and abdomen.

statement: Inherited disorders that increase the risk of adult soft tissue sarcoma include retinoblastoma, neurofibromatosis type 1, tuberous sclerosis, familial adenomatous polyposis, Li-Fraumeni syndrome, Werner syndrome, and nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome (Gorlin syndrome).
source_span: Risk factors for soft tissue sarcoma include the following inherited disorders: Retinoblastoma. Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1; von Recklinghausen disease). Tuberous sclerosis (Bourneville disease). Familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP; Gardner syndrome). Li-Fraumeni syndrome. Werner syndrome (adult progeria). Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome (Gorlin syndrome).

statement: Other risk factors for soft tissue sarcoma include past radiation therapy, exposure to chemicals such as Thorotrast, vinyl chloride, or arsenic, and long-term lymphedema in the arms or legs.
source_span: Other risk factors for soft tissue sarcoma include the following: Past treatment with radiation therapy for certain cancers. Being exposed to certain chemicals, such as Thorotrast (thorium dioxide), vinyl chloride, or arsenic. Having swelling (lymphedema) in the arms or legs for a long time.

statement: A sarcoma may appear as a painless lump under the skin, often on an arm or a leg.
source_span: A sarcoma may appear as a painless lump under the skin, often on an arm or a leg.

statement: There are three types of biopsy that may be used to diagnose adult soft tissue sarcoma: incisional biopsy, core biopsy, and excisional biopsy.
source_span: There are three types of biopsy that may be used: Incisional biopsy... Core biopsy... Excisional biopsy

statement: High-grade soft tissue sarcoma tumors usually grow and spread more quickly than low-grade tumors.
source_span: High-grade tumors usually grow and spread more quickly than low-grade tumors.

statement: Treatment options and prognosis for adult soft tissue sarcoma depend on factors including tumor type, size/grade/stage, location, whether all tumor is surgically removed, patient age and health, and recurrence.
source_span: The treatment options and prognosis (chance of recovery) depend on the following: The type of soft tissue sarcoma. The size, grade, and stage of the tumor. How fast the cancer cells are growing and dividing. Where the tumor is in the body. Whether all of the tumor is removed by surgery. The patient's age and general health. Whether the cancer has recurred (come back).

statement: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) is a disease in which abnormal cells form in the tissues of the gastrointestinal tract.
source_span: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor is a disease in which abnormal cells form in the tissues of the gastrointestinal tract.

statement: GISTs are most common in the stomach and small intestine but may be found anywhere in or near the GI tract.
source_span: They are most common in the stomach and small intestine but may be found anywhere in or near the GI tract.

statement: Some scientists believe GISTs begin in cells called interstitial cells of Cajal (ICC) in the wall of the GI tract.
source_span: Some scientists believe that GISTs begin in cells called interstitial cells of Cajal (ICC), in the wall of the GI tract.

statement: Genetic syndromes linked to GIST include neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and Carney triad.
source_span: The following genetic syndromes have been linked to GIST: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1). Carney triad.

statement: Signs of GIST include blood in the stool or vomit, abdominal pain, feeling very tired, trouble or pain when swallowing, and feeling full after eating only a little food.
source_span: Blood (either bright red or very dark) in the stool or vomit. Pain in the abdomen, which may be severe. Feeling very tired. Trouble or pain when swallowing. Feeling full after only a little food is eaten.

statement: Some GISTs are smaller than the eraser on top of a pencil and very small GISTs are common.
source_span: Sometimes GISTs are smaller than the eraser on top of a pencil.

statement: Cancer spreads through the body via tissue, the lymph system, and the blood.
source_span: Cancer can spread through tissue, the lymph system, and the blood

statement: A PET scan detects malignant tumor cells by injecting a small amount of radioactive glucose into a vein and imaging where the glucose is used.
source_span: A small amount of radioactive glucose (sugar) is injected into a vein. The PET scanner rotates around the body and makes a picture of where glucose is being used in the body.

statement: Kaposi sarcoma is a disease in which malignant tumors (cancer) can form in the skin, mucous membranes, lymph nodes, and other organs.
source_span: Kaposi sarcoma is a disease in which malignant tumors (cancer) can form in the skin, mucous membranes, lymph nodes, and other organs.

statement: Human herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8) is found in the lesions of all patients with Kaposi sarcoma.
source_span: Human herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8) is found in the lesions of all patients with Kaposi sarcoma.

statement: HHV-8 is also called Kaposi sarcoma herpesvirus (KSHV).
source_span: This virus is also called Kaposi sarcoma herpesvirus (KSHV).

statement: People infected with HHV-8 who are most likely to develop Kaposi sarcoma have immune systems weakened by disease or by drugs given after an organ transplant.
source_span: Those infected with HHV-8 who are most likely to develop Kaposi sarcoma have immune systems weakened by disease or by drugs given after an organ transplant.

statement: There are several types of Kaposi sarcoma: Classic, African, Immunosuppressive therapy-related, Epidemic, and Nonepidemic Kaposi sarcoma.
source_span: Classic Kaposi sarcoma. - African Kaposi sarcoma. - Immunosuppressive therapyrelated Kaposi sarcoma. - Epidemic Kaposi sarcoma. - Nonepidemic Kaposi sarcoma.

statement: A chest x-ray is used to find Kaposi sarcoma in the lungs.
source_span: This is used to find Kaposi sarcoma in the lungs.

statement: A lower than normal CD34 lymphocyte count can be a sign that the immune system is not working well.
source_span: A lower than normal amount of CD34 cells can be a sign the immune system is not working well.

statement: Prognosis and treatment options for Kaposi sarcoma depend on the type of Kaposi sarcoma, the general health of the patient (especially the immune system), and whether the cancer is newly diagnosed or recurrent.
source_span: The prognosis (chance of recovery) and treatment options depend on the following: - The type of Kaposi sarcoma. - The general health of the patient, especially the patient's immune system. - Whether the cancer has just been diagnosed or has recurred (come back).

statement: Classic Kaposi sarcoma is found most often in older men of Italian or Eastern European Jewish origin.
source_span: Classic Kaposi sarcoma is found most often in older men of Italian or Eastern European Jewish origin.

statement: Signs of classic Kaposi sarcoma may include slow-growing lesions on the legs and feet.
source_span: Signs of classic Kaposi sarcoma may include slow-growing lesions on the legs and feet.

statement: Risk factors for childhood rhabdomyosarcoma include the inherited diseases Li-Fraumeni syndrome, pleuropulmonary blastoma, neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), Costello syndrome, Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, and Noonan syndrome.
source_span: Risk factors for rhabdomyosarcoma include having the following inherited diseases: - Li-Fraumeni syndrome. - Pleuropulmonary blastoma. - Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1). - Costello syndrome. - Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. - Noonan syndrome.

statement: Children who had a high birth weight or were larger than expected at birth may have an increased risk of embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma.
source_span: Children who had a high birth weight or were larger than expected at birth may have an increased risk of embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma.

statement: In most cases, the cause of childhood rhabdomyosarcoma is not known.
source_span: In most cases, the cause of rhabdomyosarcoma is not known.

statement: A sign of childhood rhabdomyosarcoma is a lump or swelling that keeps getting bigger.
source_span: A sign of childhood rhabdomyosarcoma is a lump or swelling that keeps getting bigger.

statement: Symptoms of childhood rhabdomyosarcoma can include bulging of the eye, headache, trouble urinating or having bowel movements, blood in the urine, and bleeding in the nose, throat, vagina, or rectum.
source_span: Bulging of the eye. - Headache. - Trouble urinating or having bowel movements. - Blood in the urine. - Bleeding in the nose, throat, vagina, or rectum.

statement: In a sentinel lymph node biopsy, a radioactive substance and/or blue dye is injected near the tumor and the first lymph node to receive it is removed for examination.
source_span: A radioactive substance and/or blue dye is injected near the tumor. The substance or dye flows through the lymph ducts to the lymph nodes. The first lymph node to receive the substance or dye is removed.

statement: FISH (fluorescence in situ hybridization) is a laboratory test used to look at genes or chromosomes in cells and tissues to find certain gene changes.
source_span: FISH (fluorescence in situ hybridization): A laboratory test used to look at genes or chromosomes in cells and tissues... This type of test is used to find certain gene changes.

statement: Because treatment depends on the type of rhabdomyosarcoma, biopsy samples should be checked by a pathologist who has experience diagnosing rhabdomyosarcoma.
source_span: Because treatment depends on the type of rhabdomyosarcoma, biopsy samples should be checked by a pathologist who has experience in diagnosing rhabdomyosarcoma.

statement: Childhood soft tissue sarcoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in soft tissues of the body.
source_span: Childhood soft tissue sarcoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in soft tissues of the body.

statement: In children, soft tissue sarcoma tumors form most often in the arms, legs, or trunk (chest and abdomen).
source_span: In children, the tumors form most often in the arms, legs, or trunk (chest and abdomen).

statement: Myxoid liposarcoma is usually low grade and responds well to treatment, and its cells have a genetic translocation used to diagnose it.
source_span: Myxoid liposarcoma is usually low grade and responds well to treatment. The cells of myxoid liposarcoma have a certain genetic change called a translocation... In order to diagnose myxoid liposarcoma, the tumor cells are checked for this genetic change.

statement: Pleomorphic liposarcoma is usually high grade (likely to grow and spread quickly) and is less likely to respond well to treatment.
source_span: Pleomorphic liposarcoma is usually high grade (likely to grow and spread quickly) and is less likely to respond well to treatment.

statement: Extraskeletal mesenchymal chondrosarcoma often affects young adults and occurs in the head and neck.
source_span: Extraskeletal mesenchymal chondrosarcoma. This type of bone and cartilage tumor often affects young adults and occurs in the head and neck.

statement: Desmoid tumors sometimes occur in children with changes in the APC gene, which causes familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), an inherited condition in which many polyps form on the walls of the colon and rectum.
source_span: Desmoid tumors sometimes occur in children with changes in the adenomatous polyposis coli (APC) gene. Changes in this gene cause familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP). FAP is an inherited condition in which many polyps (growths on mucous membranes) form on the inside walls of the colon and rectum.

statement: Infantile fibrosarcoma is found in children aged 4 years and younger, most often in infants, and may be seen on a prenatal ultrasound exam.
source_span: Infantile fibrosarcoma... is found in children aged 4 years and younger. It most often occurs in infants and may be seen in a prenatal ultrasound exam.

statement: Low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma may come back many years after treatment and spread to the lungs and the lining of the chest cavity wall, so lifelong follow-up is needed.
source_span: The tumor may come back many years after treatment and spread to the lungs and the lining of the wall of the chest cavity. Lifelong follow-up is needed.

statement: CLSTM (Contextual LSTM) is an extension of the LSTM model that incorporates contextual features such as topics.
source_span: we present CLSTM (Contextual LSTM), an extension of the recurrent neural network LSTM (Long-Short Term Memory) model, where we incorporate contextual features (e.g., topics) into the model

statement: CLSTM is evaluated on three NLP tasks: word prediction, next sentence selection, and sentence topic prediction.
source_span: We evaluate CLSTM on three specific NLP tasks: word prediction, next sentence selection, and sentence topic prediction.

statement: On the next sentence selection task, CLSTM achieves relative accuracy improvements of 21% on the Wikipedia dataset and 18% on the Google News dataset over baseline LSTM.

statement: The CLSTM and baseline LSTM models were trained on two corpora: English documents in Wikipedia and a subset of articles from a recent snapshot of English Google News.

communicates with a ``django-uwsgi`` "worker" process to serve dynamic content.

statement: When DEBUG is False, Django emails the addresses in the ADMINS setting whenever unhandled code raises an exception resulting in an HTTP response with status code 500 or greater.
source_span:
When :setting:`DEBUG` is ``False``, Django will email the users listed in the
:setting:`ADMINS` setting whenever your code raises an unhandled exception and
results in an internal server error (strictly speaking, for any response with
an HTTP status code of 500 or greater).

statement: By default Django sends error emails from root@localhost; the sender address can be changed via the SERVER_EMAIL setting.
source_span:
By default, Django will send email from ``root@localhost``. However, some mail
providers reject all email from this address. To use a different sender
address, modify the :setting:`SERVER_EMAIL` setting.

statement: Django emails 404 errors to the MANAGERS setting when DEBUG is False, MIDDLEWARE includes BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware, and the request has a referer.
source_span:
If those conditions are met, Django will email the users listed in the
:setting:`MANAGERS` setting whenever your code raises a 404 and the request has
a referer.

statement: Django does not email about 404s that lack a referer, and ignores 404s where the referer equals the requested URL.
source_span:
It doesn't bother to email for 404s that don't have a referer --
those are usually people typing in broken URLs or broken web bots. It also
ignores 404s when the referer is equal to the requested URL

statement: The IGNORABLE_404_URLS setting takes a list of compiled regular expression objects to stop Django from reporting matching 404s.
source_span:
You can tell Django to stop reporting particular 404s by tweaking the
:setting:`IGNORABLE_404_URLS` setting. It should be a list of compiled
regular expression objects.

statement: BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware must be placed before other middleware that intercepts 404 errors, such as LocaleMiddleware or FlatpageFallbackMiddleware.
source_span:
``BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware`` must appear
before other middleware that intercepts 404 errors, such as
:class:`~django.middleware.locale.LocaleMiddleware`

statement: The dynamic memory network (DMN) obtained high accuracy on a variety of language tasks.
source_span: One such architecture, the dynamic memory network (DMN), obtained high accuracy on a variety of language tasks.

statement: The new DMN+ model improves the state of the art on both the Visual Question Answering dataset and the bAbI-10k text question-answering dataset without supporting fact supervision.
source_span: Our new DMN+ model improves the state of the art on both the Visual Question Answering dataset and the \babi-10k text question-answering dataset without supporting fact supervision.

statement: The DMN yields state of the art results on question answering with supporting facts marked during training, sentiment analysis, and part-of-speech tagging.
source_span: The DMN yields state of the art results on question answering with supporting facts marked during training, sentiment analysis, and part-of-speech tagging.

statement: Unlike the original DMN, the new DMN+ model does not require that supporting facts be labeled during training.
source_span: Unlike before, the new DMN+ model does not require that supporting facts (i.e. the facts that are relevant for answering a particular question) are labeled during training.

statement: The DMN architecture is composed of four modules: Input Module, Question Module, Episodic Memory Module, and Answer Module.
source_span: The modules, depicted in Fig. 1 , are as follows: Input Module... Question Module... Episodic Memory Module... Answer Module

statement: The Input Module processes input data into a set of vectors termed facts, F=[f_1,...,f_N], where N is the total number of facts.
source_span: This module processes the input data about which a question is being asked into a set of vectors termed facts, represented as $F=[f_1,\hdots ,f_N]$ , where $N$ is the total number of facts.

statement: In the original DMN, the text QA input module consists of a GRU over the input words.
source_span: For text QA in BIBREF6 , the module consists of a GRU over the input words.

statement: The Question Module computes the question vector q as the final hidden state of a GRU run over the words in the question.
source_span: This module computes a vector representation $q$ of the question, where $q \in \mathbb {R}^{n_H}$ is the final hidden state of a GRU over the words in the question.

statement: The initial episodic memory vector is set equal to the question vector: m^0 = q.
source_span: the initial memory vector is set to the question vector: $m^0 = q$

statement: The DMN is trained using cross entropy error on the answers, which is backpropagated through the entire network.
source_span: The cross entropy error on the answers is used for training and backpropagated through the entire network.

statement: The new GRU formulation for the memory module incorporates attention gates computed using global knowledge over the facts.
source_span: The new GRU formulation incorporates attention gates that are computed using global knowledge over the facts.

statement: The proposed new input module uses a two-level encoder with a sentence reader and an input fusion layer to allow information flow between sentences.
source_span: We propose a new input module which uses a two level encoder with a sentence reader and input fusion layer to allow for information flow between sentences.

statement: The paper proposes a joint Bayesian model of unsupervised semantic role induction in multiple languages to explore the usefulness of parallel corpora for this task.
source_span: We propose a Bayesian model of unsupervised semantic role induction in multiple languages, and use it to explore the usefulness of parallel corpora for this task.

statement: The joint Bayesian model consists of individual models for each language plus additional latent variables that capture alignments between roles across languages.
source_span: Our joint Bayesian model consists of individual models for each language plus additional latent variables that capture alignments between roles across languages.

statement: The biggest impact of adding a parallel corpus to training is the increase in monolingual data, with crosslingual alignments giving only small improvements even with labeled data for the other language.
source_span: We find that the biggest impact of adding a parallel corpus to training is actually the increase in mono-lingual data, with the alignments to another language resulting in small improvements, even with labeled data for the other language.

statement: In the example sentence, the predicate WRITE has two arguments: 'Mike' labeled A0 (the writer) and 'a book' labeled A1 (the thing written).
source_span: Here, the predicate WRITE has two arguments: `Mike' as A0 or the writer, and `a book' as A1 or the thing written.

statement: The labels A0 and A1 correspond to the PropBank annotations.
source_span: The labels A0 and A1 correspond to the PropBank annotations BIBREF0 .

statement: The example English-German word alignments given are Mike-Mike, written-geschrieben, and book-Buch.
source_span: If sentences INLINEFORM0 and INLINEFORM1 have the word alignments: Mike-Mike, written-geschrieben, and book-Buch

statement: The paper uses the Bayesian model of garg2012unsupervised as its base monolingual model.
source_span: We use the Bayesian model of garg2012unsupervised as our base monolingual model.

statement: The role inventory for each predicate is divided into Primary and Secondary roles to model role ordering and repetition preferences.
source_span: the role inventory for each predicate is divided into Primary and Secondary roles as follows

statement: garg2012unsupervised reported that in practice, Primary Roles mostly get mapped to core roles and Secondary Roles to modifier roles.
source_span: garg2012unsupervised reported that, in practice, PRs mostly get mapped to core roles and SRs to modifier roles, which conforms to the linguistic motivations for this distinction.

statement: In the multilingual model, whenever the head words of arguments are aligned in parallel sentences during training, a crosslingual latent variable (CLV) is added as a parent of the two corresponding role variables.
source_span: whenever the head words of the arguments are aligned, we add a CLV as a parent of the two corresponding role variables.

statement: All the multinomial and binomial distributions in the monolingual model have symmetric Dirichlet and beta priors respectively.
source_span: All the multinomial and binomial distributions have symmetric Dirichlet and beta priors respectively.

statement: The paper proposes leveraging domain-specific features (specific vocabulary usage, specific codes, and document type) to improve automatic quality evaluation of Wikipedia medical articles.
source_span: In this paper, we propose to leverage specific domain features to improve the results of the evaluation of Wikipedia medical articles.

statement: The evaluation adopts an 'actionable' model whose features relate to article content, so the model can directly suggest strategies for improving a given article's quality.
source_span: we evaluate the articles adopting an "actionable" model, whose features are related to the content of the articles, so that the model can also directly suggest strategies for improving a given article quality.

statement: The approach was validated by classifying medical articles from the Wikipedia Medicine Portal that had been previously manually labeled by the Wiki Project team.
source_span: We prove the effectiveness of our approach by classifying the medical articles of the Wikipedia Medicine Portal, which have been previously manually labeled by the Wiki Project team.

statement: According to the 2014 Eurobarometer survey on European citizens' digital health literacy, around six out of ten respondents have used the Internet to search for health-related information.
source_span: As pointed out by the 2014 Eurobarometer survey on European citizens' digital health literacy, around six out of ten respondents have used the Internet to search for health-related information.

statement: The literature has traditionally adopted the 'Flesch-Kincaid' measure to automatically assess readability in textual documents.
source_span: the literature has widely adopted well known criteria, as the “Flesch-Kincaid" measure" BIBREF2 , to automatically assess readability in textual documents.

statement: The paper's baseline 'actionable model' comes from prior work (BIBREF7) that uses classification techniques based on structural and linguistic features of an article.
source_span: the work in BIBREF7 exploits classification techniques based on structural and linguistic features of an article.

statement: Because Wikipedia can be edited by anyone regardless of expertise, this tends to erode the average reputation of its sources and the trustworthiness of the content.
source_span: since Wikipedia can be edited by anyone, regardless of their level of expertise, this tends to erode the average reputation of the sources, and, consequently, the trustworthiness of the contents posted by those sources.

statement: There has been a reported case of a blackmail network of accounts that threatened celebrities by menacing to insert offending information on their Wikipedia pages.
source_span: the recent news on the uncovering of a blackmail network of accounts, which threatened celebrities with the menace of inserting offending information on their Wikipedia pages.

statement: MVCNN combines diverse versions of pretrained word embeddings and extracts features of multigranular phrases with variable-size convolution filters.
source_span: It (i) combines diverse versions of pretrained word embeddings and (ii) extracts features of multigranular phrases with variable-size convolution filters.

statement: MVCNN achieves state-of-the-art performance on four tasks: small-scale binary sentiment, small-scale multi-class sentiment, large-scale Twitter sentiment prediction, and subjectivity classification.
source_span: MVCNN achieves state-of-the-art performance on four tasks: on small-scale binary, small-scale multi-class and largescale Twitter sentiment prediction and on subjectivity classification.

statement: Pretraining MVCNN is critical for good performance.
source_span: We also show that pretraining MVCNN is critical for good performance.

statement: The letters M and V in MVCNN denote multichannel and variable-size convolution filters, respectively.
source_span: The letters “M” and “V” in the name “MVCNN” of our architecture denote the multichannel and variable-size convolution filters, respectively.

statement: MVCNN employs two tricks to enhance performance: mutual learning and pretraining.
source_span: We also employ two “tricks” to further enhance system performance: mutual learning and pretraining.

statement: kimEMNLP2014's multichannel approach relies on a single version of pretrained Word2Vec embeddings kept as two copies, one stable and one fine-tuned by backpropagation.

statement: blunsom2014convolutional stacked multiple layers of one-dimensional convolution using dynamic k-max pooling to model sentences.
source_span: blunsom2014convolutional stacked multiple layers of one-dimensional convolution by dynamic k-max pooling to model sentences.

statement: MVCNN has a large number of parameters, creating a danger of overfitting when trained on small training sets, which is addressed via pretraining on unlabeled data.
source_span: MVCNN has a large number of parameters, so that overfitting is a danger when they are trained on small training sets. We address this problem by pretraining MVCNN on unlabeled data.

statement: The unsupervised system achieves a 58.44% F1 score under the CoNLL metric on the English data from the CoNLL-2012 shared task.
source_span: Our unsupervised system achieves 58.44% F1 score of the CoNLL metric on the English data from the CoNLL-2012 shared task (Pradhan et al., 2012)

statement: The unsupervised system outperforms the Stanford deterministic system (Lee et al., 2013) by 3.01% absolute.
source_span: outperforming the Stanford deterministic system (Lee et al., 2013) by 3.01%.

statement: Supervised entity coreference resolution systems can be categorized into three classes: mention-pair models, entity-mention models, and ranking models.

statement: haghighi-klein:2007 presented a mention-pair nonparametric fully-generative Bayesian model for unsupervised coreference resolution.
source_span: haghighi-klein:2007:ACLMain presented a mention-pair nonparametric fully-generative Bayesian model for unsupervised coreference resolution.

source_span: poon-domingos:2008:EMNLP proposed an entity-mention model that is able to perform joint inference across mentions by using Markov Logic.

statement: The model defines three resolution modes: string-matching (str), precise-construct (prec), and attribute-matching (attr).
source_span: we define three resolution modes — string-matching (str), precise-construct (prec), and attribute-matching (attr)

statement: The Stanford system uses string-matching sieves to link mentions with similar text, and a precise-construct sieve to link mentions with special syntactic or semantic relations such as apposition or acronym.

source_span: Our experiments on the SemEval-2016 cQA task show 10% improvement on a MAP score compared to an information retrieval-based approach

source_span: Automation of cQA forums can be divided into three tasks: question-comment relevance (Task A), question-question relevance (Task B), and question-external comment relevance (Task C).

statement: The approach achieves comparable performance to a strong handcrafted feature-based method.
source_span: achieve comparable performance to a strong handcrafted feature-based method.

source_span: Our approach does not rely on any linguistic processing, and can be applied to different languages or domains.

source_span: An LSTM unit contains a memory cell with self-connections, as well as three multiplicative gates to control information flow.

statement: BIBREF10 proposed several convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures for cQA.

statement: Hints passed to a RunPython operation are passed as **hints to the allow_migrate method of database routers.
source_span: You can also provide hints that will be passed to the :meth:`allow_migrate` method of database routers as ``**hints``

statement: If a RunPython or RunSQL operation only affects one model, it's good practice to pass model_name as a hint, especially for reusable and third-party apps.

statement: Applying a plain migration that adds a unique non-nullable field to a table with existing rows raises an error because the default value is generated only once, breaking the unique constraint.
source_span: Applying a "plain" migration that adds a unique non-nullable field to a table with existing rows will raise an error because the value used to populate existing rows is generated only once, thus breaking the unique constraint.

statement: The recommended process adds the field with default=uuid.uuid4 and unique=True, runs makemigrations, then generates two empty migration files by running makemigrations myapp --empty twice.
source_span: Add the field on your model with ``default=uuid.uuid4`` and ``unique=True``... Generate two empty migration files for the same app by running ``makemigrations myapp --empty`` twice.

statement: In the first (auto-generated) migration file, unique=True is changed to null=True to create an intermediary null field and defer the unique constraint until values are populated.
source_span: Change ``unique=True`` to ``null=True`` -- this will create the intermediary null field and defer creating the unique constraint until we've populated unique values on all the rows.

statement: The second empty migration file (e.g. 0005_populate_uuid_values.py) uses a RunPython operation to generate a unique UUID value for each existing row.
source_span: In the first empty migration file, add a ... ``RunPython`` ... operation to generate a unique value (UUID in the example) for each existing row.

statement: The last migration file (e.g. 0006_remove_uuid_null.py) changes the AddField operation to AlterField with default=uuid.uuid4 and unique=True.
source_span: Copy the ``AddField`` operation from the auto-generated migration (the first of the three new files) to the last migration, change ``AddField`` to ``AlterField``

statement: There is a race condition where objects created after the AddField operation and before the RunPython operation will have their original UUIDs overwritten.
source_span: Objects created after the ``AddField`` and before ``RunPython`` will have their original ``uuid``’s overwritten.

statement: On databases that support DDL transactions (SQLite and PostgreSQL), migrations run inside a transaction by default.
source_span: On databases that support DDL transactions (SQLite and PostgreSQL), migrations will run inside a transaction by default.

statement: Setting the atomic attribute to False on a Migration class prevents that migration from running inside a transaction (a non-atomic migration).
source_span: you may want to prevent a migration from running in a transaction by setting the ``atomic`` attribute to ``False``

statement: Within a non-atomic migration, parts can still be executed inside a transaction using transaction.atomic() or by passing atomic=True to RunPython.
source_span: It's possible to execute parts of the migration inside a transaction using :func:`~django.db.transaction.atomic` or by passing ``atomic=True`` to ``RunPython``.

statement: The Steering Council moves supported ideas through the stages: Idea, Approved - Idea refinement - Team creation, In progress, Working solution - Review - Feedback, Needs maintainer (Django only), Done.

statement: Informal Django Forum votes on feature ideas follow the Apache/Python style: +1, +0, -0, or -1.
source_span: votes are given as +1, +0, -0, or -1.

statement: A +1 vote means "I love the idea and I'm strongly committed to it."
source_span: +1: "I love the idea and I'm strongly committed to it."

statement: A -1 vote means "I strongly disagree and would be very unhappy to see the idea turn into reality."
source_span: -1: "I strongly disagree and would be very unhappy to see the idea turn into reality."

statement: Since Django is hosted on GitHub, patches are provided in the form of pull requests.
source_span: Since Django is hosted on GitHub, patches are provided in the form of pull requests.

statement: A git alias `pr = !sh -c "git fetch upstream pull/${1}/head:pr/${1} && git checkout pr/${1}"` added to ~/.gitconfig lets you run `git pr ####` to check out a pull request.
source_span: pr = !sh -c \"git fetch upstream pull/${1}/head:pr/${1} && git checkout pr/${1}\"

statement: Mergers use `git rebase -i` and `git commit --amend` to bring commits up to the expected quality level.
source_span: Use ``git rebase -i`` and ``git commit --amend`` to make sure the commits have the expected level of quality.

statement: Work is merged to main as a "fast-forward" (via git merge --ff-only) to avoid a merge commit.
source_span: Merge the work as "fast-forward" to main to avoid a merge commit.

statement: Force pushing to the pull request branch after rebasing on main but before merging makes the commit hashes on main and the branch match, which automatically closes the pull request.
source_span: Force push to the branch after rebasing on main but before merging and pushing to upstream. This allows the commit hashes on main and the branch to match which automatically closes the pull request.

statement: If a pull request doesn't need to be merged as multiple commits, GitHub's "Squash and merge" button can be used instead.
source_span: If a pull request doesn't need to be merged as multiple commits, you can use GitHub's "Squash and merge" button on the website.

statement: The published history of django/django branches must never be changed by force pushing, except in cases like security reasons, and only after discussing the situation with the team.
source_span: Never change the published history of ``django/django`` branches by force pushing. If you absolutely must (for security reasons for example), first discuss the situation with the team.

statement: Commit messages must be written in the past tense, with the subject line ending in a period, e.g. "Fixed Unicode bug in RSS API."
source_span:
Write detailed commit messages in the past tense, not present tense, and end the subject line with a period.

  * Correct: "Fixed Unicode bug in RSS API."

statement: Commit messages should use lines of 72 characters maximum.
source_span: The commit message should be in lines of 72 chars maximum.

statement: Contributors should be credited in commit messages, e.g. "Thanks A for the report and B for review," using git's Co-Authored-By as appropriate.
source_span: Credit the contributors in the commit message: "Thanks A for the report and B for review." Use git's `Co-Authored-By`_ as appropriate

statement: Commits should be limited to the most granular change that makes sense, favoring frequent small commits over infrequent large ones.
source_span: Limit commits to the most granular change that makes sense. This means, use frequent small commits rather than infrequent large commits.

statement: Bug fixes should be separated from feature changes, since bugfixes may need to be backported.
source_span: Separate bug fixes from feature changes. Bugfixes may need to be :ref:`backported

statement: Tweet2vec is a character composition model that finds vector-space representations of whole tweets by learning complex, non-local dependencies in character sequences.
source_span: We propose a character composition model, tweet2vec, which finds vector-space representations of whole tweets by learning complex, non-local dependencies in character sequences.

statement: The tweet2vec encoder is publicly available.
source_span: Our tweet2vec encoder is publicly available.

statement: The training dataset consisted of 2 million tweets with about 0.92 million unique word types.
source_span: In our moderately sized training dataset of 2 million tweets, there were about 0.92 million unique word types.

statement: The proposed model is a Bi-directional Gated Recurrent Unit (Bi-GRU) neural network for learning tweet representations.
source_span: We propose a Bi-directional Gated Recurrent Unit (Bi-GRU) BIBREF5 neural network for learning tweet representations.

statement: The training objective is to maximize cross-entropy loss for predicting hashtags for a post from its latent representation.
source_span: we formulate our training objective to maximize cross-entropy loss at the task of predicting hashtags for a post from its latent representation.

statement: The model treats white-space as a special character during its forward and backward pass over the sequence.
source_span: Treating white-space as a special character itself, the model does a forward and backward pass over the entire sequence

statement: BIBREF2 present a bidirectional LSTM for composing word vectors from their constituent characters.
source_span: BIBREF2 challenge this assumption and present a bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) BIBREF3 for composing word vectors from their constituent characters

statement: The paper introduces the Argus Yes/No Question Answering task, exemplified by the question 'Did Donald Trump announce he is running for president?'
source_span: As a specific instance, we introduce the Argus Yes/No Question Answering task. The problem is, given a real-world event binary question like Did Donald Trump announce he is running for president?

statement: The research is motivated by the Argus automatic reporting system for the Augur prediction market platform.
source_span: Our research is motivated by the Argus automatic reporting system for the Augur prediction market platform.

statement: The time domain of dataset questions was restricted from September 1, 2014 to September 1, 2015.
source_span: the time domain of questions was restricted from September 1, 2014 to September 1, 2015

statement: The topic domain of the dataset was focused on politics, sports, and the stock market.
source_span: topic domain was focused to politics, sports and the stock market

statement: Amazon Mechanical Turk users seeded the dataset with an initial, somewhat redundant 250 questions.
source_span: This seeded the dataset with initial, somewhat redundant 250 questions.

statement: The dataset was extended with questions autogenerated from 26 templates pertaining to top sporting event winners and US senate or gubernatorial elections.
source_span: We extended the data with questions autogenerated from 26 templates, pertaining top sporting event winners and US senate or gubernatorial elections.

statement: The model was also evaluated on the MCTest dataset and the AI2-8grade/CK12 dataset for ranking multiple-choice question answers.
source_span: We consider the MCTest dataset and the AI2-8grade/CK12 dataset that we introduce below.

statement: The Syphon preprocessing component of the Argus implementation was used to identify semantic roles of question tokens and produce search keywords for building the evidence dataset.
source_span: we used the Syphon preprocessing component BIBREF5 of the Argus implementation to identify semantic roles of all question tokens and produce the search keywords

statement: The researchers ran a user study with 25 participants to demonstrate the tool's speed and accuracy advantages over conventional methods.
source_span: We ran a user study with 25 participants, demonstrating that compared to more conventional methods, our tool can increase the speed and the accuracy with which users can track stories about real-world events.

statement: The researchers manually annotated 7,000 tweets about several different real-world events for assertion detection.
source_span: We manually annotated $7,000$ tweets about several different real-world events.

statement: Of the 7,000 annotated tweets, 3,290 (47%) contained assertions.
source_span: Of the $7,000$ tweets, $3,290$ ( $47\%$ ) of those tweets containing assertions and the rest containing one of the other speech-acts.

statement: The supervised Twitter speech-act classifier used to train the assertion detector was developed by Vosoughi et al.
source_span: trained a state-of-the-art supervised Twitter speech-act classifier, developed by Vosoughi et al. BIBREF3

statement: The assertion classifier was evaluated using 20-fold cross validation and achieved an F-score of 0.86.
source_span: We evaluated the classifier using 20-fold cross validation, with the F-score for classifying assertions being $.86$ .
