statement: Translations from Transifex are only integrated into the Django repository at the time of a new feature release.
source_span: Translations from Transifex are only integrated into the Django repository at the time of a new :term:`feature release <Feature release>`.

statement: Django tries to update translations a second time during one of the following patch releases, depending on the translation manager's availability.
source_span: We try to update them a second time during one of the following :term:`patch release <Patch release>`\s, but that depends on the translation manager's availability.

statement: To change locale format files, a pull request must be created against the Django Git main branch and a ticket opened with Component set to Translations and the "has patch" flag set.
source_span: Open a ticket in Django's ticket system, set its ``Component`` field to ``Translations``, set the "has patch" flag, and include the link to the pull request.

statement: A locale's date, time, and number formatting particularities are described in conf/locale/<locale>/formats.py.
source_span: You can also review ``conf/locale/<locale>/formats.py``. This file describes the date, time and numbers formatting particularities of your locale.

statement: Format files are not managed through the use of Transifex.
source_span: The format files aren't managed by the use of Transifex.

statement: Translated documentation appears at https://docs.djangoproject.com/<language_code>/ once at least the docs/intro/* files are fully translated in that language.
source_span: The translations will appear at ``https://docs.djangoproject.com/<language_code>/`` when at least the ``docs/intro/*`` files are fully translated in your language.

statement: Only translations for the latest stable Django release are updated on the documentation website.
source_span: Only translations for the latest stable Django release are updated.

statement: If a contribution is more than one or two lines of code, the contributor has the option to sign the Contributor License Agreement (CLA).
source_span: If your contribution is more than one or two lines of code, you have the option to sign the `CLA`_.

statement: Django has an eight-month release cycle, which gives plenty of time for a patch to be reviewed.
source_span: Remember that Django has an eight-month release cycle, so there's plenty of time for your patch to be reviewed.

statement: When reviewing patches, contributors should try them out on a database other than SQLite where possible and relevant.
source_span: Where possible and relevant, try them out on a database other than SQLite.

statement: If uncertain whether a ticket should be marked "Ready For Check-in," a contributor can ask on the #contributing-getting-started channel on the Django Discord server.
source_span: you might also try asking on the ``#contributing-getting-started`` channel in the `Django Discord server`_ to see if someone else can confirm your suspicions.

statement: The "Needs tests", "Needs documentation", and "Patch needs improvement" Trac flags should be unchecked once all review comments on a patch have been addressed.
source_span: Review the ticket on Trac to ensure that the *Needs tests*, *Needs documentation*, and *Patch needs improvement* flags are unchecked once you've addressed all review comments.

statement: New contributors are advised to focus on one or two tickets at a time and see them through, rather than taking on many tickets at once.
source_span: Focus on one or two tickets, see them through from start to finish, and repeat. The shotgun approach of taking on lots of tickets and letting some fall by the wayside ends up doing more harm than good.

statement: Setting up a Django development virtual environment requires a Python version of 3.12 or higher.
source_span:
$ # This needs to be >= 3.12
$ python -V

statement: Contributors clone their fork with git clone https://github.com/YourGitHubName/django.git and add the upstream remote https://github.com/django/django.git.
source_span:
$ git clone https://github.com/YourGitHubName/django.git
$ cd django
$ git remote add upstream https://github.com/django/django.git

statement: Pre-commit hooks are installed by running python -m pip install pre-commit followed by pre-commit install, so formatting and linting run automatically before each commit.
source_span:
$ python -m pip install pre-commit
$ pre-commit install

statement: The Django test suite is only guaranteed to pass on the latest point release of each supported Python version.
source_span: the test suite is only guaranteed to pass on the latest point release of each supported Python version.

statement: The "vulture method" is the process of looking for accepted Django tickets that haven't been touched in six months or longer.
source_span: The vulture method is the process of looking for accepted tickets that haven't been touched in six months or longer.

statement: Vulture-able tickets are filtered by Triage stage = Accepted, Patch needs improvement = Yes, Created between 5 years ago and today, and Modified between 5 years ago and 6 months ago.
source_span:
* Triage stage = Accepted
* Patch needs improvement = Yes
* Created = between ``5 years ago`` and ``today``
* Modified = between ``5 years ago`` and ``6 months ago``

statement: To claim a Django ticket, click the "Modify Ticket" button, select the "assign to" radio button in the "Action" section, and click "Submit changes."
source_span: make yourself the owner by clicking the "Modify Ticket" button near the bottom of the page, selecting the "assign to" radio button in the "Action" section, and clicking "Submit changes".

statement: To start a fresh branch for a ticket, run git fetch upstream then git checkout -b ticket_TicketNumber upstream/main.
source_span:
$ git fetch upstream
$ git checkout -b ticket_TicketNumber upstream/main

statement: Django uses Trac for managing the work on the code base.
source_span: Django uses Trac_ for managing the work on the code base.

statement: There are four roles in Django's ticket triage workflow diagram.
source_span: We have four roles in this diagram.

statement: The merger role is granted by a vote of the Steering Council.
source_span: The merger role is granted by a vote of the Steering Council.

statement: Mergers are people with commit access who make the final decision to merge a change.
source_span: Mergers: people with commit access who make the final decision to merge a change.

statement: Triagers are anyone who can check whether a ticket describes a real issue and keep the tracker organized.
source_span: Triagers: anyone can take on this role by checking whether a ticket describes a real issue and keeping the tracker organized.

statement: Unreviewed tickets appear in the "triage" queue.
source_span: Unreviewed tickets appear in the "triage" queue.

statement: Accepted tickets are broken into three queues: Needs Patch, Needs PR Review, and Waiting On Author.
source_span: It is broken out into three queues

statement: "Needs Patch" means the ticket is Accepted with No Flags.
source_span: **Needs Patch** (Accepted + No Flags)

statement: "Needs PR Review" means the ticket is Accepted and Has Patch.
source_span: **Needs PR Review** (Accepted + Has Patch)

statement: "Waiting On Author" means the ticket is Accepted, Has Patch, and Needs fixes.
source_span: **Waiting On Author** (Accepted + Has Patch + Needs fixes)

statement: In the example lifecycle, Alice creates a ticket and opens an incomplete pull request missing tests and with an incorrect implementation.
source_span: Alice creates a ticket and opens an incomplete pull request (missing tests, incorrect implementation).

statement: Bob reviews the pull request, marks the ticket as "Accepted", and sets the flags "needs tests" and "patch needs improvement".
source_span: Bob reviews the pull request, marks the ticket as "Accepted", sets the flags "needs tests" and "patch needs improvement"

statement: Daisy reviews the pull request and marks the ticket as "Ready for checkin".
source_span: Daisy reviews the pull request and marks the ticket as "Ready for checkin".

statement: Jacob, a merger, reviews and merges the pull request.
source_span: Jacob, a :ref:`merger <mergers-team>`, reviews and merges the pull request.

statement: All files should be formatted using the black auto-formatter.
source_span: All files should be formatted using the :pypi:`black` auto-formatter.

statement: Python files use 4 spaces for indentation and HTML files use 2 spaces.
source_span: The Python files use 4 spaces for indentation and the HTML files use 2 spaces.

statement: Django allows up to 88 characters per line in code, matching black's line length.
source_span: We allow up to 88 characters in code, as this is the line length used by ``black``.

statement: Documentation, comments, and docstrings should be wrapped at 79 characters.
source_span: Documentation, comments, and docstrings should be wrapped at 79 characters.

statement: Variable, function, and method names should use underscores, not camelCase.
source_span: Use underscores, not camelCase, for variable, function and method names

statement: Class names should use InitialCaps.
source_span: Use ``InitialCaps`` for class names

statement: f-strings should not be used for any string that may require translation, including error and logging messages.
source_span: f-strings should not be used for any string that may require translation, including error and logging messages.

statement: isort version 8.0.1 or higher is the recommended installation for import sorting.
source_span: $ python -m pip install "isort >= 8.0.1"

statement: Imports should be grouped in this order: future, standard library, third-party libraries, other Django components, local Django component, try/excepts.
source_span: Put imports in these groups: future, standard library, third-party libraries, other Django components, local Django component, try/excepts.

statement: In tests, use assertIs(…, True/False) for testing boolean values rather than assertTrue and assertFalse.
source_span: Use :meth:`assertIs(…, True/False)<unittest.TestCase.assertIs>` for testing boolean values, rather than :meth:`~unittest.TestCase.assertTrue` and :meth:`~unittest.TestCase.assertFalse`

statement: Test docstrings should not include preambles such as "Tests that" or "Ensures that".
source_span: Don't include preambles such as "Tests that" or "Ensures that".

statement: The admin and gis contrib apps contain JavaScript code within Django core.
source_span: the ``admin`` and ``gis`` contrib apps contain JavaScript code.

statement: Most JavaScript files use 4 spaces for indentation, with some exceptions.
source_span: Most of the JavaScript files use 4 spaces for indentation, but there are some exceptions.

statement: JavaScript variable names should use camelCase instead of underscore_case.
source_span: use ``camelCase`` instead of ``underscore_case``.

statement: Biome is the code linter used to check JavaScript code and is run by the pre-commit hooks.
source_span: Use the `Biome`_ code linter to check your code for bugs and style errors. Biome will be run by the pre-commit hooks.

statement: Django's JavaScript tests use QUnit.
source_span: Django's JavaScript tests use `QUnit`_.

statement: JavaScript tests are located in a top-level js_tests directory.
source_span: The tests are located in a top level :source:`js_tests` directory.

statement: Node.js must be installed to run JavaScript tests from the command line.
source_span: To run the tests from the command line, you need to have `Node.js`_ installed.

statement: Running `npm install` followed by `npm test` runs the JavaScript tests from the command line.
source_span: $ npm install ... $ npm test

statement: To measure code coverage, execute `python -m http.server` from the root directory and open http://localhost:8000/js_tests/tests.html in a browser.
source_span: Execute ``python -m http.server`` from the root directory (not from inside ``js_tests``). * Open http://localhost:8000/js_tests/tests.html in your web browser.

statement: RAFAEL is an open-domain factoid question answering system for Polish.
source_span: an open-domain factoid question answering system for Polish, RAFAEL, is presented

statement: RAFAEL stands for RApid Factoid Answer Extraction aLgorithm.
source_span: RAFAEL (RApid Factoid Answer Extraction aLgorithm)

statement: Deep Entity Recognition (DeepER) is a novel technique introduced and implemented in the paper.
source_span: a novel technique, called Deep Entity Recognition (DeepER), is introduced and implemented

statement: DeepER allows a comprehensive search of all forms of entity references matching a given WordNet synset, based on a previously assembled entity library.
source_span: It allows a comprehensive search of all forms of entity references matching a given WordNet synset (e.g. an impressionist), based on a previously assembled entity library.

statement: The entity library was created by analyzing the first sentences of encyclopaedia entries and disambiguation and redirect pages.
source_span: It has been created by analysing the first sentences of encyclopaedia entries and disambiguation and redirect pages.

statement: DeepER experiments include over a thousand questions from a Polish quiz TV show answered on the grounds of Polish Wikipedia.
source_span: including over a thousand questions from a quiz TV show answered on the grounds of Polish Wikipedia

statement: In the monarch example, Simeon II is the answer because he is a tsar, and WordNet relations imply that a tsar is a monarch.
source_span: we could utilise information that Simeon II (our answer) is a tsar; thanks to WordNet relations we know that it implies being a monarch

statement: The Arctic Tern (Sterna paradisaea) is described in Wikipedia as a seabird of the tern family Sternidae, allowing DeepER to classify it as a bird despite not being a classical NER entity.
source_span: The Arctic Tern (Sterna paradisaea) is a seabird of the tern family Sternidae.

statement: With DeepER, a candidate answer can undergo the same recognition process and be compared to the actual expected entity rather than plain string equality.
source_span: with DeepER, a candidate answer can undergo the same recognition process and be compared to the actual expected entity, not string

statement: The final system evaluation is executed on a separate test set, previously unused in development, and checked manually to avoid overfitting.
source_span: To avoid overfitting, the final system evaluation is executed on a separate test set, previously unused in development, and is checked manually.

statement: The paper adds a neural network global lexicon model (NNGLM) and a neural network joint model (NNJM) to a phrase-based SMT system for grammatical error correction.
source_span: we address these limitations by using two different yet complementary neural network models, namely a neural network global lexicon model and a neural network joint model

statement: Phrase-based SMT systems suffer from limitations of discrete word representation, linear mapping, and lack of global context.
source_span: phrase-based SMT systems suffer from limitations of discrete word representation, linear mapping, and lack of global context

statement: The paper achieves statistically significant improvement in accuracy for grammatical error correction over a state-of-the-art GEC system.
source_span: we achieve statistically significant improvement in accuracy for grammatical error correction over a state-of-the-art GEC system

statement: The F0.5 measure, which weights precision twice as much as recall, is the evaluation metric widely used for GEC and was the official metric of the CoNLL 2014 shared task.
source_span: The INLINEFORM6 measure BIBREF19 , which weights precision twice as much as recall, is the evaluation metric widely used for GEC and was the official evaluation metric adopted in the CoNLL 2014 shared task

statement: Minimum error rate training (MERT) is used to find the optimal feature weights by maximizing the F measure on the development set.
source_span: To find the optimal feature weights ( INLINEFORM4 ), we use minimum error rate training (MERT), maximizing the INLINEFORM5 measure on the development set

statement: One of the first SMT approaches to GEC focused on correcting countability errors of mass nouns (e.g., many informations -> much information), using an artificially constructed parallel corpus.
source_span: One of the first approaches of using SMT for GEC focused on correction of countability errors of mass nouns (e.g., many informations INLINEFORM0 much information) BIBREF11 . They had to use an artificially constructed parallel corpus for training their SMT system.

statement: The authors state there is no prior work that uses NNGLM and NNJM together for SMT-based grammatical error correction.
source_span: To the best of our knowledge, there is no prior work that uses these two neural network models for SMT-based GEC.

statement: 82% of sentences generated by the LSTM-with-attention model were judged correct in manual annotation, a 10.3% improvement over an LSTM baseline.
source_span: we found that 82% of generated sentences are correct, an improvement of 10.3% over an LSTM baseline

statement: The entailment generation dataset, filtered from SNLI for entailment-class pairs, has a training set of 183,416 sentence pairs, a development set of 3,329 pairs, and a test set of 3,368 pairs.
source_span: This results in a training set of $183,416$ sentence pairs, a development set of $3,329$ pairs and a test of $3,368$ pairs.

statement: Training uses stochastic gradient descent with a mini-batch size of 64 and the ADAM optimizer with a first momentum coefficient of 0.9 and a second momentum coefficient of 0.999.
source_span: We use stochastic gradient descent with a mini-batch size of 64 and the ADAM optimizer BIBREF14 with a first momentum coefficient of $0.9$ and a second momentum coefficient of $0.999$ .

statement: Out-of-vocabulary words, comprising 10.5% of words, are randomly initialized by sampling uniformly from [-sqrt(3), sqrt(3)] and optimized during training.
source_span: Out-of-vocabulary words ( $10.5\%$ ) are randomly initialized by sampling values uniformly from $[-\sqrt{3}, \sqrt{3}]$ and optimized during training.

statement: Gradients are clipped using a norm of 5.0, and training stops after 25 epochs.
source_span: Furthermore, we clip gradients using a norm of $5.0$ . We stop training after 25 epochs.

statement: Using attention yields only a marginally higher BLEU score than without attention (43.1 vs. 42.8).
source_span: we found that using attention yields only a marginally higher BLEU score (43.1 vs. 42.8)

statement: 100 random test sentences were manually annotated to decide whether the generated sentence could indeed be inferred from the source sentence.

statement: For trivial issues like changing a word in the documentation, the preferred way to submit the patch is via a GitHub pull request without a Trac ticket.
source_span: the preferred way to provide the patch is using GitHub pull requests without a Trac ticket

statement: Django's policy is for contributors to "claim" tickets to let other developers know a bug or feature is being worked on.
source_span: our policy is for contributors to "claim" tickets in order to let other developers know that a particular bug or feature is being worked on

statement: If a ticket's "Owned by" field is assigned to "nobody," the ticket is available to be claimed.
source_span: If it's assigned to "nobody," then it's available to be claimed

statement: If a ticket has been assigned for weeks or months without activity, it's probably safe to reassign it to yourself.
source_span: If a ticket has been assigned for weeks or months without any activity, it's probably safe to reassign it to yourself

statement: For non-trivial changes, contributors have the option to sign and submit a Contributor License Agreement (CLA).
source_span: you have the option to sign and submit a `Contributor License Agreement`_ clarifying the status of your contribution

statement: If there's no progress on a claimed ticket for a week or two, another developer may ask the claimer to relinquish the claim.
source_span: If there's no sign of progress on a particular claimed ticket for a week or two, another developer may ask you to relinquish the ticket claim

statement: For small changes such as documentation typos or quick bug fixes, contributors don't need to claim tickets and can submit changes directly.
source_span: In the case of small changes, such as typos in the documentation or small bugs that will only take a few minutes to fix, you don't need to jump through the hoops of claiming tickets. Submit your changes directly

statement: A good fix should include a regression test to validate the fixed behavior and prevent the problem from recurring.
source_span: A good fix should also include a :doc:`regression test... to validate the behavior that has been fixed and to prevent the problem from arising again

statement: If code adds a new feature or modifies the behavior of an existing feature, the change should also contain documentation.
source_span: If the code adds a new feature, or modifies the behavior of an existing feature, the change should also contain documentation

statement: Patches submitted via Trac (not pull request) should use the format returned by the `git diff` command.
source_span: Submit patches in the format returned by the ``git diff`` command

statement: Patch files should be named with a .diff extension so the ticket tracker applies correct syntax highlighting.
source_span: Name the patch file with a ``.diff`` extension; this will let the ticket tracker apply correct syntax highlighting

statement: Patches should not be put in the ticket description or comment unless it's a single line patch.
source_span: Please *don't* put the patch in the ticket description or comment unless it's a single line patch

statement: AI-generated submissions that show no evidence of manual verification may be closed without review, and repeated low-quality contributions may lead to restricted participation in Django's development process.
source_span: Submissions that show no evidence of manual verification may be closed without review, and repeated low-quality contributions may lead to restricted participation in Django's development process

statement: Django's own test suite is located in the `tests` directory of the code base.
source_span: Django comes with a test suite of its own, in the ``tests`` directory of the code base

statement: Django's policy is to make sure all tests pass at all times.
source_span: It's our policy to make sure all tests pass at all times

statement: The quickstart for running Django's tests starts with forking Django on GitHub, then cloning the fork into a directory named django-repo and running ./runtests.py from the tests subdirectory.
source_span:
$ git clone https://github.com/YourGitHubName/django.git django-repo
   $ cd django-repo/tests
   $ python -m pip install -e ..
   $ python -m pip install -r requirements/py3.txt
   $ ./runtests.py

statement: If installing an optional test dependency like pylibmc fails, you can comment out its line in requirements/py3.txt and tests requiring pylibmc will be skipped automatically.
source_span: if installing ``pylibmc`` fails, comment out its line in ``requirements/py3.txt`` and continue with ``./runtests.py``. Tests that require ``pylibmc`` will be skipped automatically

statement: Django provides a sample settings module that uses the SQLite database to help users get started running tests.
source_span: Django provides and uses a sample settings module that uses the SQLite database

statement: By default, tox runs the test suite with SQLite plus black, blacken-docs, flake8, isort, lint-docs, zizmor, and the documentation spelling checker.
source_span: By default, ``tox`` runs the test suite with the bundled test settings file for SQLite, ``black``, ``blacken-docs``, ``flake8``, ``isort``, ``lint-docs``, ``zizmor``, and the documentation spelling checker

statement: To run Django's tests on Python 3.12 with PostgreSQL via tox, the command is `tox -e py312-postgres -- --settings=my_postgres_settings`.
source_span: $ tox -e py312-postgres -- --settings=my_postgres_settings

statement: JavaScript tests aren't run by default via tox because they require Node.js to be installed and aren't necessary for the majority of patches.
source_span: The JavaScript tests aren't run by default using ``tox`` because they require ``Node.js`` to be installed and aren't necessary for the majority of patches

statement: To run the JavaScript tests using tox, run `tox -e javascript`, which runs `npm install` and then `npm test`.
source_span:
$ tox -e javascript

This command runs ``npm install`` to ensure test requirements are up to date and then runs ``npm test``

statement: django-docker-box allows running Django's test suite across all supported databases and Python versions.
source_span: `django-docker-box`_ allows you to run the Django's test suite across all supported databases and python versions

statement: The included settings module for running Django's tests with SQLite is tests/test_sqlite.py.
source_span: The included settings module (``tests/test_sqlite.py``) allows you to run the test suite using SQLite

statement: A custom test settings module must define a "default" database and a database with the alias "other," which must use the same backend as default but have a different name.
source_span: A database with the alias ``other``. The ``other`` database is used to test that queries can be directed to different databases. This database should use the same backend as the ``default``, and it must have a different name

statement: After installing Git, you should configure your name and email with `git config --global user.name "Your Real Name"` and `git config --global user.email "you@email.com"`.
source_span:
$ git config --global user.name "Your Real Name"
  $ git config --global user.email "you@email.com"

statement: The `user.name` git config value should be the contributor's real name, not their GitHub nick.
source_span: Note that ``user.name`` should be your real name, not your GitHub nick

statement: To create a new branch for working on a ticket based on upstream/main, run `git checkout -b ticket_xxxxx upstream/main`.
source_span: git checkout -b ticket_xxxxx upstream/main

statement: For a fix on the 1.4 branch, the branch is created with `git checkout -b ticket_xxxxx_1_4 upstream/stable/1.4.x`.
source_span: git checkout -b ticket_xxxxx_1_4 upstream/stable/1.4.x

statement: Work is published to GitHub by running `git push origin ticket_xxxxx`.
source_span: git push origin ticket_xxxxx

statement: To change the message of the most recent commit, run `git commit --amend`.
source_span: git commit --amend

statement: To reword one of the last three commits, run `git rebase -i HEAD~3`, which opens an editor to change "pick" to "reword" on the target commit.
source_span: git rebase -i HEAD~3

statement: After rewriting a commit that has already been pushed to GitHub, you need to force-push with `git push --force-with-lease origin ticket_xxxxx`.
source_span: git push --force-with-lease origin ticket_xxxxx

statement: A good pull request has well-formed commit messages: a summary line followed by paragraphs wrapped at 72 characters.
source_span: well-formed messages for each commit: a summary line and then paragraphs wrapped at 72 characters thereafter

statement: Tests are always needed for a pull request, except for documentation-only changes.
source_span: documentation and tests, if needed -- actually tests are always needed, except for documentation changes

statement: The main and stable/A.B.x branches in the django/django repository are examples of "public branches" whose history should never change.
source_span: Good examples of public branches are the ``main`` and ``stable/A.B.x`` branches in the ``django/django`` repository

statement: A "topic branch" (such as ticket_xxxxx) can have its history freely rewritten with git rebase, since others shouldn't base their work on it.
source_span: the above branch is called a "topic branch" in Git parlance. You are free to rewrite the history of this branch, by using ``git rebase``

statement: The team submitted two systems to SemEval-2016 Task 12: Clinical TempEval, participating in Phase 1 (identifying time/event text spans) and Phase 2 (predicting event-to-document-creation-time relations).
source_span: participating in Phase 1, where we identified text spans of time and event expressions in clinical notes and Phase 2, where we predicted a relation between an event and its parent document creation time.

statement: Phase 1 of the challenge required identifying text spans of time and event expressions in clinical notes.
source_span: Phase 1, where we identified text spans of time and event expressions in clinical notes

statement: Phase 2 required predicting a relation between an event and its parent document creation time.
source_span: Phase 2, where we predicted a relation between an event and its parent document creation time

statement: A joint inference-based approach using structured prediction outperformed a vanilla recurrent neural network for temporal entity extraction.
source_span: a joint inference-based approach using structured prediction outperforms a vanilla recurrent neural network

statement: The joint inference system used Stanford's knowledge base construction framework, DeepDive.
source_span: using Stanford's knowledge base construction framework DeepDive

statement: Phase 2 relations were classified into the label set {Before, Overlap, Before/Overlap, After}.
source_span: assigning event attributes from the label set {Before, Overlap, Before/Overlap, After}

statement: Entity mentions were tagged using the THYME (Temporal History of Your Medical Events) corpus, a collection of clinic and pathology notes from the Mayo Clinic.
source_span: Entity mentions are tagged using a document collection of clinic and pathology notes from the Mayo Clinic called the THYME (Temporal History of Your Medical Events) corpus

statement: The MIMIC-III database contains 2.4M notes from critical care patients at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.
source_span: the MIMIC-III database containing 2.4M notes from critical care patients at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center

statement: The University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics (UIHC) corpus contains 15M predominantly inpatient notes.
source_span: the University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics (UIHC) corpus, containing 15M predominantly inpatient notes

statement: Word embeddings were trained with word2vec using the Skip-gram model with a 10 token window size, generating 100 and 300 dimensional embeddings.
source_span: All word embeddings in this document are trained with word2vec BIBREF8 using the Skip-gram model, trained with a 10 token window size... We generated 100 and 300 dimensional embeddings

statement: The RNN implementation was based on code available as part of Theano v0.7.
source_span: Our RNN implementation is based on code available as part of Theano v0.7

statement: Baseline RNN embedding parameters were initialized randomly in the range [-1.0, 1.0].
source_span: all embedding parameters are initialized randomly in the range [-1.0, 1.0]

statement: For document creation time relations, overall system performance was better than the year's median submission but fell short of the best system.
source_span: Overall system performance was better than this year's median submission, but again fell short of the best system.

statement: The paper proposes augmenting NMT systems with discrete translation lexicons to alleviate mistranslation of low-frequency content words.
source_span: We propose a method to alleviate this problem by augmenting NMT systems with discrete translation lexicons that efficiently encode translations of these low-frequency words.

statement: Two methods were tested to combine the lexicon probability with the standard NMT probability: using it as a bias, or via linear interpolation.
source_span: We test two methods to combine this probability with the standard NMT probability: (1) using it as a bias, and (2) linear interpolation.

statement: Experiments showed an improvement of 2.0-2.3 BLEU and 0.13-0.44 NIST score, plus faster convergence time.
source_span: Experiments on two corpora show an improvement of 2.0-2.3 BLEU and 0.13-0.44 NIST score, and faster convergence time.

statement: An example NMT error cited is mistranslating "Tunisia" into the word for "Norway."
source_span: the NMT system mistakenly translated “Tunisia” into the word for “Norway.”

statement: Experiments were performed on two English-Japanese translation corpora.
source_span: We perform experiments (§ SECREF5 ) on two English-Japanese translation corpora

statement: The NMT model used is based on the attentional method of luong15emnlp.
source_span: we use attentional models BIBREF2 ... Specifically, we use the method of luong15emnlp

statement: The attention similarity function was set to the dot product, following luong15emnlp.
source_span: which we set to the dot product, following luong15emnlp

statement: Lexicon probabilities were constructed using word alignment on training data, external resources such as a handmade dictionary, or a hybrid of the two.
source_span: using traditional word alignment methods on the training data (§ SECREF11 ), other external parallel data resources such as a handmade dictionary (§ SECREF13 ), or using a hybrid between the two (§ SECREF14 )

statement: The Edinburgh team built NMT systems for four language pairs at WMT16, each trained in both directions: English<->Czech, English<->German, English<->Romanian, and English<->Russian.
source_span: We participated in the WMT 2016 shared news translation task by building neural translation systems for four language pairs, each trained in both directions: English<->Czech, English<->German, English<->Romanian and English<->Russian.

statement: The systems are based on an attentional encoder-decoder using BPE subword segmentation for open-vocabulary translation with a fixed vocabulary.
source_span: Our systems are based on an attentional encoder-decoder, using BPE subword segmentation for open-vocabulary translation with a fixed vocabulary.

statement: The systems achieved improvements of 4.3-11.2 BLEU over the baseline systems.
source_span: we see improvements of 4.3--11.2 BLEU over our baseline systems

statement: In human evaluation, the systems were the (tied) best constrained system for 7 out of 8 translation directions in which they participated.
source_span: our systems were the (tied) best constrained system for 7 out of 8 translation directions in which we participated

statement: The baseline system used minibatches of size 80, maximum sentence length of 50, word embeddings of size 500, and hidden layers of size 1024.
source_span: We use minibatches of size 80, a maximum sentence length of 50, word embeddings of size 500, and hidden layers of size 1024.

statement: The gradient norm was clipped to 1.0.
source_span: We clip the gradient norm to 1.0

statement: Models were trained with Adadelta, reshuffling the training corpus between epochs.
source_span: We train the models with Adadelta BIBREF5 , reshuffling the training corpus between epochs.

statement: The model was validated every 10000 minibatches via BLEU on a validation set.
source_span: We validate the model every 10000 minibatches via Bleu on a validation set

statement: Decoding was performed with beam search using a beam size of 12.
source_span: Decoding is performed with beam search with a beam size of 12.

statement: 89500 BPE merge operations were learned for each language pair.
source_span: For each language pair, we learn 89500 merge operations.

statement: The amount of back-translated monolingual data ranged from 2 million to 10 million sentences per translation direction.
source_span: The amount of monolingual data back-translated for each translation direction ranges from 2 million to 10 million sentences.

statement: With dl4mt, a translation speed of about 200000 sentences per day was observed on a single Titan X GPU.
source_span: we observed a translation speed of about 200000 sentences per day (on a single Titan X GPU)

statement: For English-Romanian, full words were dropped with probability 0.1 on both source and target sides, while all other layers used a dropout probability of 0.2.
source_span: we drop out full words (both on the source and target side) with a probability of 0.1. For all other layers, the dropout probability is set to 0.2.

statement: Ensembles used the 4 last saved models, with models saved every 30000 minibatches.
source_span: use the 4 last saved models (with models saved every 30000 minibatches) for the ensemble results

statement: The study compares four PoS tagging systems on datasets covering 16 languages: two feature-based (MEMMs and CRFs) and two neural-based (bi-LSTMs).
source_span: we compare the performances of four systems on datasets covering 16 languages, two of these systems being feature-based (MEMMs and CRFs) and two of them being neural-based (bi-LSTMs)

statement: The paper's MEMM-based tagging system, used as the starting point, is called MElt.
source_span: our starting point is the MElt system BIBREF12 , an MEMM tagging system

statement: The tagging models were trained on the Universal Dependencies (v1.2) corpus set, complemented by morphosyntactic lexicons.
source_span: These models are trained on the Universal Dependencies (v1.2) corpus set BIBREF21 , complemented by morphosyntactic lexicons

statement: The CRF-based system used for comparison is MarMoT.
source_span: We compare the accuracy of our models with the scores obtained by the CRF-based system MarMoT BIBREF22

statement: The LSTM models compared in the study use Polyglot word vector representations.
source_span: which both make use of Polyglot word vector representations published by BIBREF23

statement: Feature-based models perform better on lexically richer datasets (e.g. morphologically rich languages), while neural-based models perform better on datasets with less lexical variability (e.g. English).
source_span: better performances are obtained with our feature-based models on lexically richer datasets (e.g. for morphologically rich languages), whereas neural-based results are higher on datasets with less lexical variability (e.g. for English)

statement: A prior 6-language comparison using the MarMoT system found that word-vector-based PoS tagging models outperform models relying on morphosyntactic resources.
source_span: This question has already been investigated for 6 languages by BIBREF18 using the state-of-the-art CRF-based tagging system MarMoT. The authors found that their best-performing word-vector-based PoS tagging models outperform their models that rely on morphosyntactic resources

statement: The macro-averaged accuracy of the enriched MElt models is higher than that of enriched MarMoT models and virtually identical to that of LSTMs enriched with word vector representations.
source_span: The macro-averaged accuracy of our enriched MElt models is above that of enriched MarMoT models and virtually identical to that of LSTMs enriched with word vector representations.

statement: MElt is a tagging system based on maximum entropy Markov models (MEMM), a class of discriminative models suitable for sequence labelling.
source_span: MElt BIBREF12 is a tagging system based on maximum entropy Markov models (MEMM) BIBREF5 , a class of discriminative models that are suitable for sequence labelling

statement: The paper proposes a video captioning framework called Bidirectional Long-Short Term Memory (BiLSTM).
source_span: we propose a novel video captioning framework, termed as Bidirectional Long-Short Term Memory (BiLSTM)

statement: The joint visual modelling approach combines a forward LSTM pass, a backward LSTM pass, and visual features from CNNs.
source_span: we first devise a joint visual modelling approach to encode video data by combining a forward LSTM pass, a backward LSTM pass, together with visual features from Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)

statement: The framework is evaluated on the Microsoft Video Description (MSVD) corpus.
source_span: We verify the effectiveness of our proposed video captioning framework on a commonly-used benchmark, i.e., Microsoft Video Description (MSVD) corpus

statement: Yao et al. proposed using 3-D CNNs with an attention mechanism to automatically choose the most relevant temporal fragments for video description, capturing only local temporal information.
source_span: Yao et al. proposed to use 3-D Convolutional Neural Networks to explore local temporal information in video clips, where the most relevant temporal fragments were automatically chosen for generating natural language description with attention mechanism

statement: Venugopalan et al. implemented an LSTM network to model the global temporal structure of the whole video snippet.
source_span: Venugopanlan et al. implemented a Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) network, a variant of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), to model the global temporal structure in whole video snippet

statement: Video features are extracted by sampling one frame from every ten frames and extracting the fc7 (second fully-connected) layer via VGG-16, producing an N-by-4096 feature matrix.
source_span: we sample one frame from every ten frames in the video and extract the INLINEFORM1 layer, the second fully-connected layer, to express selected frames. Then a INLINEFORM2 -by-4096 feature matrix generated to denote given video clip

statement: The authors claim their approach is one of the first to use bidirectional recurrent neural networks for exploring bidirectional global temporal structure in video captioning.
source_span: our approach is one of the first to utilize bidirectional recurrent neural networks for exploring bidirectional global temporal structure in video captioning

statement: The approach constructs two separate sequential processing models for video representation learning and language generation, rather than using the same LSTM for both encoding and decoding as in prior work.
source_span: We construct two sequential processing models for adaptive video representation learning and language description generation, respectively, rather than using the same LSTM for both video frames encoding and text decoding in BIBREF19

statement: Dialog management is commonly decomposed into two sequential subtasks: dialog state tracking and dialog policy learning.
source_span: The task of dialog management is commonly decomposed into two sequential subtasks: dialog state tracking and dialog policy learning.

statement: The paper introduces a novel dialog state tracking method based on a bilinear algebraic decomposition model with an efficient inference schema through collective matrix factorization.
source_span: This paper introduces a novel method of dialog state tracking based on a bilinear algebric decomposition model that provides an efficient inference schema through collective matrix factorization.

statement: The proposed dialog state tracking approach is evaluated on the second Dialog State Tracking Challenge (DSTC-2) dataset.
source_span: We evaluate the proposed approach on the second Dialog State Tracking Challenge (DSTC-2) dataset

statement: The proposed inference procedure computes the state transition with linear complexity with respect to the number of variables and observations.
source_span: is able to compute the state transition through an inference procedure with a linear complexity with respect to the number of variables and observations

statement: Statistical dialog state trackers are commonly categorized into generative and discriminative approaches, based on how the posterior probability distribution over the state is defined.
source_span: Statistical dialog state trackers are commonly categorized into one of two approaches according to how the posterior probability distribution over the state calculation is defined.

statement: The generative approach to dialog state tracking naturally fits into the Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) model, an integrated model for dialog state tracking and dialog strategy optimization.
source_span: it naturally fits into the Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) models as described in BIBREF3 , which is an integrated model for dialog state tracking and dialog strategy optimization

statement: The proposed decompositional model addresses coupled and temporal hidden variable models using an inference procedure based on Collective Matrix Factorization (CMF).
source_span: describes the proposed decompositional model for coupled and temporal hidden variable models and the associated inference procedure based on Collective Matrix Factorization (CMF)

statement: The paper's approach to increasing interpretability of RNNs is to combine a recurrent neural network with a hidden Markov model (HMM), described as a simpler and more transparent model.
source_span: combining an RNN with a hidden Markov model (HMM), a simpler and more transparent model

statement: The paper explores three combinations of RNNs and HMMs: an HMM trained on LSTM states; a hybrid model where an HMM is trained first and then a small LSTM is trained on HMM state distributions to fill performance gaps; and a jointly trained hybrid model.
source_span: an HMM trained on LSTM states; a hybrid model where an HMM is trained first, then a small LSTM is given HMM state distributions and trained to fill in gaps in the HMM's performance; and a jointly trained hybrid model

statement: In 2015, Google Photos' image tagging algorithm made headlines for mislabeling African Americans as gorillas.
source_span: made headlines in 2015 when the image tagging algorithm in Google Photos mislabeled African Americans as gorillas

statement: BIBREF4 showed that in LSTM language models, around 10% of the memory state dimensions can be interpreted with the naked eye by color-coding text data with the state values.
source_span: around 10% of the memory state dimensions can be interpreted with the naked eye by color-coding the text data with the state values

statement: The LSTM model used is a character-level LSTM with 1 layer and no dropout, based on the Element-Research library.
source_span: We use a character-level LSTM with 1 layer and no dropout, based on the Element-Research library.

statement: The LSTM is trained for 10 epochs, starting with a learning rate of 1, which is halved under a specified log-likelihood condition.
source_span: We train the LSTM for 10 epochs, starting with a learning rate of 1, where the learning rate is halved whenever

statement: The L2-norm of the parameter gradient vector is clipped at a threshold of 5 during LSTM training.
source_span: The $L_2$ -norm of the parameter gradient vector is clipped at a threshold of 5.

statement: The continuous HMM's hidden states are initialized using K-means clusters fit on LSTM states, to speed up convergence relative to random initialization.
source_span: (Continuous HMM) K-means clusters fit on LSTM states, to speed up convergence relative to random initialization.

statement: HMM states are sampled at each training iteration using the Forward Filtering Backwards Sampling (FFBS) algorithm.
source_span: Sample states using Forward Filtering Backwards Sampling algorithm (FFBS, BIBREF7 ).

statement: The study compares a hybrid HMM-LSTM approach, a continuous emission HMM trained on the hidden states of a 2-layer LSTM, and a discrete emission HMM trained directly on data.
source_span: We compare a hybrid HMM-LSTM approach with a continuous emission HMM (trained on the hidden states of a 2-layer LSTM), and a discrete emission HMM (trained directly on data).

statement: The framework couples the syntax and semantics of natural language sentences in a single generative model to build a semantic parser.
source_span: We present a framework that couples the syntax and semantics of natural language sentences in a generative model

statement: In the generative process, a semantic statement is first sampled from a prior, such as a set of beliefs in a knowledge base, and then a grammar probabilistically generates the output sentence.
source_span: a semantic statement is first sampled from a prior, such as from a set of beliefs in a knowledge base. Given this semantic statement, a grammar probabilistically generates the output sentence

statement: A joint semantic-syntactic parser is derived that returns the k-best semantic and syntactic parses for a given sentence.
source_span: A joint semantic-syntactic parser is derived that returns the $k$-best semantic and syntactic parses for a given sentence.

statement: The construction of the grammar invokes a novel application of hierarchical Dirichlet processes (HDPs), which requires a novel and efficient inference approach.
source_span: The construction of our grammar invokes a novel application of hierarchical Dirichlet processes (HDPs), which in turn, requires a novel and efficient inference approach.

statement: The experimental results show that, for a simple grammar, the parser outperforms a state-of-the-art CCG semantic parser and scales to knowledge bases with millions of beliefs.
source_span: our parser outperforms a state-of-the-art CCG semantic parser and scales to knowledge bases with millions of beliefs

statement: The semantic parser uses a large knowledge base called NELL to form a prior probability distribution on the meanings of sentences it parses.
source_span: a probabilistic semantic parser that uses a large knowledge base (NELL) to form a prior probability distribution on the meanings of sentences it parses

statement: The current work is limited to parsing sentences with simple noun-verb-noun syntax, such as "Horses eat hay," and considers only factual assertions in declarative sentences.
source_span: we currently use it to parse sentences with a simple noun-verb-noun syntax (e.g. "Horses eat hay."), and considers only factual assertions in declarative sentences

statement: The paper uses the example sentence "She started the machine with the GPU" to illustrate that without additional knowledge, it is ambiguous whether the GPU is part of the machine or a device used to start machines.
source_span: Consider the sentence “She started the machine with the GPU,” for example. Without additional knowledge... the reader cannot determine whether the GPU is part of the machine or if the GPU is a device that is used to start machines.

statement: This paper applies layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP) for the first time to natural language processing (NLP).
source_span: In this paper, we apply LRP for the first time to natural language processing (NLP).

statement: LRP is used to explain the predictions of a convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on a topic categorization task.
source_span: we use it to explain the predictions of a convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on a topic categorization task

statement: The paper compares LRP to standard sensitivity analysis using a word-deleting perturbation experiment, a PCA analysis, and various visualizations.
source_span: We compare our technique to standard sensitivity analysis, both qualitatively and quantitatively, using a"word deleting"perturbation experiment, a PCA analysis, and various visualizations.

statement: The experiments use the 20news-bydate version of the 20Newsgroups dataset, consisting of 11314 training and 7532 test documents evenly distributed among twenty fine-grained categories.
source_span: we use the 20news-bydate version of the 20Newsgroups dataset consisting of 11314/7532 train/test documents evenly distributed among twenty fine-grained categories

statement: LRP produces a decomposition of the function value f(x) on its input variables that satisfies the conservation property f(x) = sum over d of R_d.
source_span: The LRP technique produces a decomposition of the function value $f(x)$ on its input variables, that satisfies the conservation property

statement: In the LRP relevance redistribution formula, the stabilizing term epsilon that handles near-zero denominators is set to 0.01.
source_span: is a stabilizing term that handles near-zero denominators, with $\epsilon $ set to $0.01$

statement: Sensitivity analysis scores each input variable by its squared partial derivative, and unlike LRP it does not preserve the function value f(x) but instead preserves the squared l2-norm of the function gradient.
source_span: unlike LRP, sensitivity analysis does not preserve the function value $f(x)$ , but the squared $l_2$ -norm of the function gradient

statement: The CNN document classifier used consists of the sequence of layers: convolution, ReLU, 1-max-pooling, and a fully-connected layer.
source_span: Conv \xrightarrow{} \texttt {ReLU} \xrightarrow{} \texttt {1-Max-Pool} \xrightarrow{} \texttt {FC}

statement: An implementation of LRP can be downloaded from www.heatmapping.org.
source_span: An implementation of LRP can be found in BIBREF10 and downloaded from www.heatmapping.org.

statement: There are three types of Django releases: security releases, regular version releases, and pre-releases.
source_span: There are three types of releases that you might need to make: * Security releases... * Regular version releases... * Pre-releases

statement: Security releases generally involve two or three simultaneous releases, e.g. 3.2.x, 4.0.x, and perhaps 4.1.x.
source_span: This'll generally involve two or three simultaneous releases -- e.g. 3.2.x, 4.0.x, and, depending on timing, perhaps a 4.1.x.

statement: A regular version release can be either a final release (e.g. 4.1) or a bugfix update (e.g. 4.1.1).
source_span: either a final release (e.g. 4.1) or a bugfix update (e.g. 4.1.1)

statement: Pre-releases include versions such as 4.2 alpha, beta, or rc.
source_span: Pre-releases: e.g. 4.2 alpha, beta, or rc.

statement: For a security release, the security distribution list must be pre-notified one week before the actual release.
source_span: If this is a security release, pre-notify the security distribution list one week before the actual release.

statement: Required Unix tools for releasing Django include bash 4.0+, git, GPG, make, man, hashing tools, and python.
source_span: bash (version 4.0+) * git * GPG * make * man * hashing tools... * python

statement: Building Django release artifacts requires a clean Python virtual environment with Python 3.10+ and pip 26.1+.
source_span: A clean Python virtual environment (Python 3.10+, pip 26.1+) to build artifacts.

statement: PyPI accounts used for Django releases must use only WebAuthn-based authentication factors, not TOTP one-time codes.
source_span: Ensure your PyPI account only uses WebAuthn-based authentication factors, not TOTP (one-time codes).

statement: Access to Django's project on Transifex requires a Manager role.
source_span: Access to Django's project on Transifex... with a Manager role.

statement: CVE IDs should be reserved 10 or more days before a security release.
source_span: 10 (or more) days before a security release

statement: Pre-notification of a security release must be sent out exactly one week before the release.
source_span: Send out pre-notification exactly **one week** before the security release.

statement: The security pre-notification email is signed with a command such as gpg --clearsign --digest-algo SHA256.
source_span: $ gpg --clearsign --digest-algo SHA256 prenotification-email.txt

statement: Security issues should be reported only to security@djangoproject.com, a private list open only to long-time, highly trusted Django developers, whose archives are not public.
source_span: Please report security issues **only** to ``security@djangoproject.com``. This is a private list only open to long-time, highly trusted Django developers, and its archives are not public.

statement: The Django Forum's "Using Django" category is for questions on installation, usage, or debugging of Django, and "Internals" is for discussion of Django's own development.
source_span: Using Django_: to ask any question regarding the installation, usage, or debugging of Django. * Internals_: for discussion of the development of Django itself.

statement: django-announce is a very low-traffic mailing list for announcing upcoming security releases, new Django releases, and security advisories.
source_span: A (very) low-traffic list for announcing upcoming security releases, new releases of Django, and security advisories.

statement: All ticket updates are mailed automatically to the django-updates mailing list, which is tracked by developers and interested community members.
source_span: All the ticket updates are mailed automatically to this list, which is tracked by developers and interested community members.

statement: The django-users and django-developers mailing lists are archived and no longer active, but remain available as a historical resource.
source_span: The following mailing lists are archived and no longer active. These are still available as a historical resource.

statement: The Using Django Forum category is now the preferred venue for usage questions, replacing the django-users mailing list.
source_span: The Using Django_ category of the official Forum_ is now the preferred venue for asking usage questions.

statement: The Internals Forum category is now the preferred venue for discussing Django's development, replacing the django-developers mailing list.
source_span: The Internals_ category of the official Forum_ is now the preferred venue for discussing the development of Django.

statement: The Django Project is managed by a team of volunteers pursuing three goals: driving development of the Django framework, fostering the Django ecosystem, and leading the Django community per its Code of Conduct.
source_span: managed by a team of volunteers pursuing three goals: - Driving the development of the Django web framework, - Fostering the ecosystem of Django-related software, - Leading the Django community in accordance with the values described in the Django Code of Conduct.

statement: The Django Project is not a legal entity; the Django Software Foundation, a non-profit organization, handles its financial and legal matters.
source_span: The Django Project isn't a legal entity. The Django Software Foundation, a non-profit organization, handles financial and legal matters related to the Django Project.

statement: Mergers are a small set of people who merge pull requests to the Django Git repository.
source_span: Mergers_ are a small set of people who merge pull requests to the Django Git repository.

statement: A Merger must not merge a change primarily authored by that Merger unless it has been approved by another Merger, a steering council member, a triage & review team member, or a security team member.
source_span: A Merger must not merge a change primarily authored by that Merger, unless the pull request has been approved by: - another Merger, - a steering council member, - a member of the triage & review team, or - a member of the security team.

statement: The steering council selects Mergers as necessary to maintain a minimum of three, with no upper limit on the number of Mergers.
source_span: The steering council_ selects Mergers_ as necessary to maintain their number at a minimum of three... There is no upper limit to the number of Mergers.

statement: A person must not simultaneously serve as both a Merger and a steering council member; if a Merger is elected to the council, they immediately cease being a Merger.
source_span: A person must not simultaneously serve as a member of the steering council. If a Merger is elected to the steering council, they shall cease to be a Merger immediately upon taking up membership in the steering council.

statement: A person may serve in the roles of Releaser and Merger simultaneously.
source_span: A person may serve in the roles of Releaser and Merger simultaneously.

statement: Releasers are a small set of people who have the authority to upload packaged Django releases to the Python Package Index (PyPI) and to the djangoproject.com website.
source_span: Releasers_ are a small set of people who have the authority to upload packaged releases of Django to the :pypi:`Python Package Index <Django>` and to the `djangoproject.com`_ website.

statement: The steering council selects Releasers as necessary to maintain a minimum of three, with no upper limit on the number of Releasers.
source_span: The steering council_ selects Releasers_ as necessary to maintain their number at a minimum of three... There is no upper limit to the number of Releasers.

statement: The steering council provides oversight of Django's development and release process, assists in setting the direction of feature development and releases, selects Mergers and Releasers, and has a tie-breaking vote when other decision-making processes fail.
source_span: The steering council is a group of experienced contributors who: - provide oversight of Django's development and release process, - assist in setting the direction of feature development and releases, - select Mergers and Releasers, and - have a tie-breaking vote when other decision-making processes fail.

statement: The paper addresses KBP slot filling, which extracts relation information from newswire documents for knowledge base construction.
source_span: the task of KBP slot filling -- extracting relation information from newswire documents for knowledge base construction

statement: The pipeline employs Relational Dependency Networks (RDNs) to learn linguistic patterns for relation extraction.
source_span: employs Relational Dependency Networks (RDNs) to learn linguistic patterns for relation extraction

statement: The system incorporates weak supervision, word2vec features, joint learning, and human advice as components.
source_span: weak supervision, word2vec features, joint learning and the use of human advice, can be incorporated in this relational framework

statement: The different components are evaluated on the benchmark KBP 2015 task.
source_span: evaluate the different components in the benchmark KBP 2015 task

statement: The KBP relation extraction task is commonly decomposed into two subtasks: entity linking and slot filling.
source_span: entity linking, in which entities are linked to already identified identities within the document or to entities in the existing KB, and slot filling, which identifies certain attributes about a target entity

statement: The authors learn on a set of 14 relations.
source_span: present the set of 14 relations that we learn on

statement: Raw text is processed using the Stanford CoreNLP Toolkit to extract parts-of-speech, word lemmas, parse trees, dependency graphs, and named-entity recognition information.
source_span: Raw text is processed using the Stanford CoreNLP Toolkit to extract parts-of-speech, word lemmas, etc. as well as generate parse trees, dependency graphs and named-entity recognition information

statement: The system uses word vectors from Stanford and Google along with expert-selected words related to the target relations, such as 'father' and 'mother', or 'devout', 'convert', and 'follow'.
source_span: We use word vectors from Stanford and Google along with a few specific words that, experts believe, are related to the relations learned. For example, we include words such as “father” and “mother”... or “devout”,“convert”, and “follow”

statement: The two weak supervision approaches used are distant supervision and knowledge-based weak supervision, following Soni et al. akbc16.
source_span: we employ two approaches for generating weakly supervised examples – distant supervision and knowledge-based weak supervision

statement: Distant supervision uses three data sources: Never Ending Language Learner (NELL), Wikipedia Infoboxes, and Freebase.
source_span: we use three data sources – Never Ending Language Learner (NELL) BIBREF4 , Wikipedia Infoboxes and Freebase

statement: The study proposes a statistical learning approach to predict political bias from text, using standard text features extracted from speeches and manifestos of political parties.

statement: Political power appears to be strongly correlated with positive sentiment of a text.

statement: Two approaches are used to make the model's results more interpretable: relating discriminative text features to a party's political orientation, and correlating sentiment features of texts with a measure of political power.

statement: The Question.was_published_recently() method incorrectly returns True if the Question's pub_date is in the future, not just when published within the last day.
source_span: the ``Question.was_published_recently()`` method returns ``True`` if the ``Question`` was published within the last day (which is correct) but also if the ``Question``’s ``pub_date`` field is in the future (which certainly isn't).

statement: In the shell demonstration, a Question object with pub_date set 30 days in the future returns True from was_published_recently(), confirming the bug.
source_span:
>>> future_question = Question(pub_date=timezone.now() + datetime.timedelta(days=30))
    >>> # was it published recently?
    >>> future_question.was_published_recently()
    True
