source_span: This was the first time React Conf was hosted online, and it was streamed for free, translated to 8 different languages.

statement: Over 50,000 people registered for React Conf 2021, with over 60,000 views of 19 talks and 5,000 Discord participants across both events.
source_span: Over 50,000 people registered, with over 60,000 views of 19 talks, and 5,000 participants in Discord across both events.

statement: React 18 adds the long-awaited concurrent renderer and updates to Suspense without any major breaking changes.
source_span: React 18 adds the long-awaited concurrent renderer and updates to Suspense without any major breaking changes.

statement: There is no concurrent mode in React 18, only concurrent features.
source_span: This means there is no concurrent mode, only concurrent features.

statement: At the keynote, the React team announced that the React 18 RC was available to try.
source_span: we also announced that the React 18 RC is available to try now

statement: To try the React 18 RC, developers upgrade dependencies with 'npm install react@rc react-dom@rc'.
source_span: npm install react@rc react-dom@rc

statement: Shaundai Person gave a talk deep-diving into Streaming Server Rendering with Suspense.
source_span: For a deep dive, see [Shaundai Person](https://twitter.com/shaundai)'s talk here

statement: The first React Working Group was created for React 18 and helped refine new APIs including useId, useSyncExternalStore, and useInsertionEffect.
source_span: Together we worked to create our gradual adoption strategy and refine new APIs such as `useId`, `useSyncExternalStore`, and `useInsertionEffect`.

statement: The React team announced a newly formed React DevTools team and a new Timeline Profiler to help debug React apps.
source_span: we also announced the newly formed React DevTools team and a new Timeline Profiler to help developers debug their React apps

statement: Xuan Huang (黄玄) shared an update from React Labs research into an auto-memoizing compiler.
source_span: Xuan Huang (黄玄) shared an update from our React Labs research into an auto-memoizing compiler

statement: Rachel Nabors gave a keynote about React's investment in new documentation, which later shipped as react.dev.
source_span: Rachel Nabors kicked off a section of talks about learning and designing with React with a keynote about our investment in React's new docs

statement: The React 18 upgrade guide was published March 8, 2022 by Rick Hanlon.
source_span: March 08, 2022 by [Rick Hanlon]

statement: React 18 will ship in a future version of React Native because it relies on the New React Native Architecture.
source_span: For React Native users, React 18 will ship in a future version of React Native. This is because React 18 relies on the New React Native Architecture

statement: To install the latest version of React, run 'npm install react react-dom'.
source_span: npm install react react-dom

statement: ReactDOM.render is no longer supported in React 18; createRoot should be used instead.
source_span: ReactDOM.render is no longer supported in React 18. Use createRoot instead.

statement: unmountComponentAtNode has been changed to root.unmount in the new root API.
source_span: We've also changed `unmountComponentAtNode` to `root.unmount`

statement: The callback argument was removed from render because it usually does not work as expected with Suspense.
source_span: We've also removed the callback from render, since it usually does not have the expected result when using Suspense

statement: Apps using server-side rendering with hydration should upgrade 'hydrate' to 'hydrateRoot'.
source_span: if your app uses server-side rendering with hydration, upgrade `hydrate` to `hydrateRoot`

statement: renderToNodeStream is deprecated in React 18.
source_span: `renderToNodeStream`: **Deprecated ⛔️️**

statement: renderToPipeableStream is a new API for streaming in Node environments.
source_span:
Instead, for streaming in Node environments, use:
* `renderToPipeableStream`: **New ✨**

statement: renderToReadableStream is a new API introduced to support streaming SSR with Suspense for modern edge runtime environments such as Deno and Cloudflare Workers.
source_span:
We're also introducing a new API to support streaming SSR with Suspense for modern edge runtime environments, such as Deno and Cloudflare workers:
* `renderToReadableStream`: **New ✨**

statement: renderToString and renderToStaticMarkup continue to work in React 18 but with limited support for Suspense.
source_span:
The following APIs will continue working, but with limited support for Suspense:
* `renderToString`: **Limited** ⚠️
* `renderToStaticMarkup`: **Limited** ⚠️

statement: renderToStaticNodeStream continues to work in React 18 for rendering e-mails.
source_span:
this API will continue to work for rendering e-mails:
* `renderToStaticNodeStream`

statement: With the updated TypeScript definitions, the children prop must now be listed explicitly when defining component props.
source_span: The most notable change is that the `children` prop now needs to be listed explicitly when defining props

statement: React 18 adds out-of-the-box performance improvements by doing more batching by default (Automatic Batching).
source_span: React 18 adds out-of-the-box performance improvements by doing more batching by default.

statement: The React v18.0 announcement was published March 29, 2022 by The React Team.
source_span: March 29, 2022 by [The React Team]

statement: React 18 became available on npm.
source_span: React 18 is now available on npm!

statement: React 18 includes automatic batching, the new startTransition API, and streaming server-side rendering with Suspense support.
source_span: Our latest major version includes out-of-the-box improvements like automatic batching, new APIs like startTransition, and streaming server-side rendering with support for Suspense.

statement: Concurrent React is opt-in and only enabled when a concurrent feature is used.
source_span: Concurrent React is opt-in — it's only enabled when you use a concurrent feature

statement: The React 18 Working Group was formed last summer (before the March 2022 release) to gather feedback from community experts and ensure a smooth upgrade experience.
source_span: Last summer, [we formed the React 18 Working Group] to gather feedback from experts in the community and ensure a smooth upgrade experience for the entire React ecosystem.

statement: React 18 will ship in React Native with the New React Native Architecture.
source_span: For React Native users, React 18 will ship in React Native with the New React Native Architecture.

statement: A key property of Concurrent React is that rendering is interruptible.
source_span: A key property of Concurrent React is that rendering is interruptible.

statement: The React team planned to add a new component called Offscreen in an upcoming minor release to implement reusable state.
source_span: In an upcoming minor, we're planning to add a new component called `<Offscreen>` that implements this pattern.

statement: Strict Mode does not affect production behavior; in development it logs extra warnings and double-invokes functions expected to be idempotent.
source_span: Strict Mode doesn't affect production behavior, but during development it will log extra warnings and double-invoke functions that are expected to be idempotent.

statement: The tutorial shows how to add Django Debug Toolbar, a commonly used third-party package.
source_span: This tutorial will show how to add :pypi:`Django Debug Toolbar<django-debug-toolbar>`, a commonly used third-party package.

statement: Django Debug Toolbar has ranked in the top three most used third-party packages in the Django Developers Survey in recent years.
source_span: The Django Debug Toolbar has ranked in the top three most used third-party packages in the Django Developers Survey in recent years.

statement: Django Debug Toolbar is a third-party package maintained by the community organization Django Commons.
source_span: It's a third-party package that is maintained by the community organization `Django Commons <https://github.com/django-commons>`_.

statement: Django Debug Toolbar is installed by running 'python -m pip install django-debug-toolbar' within an activated virtual environment.
source_span: $ python -m pip install django-debug-toolbar

statement: Once installed, the DjDT handle appears on the right side of the browser window when browsing to http://localhost:8000/admin/.
source_span: you should be able to see the DjDT "handle" on the right side of the browser window when you browse to ``http://localhost:8000/admin/``.

statement: Django Debug Toolbar's issue tracker is on GitHub.
source_span: Django Debug Toolbar’s is `on GitHub <https://github.com/django-commons/django-debug-toolbar/issues>`_.

statement: Django Packages (djangopackages.org) is a resource for finding third-party Django packages.
source_span: the fantastic Django resource, `Django Packages <https://djangopackages.org/>`_.

statement: Adam Johnson wrote a blog post outlining characteristics that qualify a package as 'well maintained'.
source_span: `Adam Johnson has a blog post <https://adamj.eu/tech/2021/11/04/the-well-maintained-test/>`_ that outlines a set of characteristics that qualifies a package as "well maintained".

statement: Django's documentation contains almost 450,000 words.
source_span: Django's got a *lot* of documentation -- almost 450,000 words and counting

statement: Reading every word of the introductory material amounts to reading about 5% of the overall Django documentation.
source_span: if you've read every single word, you've read about 5% of the overall documentation

statement: Django's documentation is kept in the same source control system as its code, living in the docs directory of the Git repository.
source_span: Django's documentation is kept in the same source control system as its code. It lives in the :source:`docs` directory of our Git repository.

statement: The most recent version of the Django documentation lives at https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/.
source_span: The most recent version of the Django documentation lives at https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/.

statement: Documentation-related changes, corrections, and suggestions should be submitted via the ticket system at https://code.djangoproject.com/.
source_span: .. _ticket system: https://code.djangoproject.com/

statement: For help with a particular Django setup rather than documentation tickets, users should try the Django Forum or the Django Discord server.
source_span: try the `Django Forum`_ or the `Django Discord server`_ instead.

statement: The Unix grep utility can be used to search Django's plain-text documentation, e.g. 'grep -r max_length /path/to/django/docs/'.
source_span: $ grep -r max_length /path/to/django/docs/

statement: Django's documentation uses a system called Sphinx to convert from plain text to HTML.
source_span: Django's documentation uses a system called Sphinx__ to convert from plain text to HTML.

statement: The blog post 'The Plan for React 18' was published on June 8, 2021.
source_span: June 8, 2021 by

statement: The React team started work on React 18, which will be the next major version.
source_span: We’ve started work on the React 18 release, which will be our next major version.

statement: The React team created a Working Group to prepare the community for gradual adoption of new features in React 18.
source_span: We’ve created a Working Group to prepare the community for gradual adoption of new features in React 18.

statement: The React team published a React 18 Alpha so that library authors can try it and provide feedback.
source_span: We’ve published a React 18 Alpha so that library authors can try it and provide feedback.

statement: React 18 will include automatic batching, a new startTransition API, and a new streaming server renderer with built-in support for React.lazy.
source_span: React 18 will include out-of-the-box improvements (like automatic batching), new APIs (like `startTransition`), and a new streaming server renderer with built-in support for `React.lazy`.

statement: Concurrent rendering is a new opt-in mechanism that lets React prepare multiple versions of the UI at the same time.
source_span: It’s called “concurrent rendering” and it lets React prepare multiple versions of the UI at the same time.

statement: Concurrent rendering will only be enabled for updates triggered by one of the new features, allowing adoption of React 18 without rewrites.
source_span: concurrent rendering will only be enabled for updates triggered by one of the new features. In practice, this means you will be able to adopt React 18 without rewrites and try the new features at your own pace.

statement: Users can upgrade to React 18 with minimal or no changes to their application code, with effort comparable to a typical major React release, and many are expected to upgrade within a single afternoon.
source_span: You can upgrade to React 18 with minimal or no changes to your application code, with a level of effort comparable to a typical major React release...we expect that many users will be able to upgrade within a single afternoon.

statement: The React team successfully shipped concurrent features to tens of thousands of components at Facebook.
source_span: We successfully shipped concurrent features to tens of thousands of components at Facebook

statement: The React 18 Working Group is hosted on GitHub Discussions and available for the public to read, though only invited members can create or comment on threads.
source_span: The Working Group is hosted on GitHub Discussions and is available for the public to read....only invited members will be allowed to create or comment on threads. However, the threads are fully visible to the public

statement: New React 18 alphas are regularly published to npm using the @alpha tag, built from the most recent commit to the main repo; a merged feature or bugfix appears in an alpha the following weekday.
source_span: New alphas are regularly published to npm using the `@alpha` tag. These releases are built using the most recent commit to our main repo. When a feature or bugfix is merged, it will appear in an alpha the following weekday.

statement: Alpha releases of React 18 are not recommended for user-facing, production applications.
source_span: alpha releases are not recommended for user-facing, production applications

statement: The projected React 18 release timeline is: Library Alpha available today, Public Beta at least several months later, Release Candidate at least several weeks after Beta, and General Availability at least several weeks after RC.
source_span:
Library Alpha: Available today
* Public Beta: At least several months
* Release Candidate (RC): At least several weeks after Beta
* General Availability: At least several weeks after RC

statement: The researchers created a corpus of 5,000 Reddit posts annotated with levels of dogmatism.
source_span: we have created a corpus of 5,000 Reddit posts annotated with levels of dogmatism

statement: The training dataset was built by randomly sampling 1000 posts each from the subreddits politics, business, science, and AskReddit, plus 1000 additional posts from the Reddit frontpage.
source_span: we have randomly sampled 1000 posts each from the subreddits politics, business, science, and AskReddit, and 1000 additional posts from the Reddit frontpage

statement: All sampled posts appeared on Reddit between January 2007 and March 2015.
source_span: All posts in our sample appeared between January 2007 and March 2015

statement: To control for length effects, sampled posts contained between 300 and 400 characters.
source_span: contain between 300 and 400 characters

statement: The sampling resulted in a total training dataset of 5000 posts.
source_span: This results in a total training dataset of 5000 posts.

statement: The Reddit dataset was labeled using crowdworkers on Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT).
source_span: We labeled the Reddit dataset using crowdworkers on Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT)

statement: Crowdworkers rated levels of dogmatism on a 5-point Likert scale.
source_span: we asked crowdworkers to rate levels of dogmatism on a 5-point Likert scale

statement: The annotation task was restricted to Masters workers on AMT to ensure quality.
source_span: we restricted the task to Masters workers and provided examples corresponding to each point on the scale

statement: The paper poses four research questions (R1-R4): what topics attract the highest dogmatism, how dogmatic beliefs cluster, how dogmatism influences conversation, and how other user behaviors relate to dogmatism.
source_span: R1: What kinds of topics (e.g., guns, LGBT) attract the highest levels of dogmatism?

statement: After training on the 5,000 annotated posts, the model was used to analyze millions of other Reddit posts to answer the research questions.
source_span: Our model is trained on only 5,000 annotated posts, but once trained, we use it to analyze millions of other Reddit posts to answer our research questions.

statement: The study uses two taxonomies, SNOMED-CT and MeSH, obtained via the UMLS Metathesaurus version 2016AA.
source_span: We obtain SNOMED–CT and MeSH via the Unified Medical Language System (UMLS) Metathesaurus (version 2016AA).

statement: The UMLS Metathesaurus contains approximately 2 million biomedical and clinical concepts integrated from over 150 different terminologies.
source_span: The Metathesaurus contains approximately 2 million biomedical and clinical concepts from over 150 different terminologies

statement: Concepts in the Metathesaurus are connected largely by two types of hierarchical relations: parent/child (PAR/CHD) and broader/narrower (RB/RN).
source_span: Concepts in the Metathesaurus are connected largely by two types of hierarchical relations: INLINEFORM0 / INLINEFORM1 (PAR/CHD) and INLINEFORM2 / INLINEFORM3 (RB/RN).

statement: Semantic similarity measures can be classified into three broad categories: path-based, feature-based, and information content (IC).
source_span: Measures of semantic similarity can be classified into three broad categories : path–based, feature–based and information content (IC).

statement: Rada et al. (1989) introduced the Conceptual Distance measure, defined as the length of the shortest path between two concepts in the MeSH hierarchy using broader-than (RB) and narrower-than (RN) relations.
source_span: RadaMBB89 introduce the Conceptual Distance measure. This measure is simply the length of the shortest path between two concepts ( INLINEFORM0 and INLINEFORM1 ) in the MeSH hierarchy.

statement: CaviedesC04 extended the Conceptual Distance measure to use parent (PAR) and child (CHD) relations.
source_span: CaviedesC04 extends this measure to use parent (PAR) and child (CHD) relations.

statement: Wu and Palmer (1994) introduced a correction to the shortest-path similarity measure that incorporates the depth of the two concepts and the depth of their Least Common Subsumer (LCS): similarity is twice the LCS depth divided by the product of the individual concepts' depths.
source_span: similarity is twice the depth of the two concept's LCS divided by the product of the depths of the individual concepts

statement: The method was evaluated on two datasets: one annotated for both similarity and relatedness, and another annotated for relatedness by two types of experts, medical doctors and medical coders.
source_span: One has been annotated for both similarity and relatedness, and the other has been annotated for relatedness by two different types of experts (medical doctors and medical coders).

statement: The classifier categorizes the stance of each tweet in a rumourous conversation as supporting, denying, or questioning the rumour.
source_span: classify the stance expressed in each individual tweet in a rumourous conversation as either supporting, denying or questioning the rumour

statement: The classifier is based on Gaussian Processes combined with multi-task learning.
source_span: we set out to develop an automated, supervised classifier that uses multi-task learning to classify the stance

statement: The approach was tested on two datasets with very different characteristics and varying distributions of stances.
source_span: exploring its effectiveness on two datasets with very different characteristics and varying distributions of stances

statement: After the 2010 earthquake in Chile, rumours of a volcano eruption and a tsunami warning in Valparaiso spread on Twitter and were later disproven.
source_span: a 2010 earthquake in Chile, where rumours of a volcano eruption and a tsunami warning in Valparaiso spawned on Twitter

statement: The Oxford English Dictionary defines a rumour as "a currently circulating story or report of uncertain or doubtful truth."

statement: DiFonzo and Bordia defined rumours as "unverified and instrumentally relevant information statements in circulation."

statement: The React team is abandoning forked I/O libraries like react-fetch in favor of an async/await model for Server Components.

statement: The React team is working with Vercel and Shopify to unify bundler support for shared RSC semantics in both webpack and Vite.

statement: Unifying RSC semantics across the whole React ecosystem is the major blocker for RSC reaching stable.
source_span: This is the major blocker for reaching stable.

statement: The React team gave an early preview of React Forget, a compiler, at React Conf 2021.

statement: React Forget automatically generates the equivalent of useMemo and useCallback calls to minimize the cost of re-rendering.
source_span: It’s a compiler that automatically generates the equivalent of useMemo and useCallback calls to minimize the cost of re-rendering

statement: The React team finished a rewrite of the compiler's architecture to make it more reliable and capable, enabling analysis of patterns such as local mutations.

statement: Offscreen hides UI visually while deprioritizing its content, an idea similar in spirit to the content-visibility CSS property.

statement: The React team introduced async/await as the primary way to do data fetching from Server Components.

statement: The React team plans to support client-side data loading via a new Hook called `use` that unwraps Promises.

statement: The React Canaries post was written by Dan Abramov, Sophie Alpert, Rick Hanlon, Sebastian Markbage, and Andrew Clark, and published May 3, 2023.
source_span: May 3, 2023 by Dan Abramov, Sophie Alpert, Rick Hanlon, Sebastian Markbåge, and Andrew Clark

statement: React is introducing a new officially supported Canary release channel.
source_span: We are introducing a new officially supported Canary release channel.

statement: Canaries let developers start using individual new React features before they land in the semver-stable releases.
source_span: Canaries let you start using individual new React features before they land in the semver-stable releases.

statement: Unlike the Experimental channel, React Canaries only include features the team reasonably believes to be ready for adoption.
source_span: Unlike the Experimental channel, React Canaries only include features that we reasonably believe to be ready for adoption.

statement: React continues to follow semver for every Stable release.
source_span: As always, React continues to follow semver for every Stable release.

statement: Typical React feature development goes through five stages: experimental_/unstable_ prefix in the experimental channel, testing with a Meta team, prefix removal and default availability on the main branch, posting an RFC, then writing documentation and releasing in a stable release.
source_span: Typically, every React feature has gone through the same stages: 1. We develop an initial version and prefix it with experimental_ or unstable_... 5. When we are close to cutting an open source release, we write documentation for the feature and finally release the feature in a stable React release.

statement: Every stable release of React Native is pinned to a specific commit from the main branch of the React repository.
source_span: Every stable release of React Native is pinned to a specific commit from the main branch of the React repository.

statement: TC39, the JavaScript standards committee, handles changes in numbered stages, a process the Canaries workflow resembles.
source_span: This workflow is closer to how TC39, the JavaScript standards committee, handles changes in numbered stages.

statement: The React team recommends against using Experimental releases in production because experimental APIs can undergo significant breaking changes or be removed entirely.
source_span: we recommend against using them in production because experimental APIs can undergo significant breaking changes on their way to stabilization (or can even be removed entirely)

statement: Going forward, the React team plans to announce significant breaking changes in Canary releases on their blog.

statement: The "React Labs: What We've Been Working On – February 2024" post was authored by Joseph Savona, Ricky Hanlon, Andrew Clark, Matt Carroll, and Dan Abramov, published February 15, 2024.

statement: React Compiler now powers instagram.com in production.

statement: React Compiler compiles code safely by modeling both the rules of JavaScript and the "rules of React," such as components needing to be idempotent and not mutate props or state.
source_span: React Compiler is able to compile code safely by modeling both the rules of JavaScript and the "rules of React". For example, React components must be idempotent — returning the same value given the same inputs — and can’t mutate props or state values.

statement: The React team recommends enabling Strict Mode and configuring React's ESLint plugin to catch subtle bugs and prepare code for React Compiler.

statement: Actions allow passing a function to DOM elements such as <form/>, e.g. <form action={search}>.

statement: Lifting state up means removing state from two components, moving it to their closest common parent, and passing it down via props.
source_span: remove state from both of them, move it to their closest common parent, and then pass it down to them via props. This is known as *lifting state up,*

statement: In the example, a parent Accordion component renders two separate Panel components.
source_span: a parent `Accordion` component renders two separate `Panel`s

statement: Each Panel component has a boolean isActive state that determines whether its content is visible.
source_span: Each `Panel` component has a boolean `isActive` state that determines whether its content is visible.

statement: Lifting state up to coordinate the two panels requires three steps: remove state from the child components, pass hardcoded data from the common parent, and add state to the common parent with event handlers.
source_span:
1. **Remove** state from the child components.
2. **Pass** hardcoded data from the common parent.
3. **Add** state to the common parent and pass it down together with the event handlers.

Childhood vascular tumors form from cells that make blood vessels or lymph vessels.
source_span: Childhood vascular tumors form from cells that make blood vessels or lymph vessels.

statement: Childhood vascular tumors may be classified into four groups: benign tumors, intermediate (locally aggressive) tumors, intermediate (rarely metastasizing) tumors, and malignant tumors.
source_span: Childhood vascular tumors may be classified into four groups.         - Benign tumors     - Intermediate (locally aggressive) tumors     - Intermediate (rarely metastasizing) tumors     - Malignant tumors

statement: The most common type of childhood vascular tumor is hemangioma, a benign tumor that usually goes away on its own.
source_span: The most common type of childhood vascular tumor is hemangioma, which is a benign tumor that usually goes away on its own.

statement: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma and tufted angioma are classified as intermediate, locally aggressive vascular tumors.
source_span: This summary has information about the following locally aggressive vascular tumors:            -  Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma and tufted angioma.

statement: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma and angiosarcoma of soft tissue are the malignant vascular tumors covered in the summary.
source_span: This summary has information about the following malignant vascular tumors:            -  Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma.     -  Angiosarcoma of soft tissue.

statement: Infantile hemangiomas are the most common type of benign vascular tumor in children and may also be called a "strawberry mark."
source_span: Infantile hemangiomas are the most common type of benign vascular tumor in children. An infantile hemangioma may also be called a "strawberry mark."

statement: Infantile hemangiomas are not usually seen at birth but appear when the infant is 3 to 6 weeks old.
source_span: These tumors are not usually seen at birth but appear when the infant is 3 to 6 weeks old.

statement: Most hemangiomas get bigger for about 5 months, then stop growing and slowly fade away completely over the next several years.
source_span: Most hemangiomas get bigger for about 5 months, then stop growing and slowly fade away completely during the next several years.

statement: Infantile hemangiomas are more common in girls, whites, premature babies, twins/triplets/other multiple births, and babies of older mothers or mothers with placental problems.
source_span: Infantile hemangiomas are more common in the following:          - Girls.    - Whites.    - Premature babies.    -  Twins, triplets, or other multiple births.     - Babies of mothers who are older at time of the pregnancy or who have problems with the placenta during pregnancy.

statement: Having more than five hemangiomas on the skin is a sign there may be hemangiomas in an organ, most commonly the liver.
source_span: Having more than five hemangiomas on the skin is a sign that there may be hemangiomas in an organ, most commonly the liver.

statement: PHACE syndrome causes hemangioma to spread across a large area of the body (usually head or face) and may involve other health problems with the large blood vessels, heart, eyes, and/or brain.
source_span: PHACE syndrome: A syndrome in which the hemangioma spreads across a large area of the body (usually the head or face). Other health problems involving the large blood vessels, heart, eyes, and/or brain may also occur.

statement: A physical exam and history are usually all that are needed to diagnose infantile hemangiomas.
source_span: A physical exam and history are usually all that are needed to diagnose infantile hemangiomas.

statement: Adult Hodgkin lymphoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the lymph system.
source_span: Adult Hodgkin lymphoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the lymph system.

statement: There are two main types of Hodgkin lymphoma: classical and nodular lymphocyte-predominant.
source_span: There are two main types of Hodgkin lymphoma: classical and nodular lymphocyte-predominant.

statement: The classical type of Hodgkin lymphoma is broken into four subtypes: nodular sclerosing, mixed cellularity, lymphocyte depletion, and lymphocyte-rich classical Hodgkin lymphoma.
source_span: The classical type is broken down into the following four subtypes:         - Nodular sclerosing Hodgkin lymphoma.    - Mixed cellularity Hodgkin lymphoma.    - Lymphocyte depletion Hodgkin lymphoma.    - Lymphocyte-rich classical Hodgkin lymphoma.

statement: Risk factors for adult Hodgkin lymphoma include being in young or late adulthood, being male, being infected with Epstein-Barr virus, and having a first-degree relative with Hodgkin lymphoma.
source_span: Risk factors for adult Hodgkin lymphoma include the following:         - Being in young or late adulthood.     - Being male.     - Being infected with the Epstein-Barr virus.    - Having a first-degree relative (parent, brother, or sister) with Hodgkin lymphoma.

statement: Pregnancy is not a risk factor for Hodgkin lymphoma.
source_span: Pregnancy is not a risk factor for Hodgkin lymphoma.

statement: Signs of adult Hodgkin lymphoma include swollen lymph nodes, fever, night sweats, and weight loss.
source_span: Signs of adult Hodgkin lymphoma include swollen lymph nodes, fever, night sweats, and weight loss.

statement: Other symptoms checked for in adult Hodgkin lymphoma include itchy skin and feeling very tired.
source_span: - Itchy skin.    - Feeling very tired.

statement: The sedimentation rate procedure measures how much inflammation is in the body and is also called erythrocyte sedimentation rate, sed rate, or ESR.
source_span: The sedimentation rate is a measure of how much inflammation is in the body. A higher than normal sedimentation rate may be a sign of lymphoma or another condition. Also called erythrocyte sedimentation rate, sed rate, or ESR.

statement: A pathologist views lymph node tissue under a microscope to look for cancer cells, especially Reed-Sternberg cells.
source_span: A pathologist views the tissue under a microscope to look for cancer cells, especially Reed-Sternberg cells.

statement: Three types of lymph node biopsy are excisional biopsy (removal of an entire lymph node), incisional biopsy (removal of part of a lymph node), and core biopsy (removal of part of a lymph node using a wide needle).
source_span: -  Excisional biopsy : The removal of an entire lymph node.       -  Incisional biopsy : The removal of part of a lymph node.      -  Core biopsy : The removal of part of a lymph node using a wide needle.

statement: Adult non-Hodgkin lymphoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the lymph system.
source_span: Adult non-Hodgkin lymphoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the lymph system.

statement: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma can begin in B lymphocytes, T lymphocytes, or natural killer cells.
source_span: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma can begin in B lymphocytes, T lymphocytes, or natural killer cells.

statement: Most types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma begin in B lymphocytes.
source_span: Most types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma begin in B lymphocytes.

statement: Indolent lymphoma tends to grow and spread slowly with few signs and symptoms, while aggressive lymphoma grows and spreads quickly with symptoms that can be severe.
source_span: Indolent lymphoma tends to grow and spread slowly, and has few signs and symptoms. Aggressive lymphoma grows and spreads quickly, and has signs and symptoms that can be severe.

statement: Follicular lymphoma is the most common type of indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma and begins in B lymphocytes.
source_span: Follicular lymphoma is the most common type of indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma. It is a very slow-growing type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that begins in B lymphocytes.

statement: Most patients with follicular lymphoma are age 50 years and older when they are diagnosed.
source_span: Most patients with follicular lymphoma are age 50 years and older when they are diagnosed.

statement: Follicular lymphoma can sometimes become a more aggressive type of lymphoma, such as diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
source_span: Sometimes follicular lymphoma can become a more aggressive type of lymphoma, such as diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

statement: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma is also called Waldenström macroglobulinemia and often spreads to the bone marrow, lymph nodes, and spleen.
source_span: It is also called Waldenstrm macroglobulinemia... Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma often spreads to the bone marrow, lymph nodes, and spleen.

statement: In lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, B lymphocytes turning into plasma cells make large amounts of monoclonal immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibody, and high levels of IgM cause the blood plasma to thicken.
source_span: B lymphocytes that are turning into plasma cells make large amounts of a protein called monoclonal immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibody. High levels of IgM antibody in the blood cause the blood plasma to thicken.

statement: There are five different types of marginal zone lymphoma, grouped by the type of tissue where the lymphoma formed.
source_span: There are five different types of marginal zone lymphoma. They are grouped by the type of tissue where the lymphoma formed

statement: Nodal marginal zone lymphoma forms in lymph nodes and is also called monocytoid B-cell lymphoma.
source_span: Nodal marginal zone lymphoma forms in lymph nodes. This type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma is rare. It is also called monocytoid B-cell lymphoma.

statement: AIDS-related lymphoma is a disease in which malignant cells form in the lymph system of patients who have AIDS.
source_span: AIDS-related lymphoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the lymph system of patients who have acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS).

statement: AIDS is caused by HIV, which attacks and weakens the body's immune system.
source_span: AIDS is caused by the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), which attacks and weakens the body's immune system.

statement: Signs of AIDS-related lymphoma include weight loss, fever, and night sweats.
source_span: Signs of AIDS-related lymphoma include weight loss, fever, and night sweats.

statement: Lymphomas are divided into two general types: Hodgkin lymphoma and non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
source_span: Lymphomas are divided into two general types: - Hodgkin lymphoma. - Non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

statement: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is more common than Hodgkin lymphoma in patients with AIDS.
source_span: Both Hodgkin lymphoma and non-Hodgkin lymphoma may occur in patients with AIDS, but non-Hodgkin lymphoma is more common.

statement: When AIDS-related lymphoma occurs in the central nervous system, it is called AIDS-related primary CNS lymphoma.
source_span: When AIDS-related lymphoma occurs in the central nervous system (CNS), it is called AIDS-related primary CNS lymphoma.

statement: AIDS-related lymphomas are aggressive (fast-growing).
source_span: AIDS-related lymphomas are aggressive.

statement: The two main types of AIDS-related non-Hodgkin lymphoma are diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (including B-cell immunoblastic lymphoma) and Burkitt or Burkitt-like lymphoma.
source_span: There are two main types of AIDS-related non-Hodgkin lymphoma: - Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (including B-cell immunoblastic lymphoma). - Burkitt or Burkitt-like lymphoma.

statement: Additional symptoms of AIDS-related lymphoma include painless swollen lymph nodes in the neck, chest, underarm, or groin and a feeling of fullness below the ribs.
source_span: Painless, swollen lymph nodes in the neck, chest, underarm, or groin. - A feeling of fullness below the ribs.

statement: Diagnostic tests for AIDS-related lymphoma include physical exam and history, complete blood count, HIV test, lymph node biopsy, bone marrow aspiration and biopsy, and chest x-ray.
source_span: Physical exam and history ... Complete blood count (CBC) ... HIV test ... Lymph node biopsy ... Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy ... Chest x-ray

statement: AIDS-related lymphoma can occur outside lymph nodes in the bone marrow, liver, meninges, and gastrointestinal tract, and less often in the anus, heart, bile duct, gingiva, and muscles.
source_span: Sometimes AIDS-related lymphoma occurs outside the lymph nodes in the bone marrow, liver, meninges (thin membranes that cover the brain) and gastrointestinal tract. Less often, it may occur in the anus, heart, bile duct, gingiva, and muscles.

statement: Mycosis fungoides and the Sézary syndrome are diseases in which lymphocytes become malignant and affect the skin.
source_span: Mycosis fungoides and the Szary syndrome are diseases in which lymphocytes (a type of white blood cell) become malignant (cancerous) and affect the skin.

statement: Mycosis fungoides and the Sézary syndrome are the two most common types of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
source_span: Mycosis fungoides and the Szary syndrome are the two most common types of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma).

statement: In mycosis fungoides, T-cell lymphocytes become cancerous and affect only the skin; in Sézary syndrome, cancerous T-cell lymphocytes affect the skin and are also found in the blood.
source_span: In mycosis fungoides, T-cell lymphocytes become cancerous and affect the skin. In the Szary syndrome, cancerous T-cell lymphocytes affect the skin and are in the blood.

statement: In Sézary syndrome, skin all over the body is reddened, itchy, peeling, and painful.
source_span: Also, skin all over the body is reddened, itchy, peeling, and painful.

statement: A sign of mycosis fungoides is a red rash on the skin.
source_span: A sign of mycosis fungoides is a red rash on the skin.

statement: Mycosis fungoides may go through four phases: premycotic, patch, plaque, and tumor.
source_span: Mycosis fungoides may go through the following phases: - Premycotic phase ... - Patch phase ... - Plaque phase ... - Tumor phase

statement: The premycotic phase is a scaly, red rash in areas of the body usually not exposed to the sun, causes no symptoms, and may last for months or years.
source_span: Premycotic phase: A scaly, red rash in areas of the body that usually are not exposed to the sun. This rash does not cause symptoms and may last for months or years.

statement: Diagnostic tests for mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome include physical exam and history, complete blood count with differential, peripheral blood smear, skin biopsy, immunophenotyping, T-cell receptor (TCR) gene rearrangement test, and flow cytometry.
source_span: Physical exam and history ... Complete blood count with differential ... Peripheral blood smear ... Skin biopsy ... Immunophenotyping ... T-cell receptor (TCR) gene rearrangement test ... Flow cytometry

statement: Prognosis and treatment options for mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome depend on the stage of the cancer and the type of lesion (patches, plaques, or tumors).
source_span: The prognosis (chance of recovery) and treatment options depend on the following: - The stage of the cancer. - The type of lesion (patches, plaques, or tumors).

statement: Mycosis fungoides and the Sézary syndrome are hard to cure, and treatment is usually palliative to relieve symptoms and improve quality of life.
source_span: Mycosis fungoides and the Szary syndrome are hard to cure. Treatment is usually palliative, to relieve symptoms and improve the quality of life.

statement: Primary CNS lymphoma is a disease in which malignant cells form in the lymph tissue of the brain and/or spinal cord.
source_span: Primary central nervous system (CNS) lymphoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the lymph tissue of the brain and/or spinal cord.

statement: Primary CNS lymphoma can start in the brain, spinal cord, meninges, or the eye, where it is called ocular lymphoma.
source_span: Primary CNS lymphoma can start in the brain, spinal cord, or meninges (the layers that form the outer covering of the brain). Because the eye is so close to the brain, primary CNS lymphoma can also start in the eye (called ocular lymphoma).

statement: Having a weakened immune system may increase the risk of developing primary CNS lymphoma.
source_span: Having a weakened immune system may increase the risk of developing primary CNS lymphoma.

statement: Primary CNS lymphoma may occur in patients with AIDS, other immune system disorders, or those who have had a kidney transplant.
source_span: Primary CNS lymphoma may occur in patients who have acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) or other disorders of the immune system or who have had a kidney transplant.

statement: Diagnostic tests for primary CNS lymphoma include physical exam and history, neurological exam, slit-lamp eye exam, MRI, PET scan, lumbar puncture, stereotactic biopsy, and complete blood count with differential.
source_span: Physical exam and history ... Neurological exam ... Slit-lamp eye exam ... MRI ... PET scan ... Lumbar puncture ... Stereotactic biopsy ... Complete blood count (CBC) with differential

statement: A lumbar puncture, also called an LP or spinal tap, collects cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from the spinal column for examination.
source_span: Lumbar puncture: A procedure used to collect cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from the spinal column ... This procedure is also called an LP or spinal tap.

statement: During MRI for primary CNS lymphoma, gadolinium is injected into a vein and collects around cancer cells so they show up brighter in the picture.
source_span: A substance called gadolinium is injected into the patient through a vein. The gadolinium collects around the cancer cells so they show up brighter in the picture.

statement: Prognosis for primary CNS lymphoma depends on the patient's age and general health, the level of certain substances in the blood and CSF, where the tumor is located, and whether the patient has AIDS.
source_span: The prognosis (chance of recovery) depends on the following: - The patient's age and general health. - The level of certain substances in the blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). - Where the tumor is in the central nervous system, eye, or both. - Whether the patient has AIDS.

statement: Childhood Hodgkin lymphoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the lymph system.
source_span: Childhood Hodgkin lymphoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the lymph system.

statement: There are two types of childhood Hodgkin lymphoma: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma and Nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma.
source_span: The two types of childhood Hodgkin lymphoma are: - Classical Hodgkin lymphoma. - Nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma.

statement: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma is divided into four subtypes: lymphocyte-rich, nodular sclerosis, mixed cellularity, and lymphocyte-depleted.
source_span: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma is divided into four subtypes, based on how the cancer cells look under a microscope: - Lymphocyte-rich classical Hodgkin lymphoma. - Nodular sclerosis Hodgkin lymphoma. - Mixed cellularity Hodgkin lymphoma. - Lymphocyte-depleted Hodgkin lymphoma.

statement: Hodgkin lymphoma often occurs in adolescents 15 to 19 years of age.
source_span: Hodgkin lymphoma often occurs in adolescents 15 to 19 years of age.

statement: Epstein-Barr virus infection increases the risk of childhood Hodgkin lymphoma.
source_span: Epstein-Barr virus infection increases the risk of childhood Hodgkin lymphoma.

statement: Risk factors for childhood Hodgkin lymphoma include EBV infection, HIV infection, certain immune system diseases, a personal history of mononucleosis, and having a parent or sibling with a personal history of Hodgkin lymphoma.
source_span: Risk factors for childhood Hodgkin lymphoma include the following: - Being infected with the Epstein-Barr virus. - Being infected with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). - Having certain diseases of the immune system. - Having a personal history of mononucleosis ("mono"). - Having a parent or sibling with a personal history of Hodgkin lymphoma.

statement: Being exposed to common infections in early childhood may decrease the risk of Hodgkin lymphoma in children.
source_span: Being exposed to common infections in early childhood may decrease the risk of Hodgkin lymphoma in children because of the effect it has on the immune system.

statement: Signs of childhood Hodgkin lymphoma include swollen lymph nodes, fever, night sweats, and weight loss.
source_span: Signs of childhood Hodgkin lymphoma include swollen lymph nodes, fever, night sweats, and weight loss.

statement: Fever, weight loss, and night sweats in childhood Hodgkin lymphoma are called B symptoms.
source_span: Fever, weight loss, and night sweats are called B symptoms.

statement: Tests used to diagnose childhood Hodgkin lymphoma include physical exam and history, CT scan, PET scan, chest x-ray, and complete blood count (CBC).
source_span: Physical exam and history ... CT scan (CAT scan) ... PET scan (positron emission tomography scan) ... Chest x-ray ... Complete blood count (CBC)

statement: In a PET scan, a small amount of radioactive glucose is injected into a vein and malignant tumor cells show up brighter because they take up more glucose than normal cells.
source_span: A small amount of radioactive glucose (sugar) is injected into a vein. ... Malignant tumor cells show up brighter in the picture because they are more active and take up more glucose than normal cells do.

statement: Childhood non-Hodgkin lymphoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the lymph system.
source_span: Childhood non-Hodgkin lymphoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the lymph system.

statement: There are three major types of childhood non-Hodgkin lymphoma: mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, lymphoblastic lymphoma, and anaplastic large cell lymphoma.
source_span: There are three major types of childhood non-Hodgkin lymphoma. - Mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma - Lymphoblastic lymphoma - Anaplastic large cell lymphoma

statement: Mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas include Burkitt and Burkitt-like lymphoma/leukemia, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma.
source_span: Mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas include: - Burkitt and Burkitt-like lymphoma/leukemia ... - Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma ... - Primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma

statement: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is the most common type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma and occurs more often in adolescents than in children.
source_span: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is the most common type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma. ... Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma occurs more often in adolescents than in children.

statement: Burkitt and Burkitt lymphoma/leukemia have been linked to Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection, which is more likely to occur in patients in Africa than in the United States.
source_span: Both Burkitt leukemia and Burkitt lymphoma have been linked to infection with the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), although EBV infection is more likely to occur in patients in Africa than in the United States.

statement: Burkitt and Burkitt-like lymphoma/leukemia are diagnosed when a sample of tissue is checked and a certain change to the c-myc gene is found.
source_span: Burkitt and Burkitt-like lymphoma/leukemia are diagnosed when a sample of tissue is checked and a certain change to the c-myc gene is found.

statement: Lymphoblastic lymphoma mainly affects T-cell lymphocytes, usually forms in the mediastinum, and causes trouble breathing, wheezing, trouble swallowing, or swelling of the head and neck.
source_span: Lymphoblastic lymphoma is a type of lymphoma that mainly affects T-cell lymphocytes. It usually forms in the mediastinum (the area behind the breastbone). This causes trouble breathing, wheezing, trouble swallowing, or swelling of the head and neck.

statement: Patients with anaplastic large cell lymphoma have a receptor called CD30 on the surface of their T cells.
source_span: Patients with anaplastic large cell lymphoma have a receptor, called CD30, on the surface of their T cells.

statement: Past treatment for cancer and having a weakened immune system affect the risk of having childhood non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
source_span: Past treatment for cancer and having a weakened immune system affect the risk of having childhood non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

statement: Signs of childhood non-Hodgkin lymphoma include breathing problems and swollen lymph nodes.
source_span: Signs of childhood non-Hodgkin lymphoma include breathing problems and swollen lymph nodes.

statement: Anal cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the anus.
source_span: Anal cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the anus.

statement: Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common type of anal cancer in the United States.
source_span: In the United States, the most common type of anal cancer is squamous cell carcinoma.

statement: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is the main cause of squamous cell carcinoma of the anus.
source_span: Studies show that human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is the main cause of this type of anal cancer.

statement: From 2004 to 2013, new cases of and deaths from anal cancer increased each year in the United States; the increase in new cases was slightly higher in women and the increase in deaths was slightly higher in men.
source_span: From 2004 to 2013, new cases of anal cancer and deaths from anal cancer increased each year. The increase in new cases was slightly higher in women and the increase in deaths from anal cancer was slightly higher in men.

statement: Risk factors for anal cancer include HPV infection, having many sexual partners, receptive anal intercourse, being older than 50 years, frequent anal redness/swelling/soreness, anal fistulas, and smoking cigarettes.
source_span: Risk factors include the following: - Being infected with human papillomavirus (HPV). - Having many sexual partners. - Having receptive anal intercourse (anal sex). - Being older than 50 years. - Frequent anal redness, swelling, and soreness. - Having anal fistulas (abnormal openings). - Smoking cigarettes.

statement: Signs of anal cancer include bleeding from the anus or rectum or a lump near the anus.
source_span: Signs of anal cancer include bleeding from the anus or rectum or a lump near the anus.

statement: Tests used to diagnose anal cancer include physical exam and history, digital rectal examination (DRE), anoscopy, proctoscopy, endo-anal or endorectal ultrasound, and biopsy.
source_span: Physical exam and history ... Digital rectal examination (DRE) ... Anoscopy ... Proctoscopy ... Endo-anal or endorectal ultrasound ... Biopsy

statement: The stages used for anal cancer are Stage 0 (Carcinoma in Situ), Stage I, Stage II, Stage IIIA, Stage IIIB, and Stage IV.
source_span: The following stages are used for anal cancer: - Stage 0 (Carcinoma in Situ) - Stage I - Stage II - Stage IIIA - Stage IIIB - Stage IV

statement: MRI with gadolinium uses a magnet, radio waves, and a computer to make detailed pictures of the brain and spinal cord, with gadolinium injected into a vein so cancer cells show up brighter; it is also called nuclear magnetic resonance imaging (NMRI).

This procedure is also called nuclear magnetic resonance imaging (NMRI).

statement: It is often difficult to completely remove AT/RT because of where the tumor is in the brain and because it may already have spread at the time of diagnosis.
source_span: It is often difficult to completely remove AT/RT because of where the tumor is in the brain and because it may already have spread at the time of diagnosis

statement: Immunohistochemistry is a test that uses antibodies to check for certain antigens in a tissue sample.
source_span: Immunohistochemistry : A test that uses antibodies to check for certain antigens in a sample of tissue

statement: Childhood brain stem glioma is a disease in which benign or malignant cells form in the tissues of the brain stem.
source_span: Childhood brain stem glioma is a disease in which benign (noncancer) or malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the brain stem

statement: Most childhood brain stem gliomas are pontine gliomas, which form in a part of the brain stem called the pons.
source_span: Most childhood brain stem gliomas are pontine gliomas, which form in a part of the brain stem called the pons

statement: Brain tumors are the third most common type of cancer in children.
source_span: Brain tumors are the third most common type of cancer in children

statement: There are two types of childhood brain stem glioma: diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) and focal glioma.
source_span: Childhood brain stem glioma is either a diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) or a focal glioma

statement: DIPG is a high-grade, fast-growing tumor that spreads all through the brain stem, is hard to treat, and has a poor prognosis.
source_span: DIPG is a high-grade tumor that is fast-growing and spreads all through the brain stem. It is hard to treat and has a poor prognosis

statement: Children younger than 3 years diagnosed with DIPG may have a better prognosis than children 3 years and older.
source_span: Children younger than 3 years diagnosed with DIPG may have a better prognosis than children who are 3 years and older

statement: A focal glioma is slow-growing, confined to one area of the brain stem, easier to treat than DIPG, and has a better prognosis.
source_span: A focal glioma is slow-growing and is in one area of the brain stem. It is easier to treat than DIPG and has a better prognosis

statement: The cause of most childhood brain tumors is unknown.
source_span: The cause of most childhood brain tumors is unknown

statement: Having neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is a possible risk factor for brain stem glioma.
source_span: Having certain genetic disorders, such as neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1)

statement: Symptoms of brain stem glioma include loss of ability to move one side of the face/body, loss of balance and trouble walking, vision and hearing problems, morning headache or headache after vomiting, nausea and vomiting, unusual sleepiness, more or less energy than usual, changes in behavior, and trouble learning in school.
source_span: Loss of ability to move one side of the face and/or body. - Loss of balance and trouble walking. - Vision and hearing problems.

statement: MRI with gadolinium involves injecting gadolinium into a vein, which collects around cancer cells so they show up brighter in the picture.
source_span: A substance called gadolinium is injected into a vein. The gadolinium collects around the cancer cells so they show up brighter in the picture

statement: If the MRI scan looks like the tumor is a DIPG, a biopsy is usually not done and the tumor is not removed.
source_span: If the MRI scan looks like the tumor is a DIPG, a biopsy is usually not done and the tumor is not removed

statement: If the MRI scan looks like a focal brain stem glioma, a biopsy may be done.
source_span: If the MRI scan looks like a focal brain stem glioma, a biopsy may be done

statement: CNS embryonal tumors may begin in embryonic (fetal) cells that remain in the brain after birth.
source_span: Central nervous system (CNS) embryonal tumors form in embryonic cells that remain in the brain after birth

statement: CNS embryonal tumors tend to spread through the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) to other parts of the brain and spinal cord.
source_span: CNS embryonal tumors tend to spread through the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) to other parts of the brain and spinal cord

statement: Brain tumors are the third most common type of childhood cancer, after leukemia and lymphoma.
source_span: brain tumors are the third most common type of childhood cancer, after leukemia and lymphoma

statement: Most CNS embryonal tumors are medulloblastomas, fast-growing tumors that form in brain cells in the cerebellum.
source_span: Most CNS embryonal tumors are medulloblastomas. Medulloblastomas are fast-growing tumors that form in brain cells in the cerebellum

statement: Medulloblastomas sometimes spread to the bone, bone marrow, lung, or other parts of the body, but this is rare.
source_span: Medulloblastomas sometimes spread to the bone, bone marrow, lung, or other parts of the body, but this is rare

statement: Nonmedulloblastoma embryonal tumors usually form in the cerebrum and include four types: embryonal tumors with multilayered rosettes (ETMR), medulloepitheliomas, CNS neuroblastomas, and CNS ganglioneuroblastomas.
source_span: Nonmedulloblastoma embryonal tumors are fast-growing tumors that usually form in brain cells in the cerebrum. ... There are four types of nonmedulloblastoma embryonal tumors

statement: Medulloepitheliomas occur most often in infants and young children.
source_span: They occur most often in infants and young children

statement: Pineoblastomas form in cells of the pineal gland and are usually malignant.
source_span: Pineoblastomas form in cells of the pineal gland and are usually malignant

statement: Pineoblastoma is linked with inherited changes in the retinoblastoma (RB1) gene.
source_span: Pineoblastoma is linked with inherited changes in the retinoblastoma (RB1) gene

statement: When retinoblastoma forms at the same time as a tumor in or near the pineal gland, it is called trilateral retinoblastoma.
source_span: When retinoblastoma forms at the same time as a tumor in or near the pineal gland, it is called trilateral retinoblastoma

statement: Risk factors for CNS embryonal tumors include the inherited diseases Turcot syndrome, Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome, Nevoid basal cell carcinoma (Gorlin) syndrome, Li-Fraumeni syndrome, and Fanconi anemia.
source_span: Risk factors for CNS embryonal tumors include having the following inherited diseases: -  Turcot syndrome. -  Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome. -  Nevoid basal cell carcinoma (Gorlin) syndrome. -  Li-Fraumeni syndrome. -  Fanconi anemia

statement: Germ cells that travel to other parts of the body during fetal development can grow into germ cell tumors, and those forming in the brain or spinal cord are called CNS germ cell tumors.
source_span: Sometimes while the fetus is forming, germ cells travel to other parts of the body and grow into germ cell tumors.

statement: The most common places for CNS germ cell tumors to form are near the pineal gland and in the area of the brain that includes the pituitary gland and tissue just above it.
source_span: The most common places for one or more central nervous system (CNS) germ cell tumors to form is near the pineal gland and in an area of the brain that includes the pituitary gland and the tissue just above it.

statement: There are two main types of childhood CNS germ cell tumors: germinomas and nongerminomas.
source_span: Germinomas    Nongerminomas

statement: Germinomas are the most common type of CNS germ cell tumor and have a good prognosis.
source_span: Germinomas are the most common type of CNS germ cell tumor and have a good prognosis.

statement: Choriocarcinomas, a type of nongerminoma, make the hormone beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG).
source_span: Choriocarcinomas make the hormone beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (-hCG).

statement: Yolk sac tumors, a type of nongerminoma, make the hormone alpha-fetoprotein (AFP).
source_span: Yolk sac tumors make the hormone alpha-fetoprotein (AFP).

statement: Embryonal carcinomas, a type of nongerminoma, do not make hormones.
source_span: Embryonal carcinomas do not make hormones.

statement: The cause of most childhood CNS germ cell tumors is not known.
source_span: The cause of most childhood CNS germ cell tumors is not known.

statement: Signs and symptoms of childhood CNS germ cell tumors include unusual thirst, frequent urination, early puberty, or vision changes.
source_span: Signs and symptoms of childhood CNS germ cell tumors include unusual thirst, frequent urination, early puberty, or vision changes.

statement: There is no standard staging system for childhood CNS germ cell tumors.
source_span: There is no standard staging system for childhood central nervous system (CNS) germ cell tumors.

statement: Childhood CNS germ cell tumors rarely spread outside of the brain and spinal cord.
source_span: Childhood central nervous system (CNS) germ cell tumors rarely spread outside of the brain and spinal cord.

statement: Childhood craniopharyngiomas are rare, benign tumors usually found near the pituitary gland and the hypothalamus.
source_span: Childhood craniopharyngiomas are rare tumors usually found near the pituitary gland (a pea-sized organ at the bottom of the brain that controls other glands) and the hypothalamus

statement: There are no known risk factors for childhood craniopharyngioma.
source_span: There are no known risk factors for childhood craniopharyngioma.

statement: Craniopharyngiomas are rare in children younger than 2 years of age and are most often diagnosed in children aged 5 to 14 years.
source_span: Craniopharyngiomas are rare in children younger than 2 years of age and are most often diagnosed in children aged 5 to 14 years.

statement: Craniopharyngiomas are usually part solid mass and part fluid-filled cyst.
source_span: Craniopharyngiomas are usually part solid mass and part fluid -filled cyst.

statement: Craniopharyngiomas are benign and do not spread to other parts of the brain or to other parts of the body.
source_span: They are benign (not cancer) and do not spread to other parts of the brain or to other parts of the body.

statement: Signs of childhood craniopharyngioma include vision changes and slow growth.
source_span: Signs of childhood craniopharyngioma include vision changes and slow growth.

statement: Blood hormone studies for craniopharyngioma diagnosis may check for unusual levels of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) or adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), both made by the pituitary gland.
source_span: the blood may be checked for unusual levels of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) or adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH). TSH and ACTH are made by the pituitary gland in the brain.

statement: Three types of biopsy procedures may be used to sample craniopharyngioma tissue: open biopsy, computer-guided needle biopsy, and transsphenoidal biopsy.
source_span: Open biopsy: A hollow needle is inserted through a hole in the skull into the brain.    - Computer-guided needle biopsy... - Transsphenoidal biopsy: Instruments are inserted through the nose and sphenoid bone

statement: Childhood craniopharyngiomas are diagnosed and may be removed in the same surgery.
source_span: Childhood craniopharyngiomas are diagnosed and may be removed in the same surgery.

statement: Childhood ependymoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the brain and spinal cord.
source_span: Childhood ependymoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the brain and spinal cord.

statement: Ependymomas form from ependymal cells that line the ventricles and passageways in the brain and spinal cord, and these cells make cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).
source_span: Ependymomas form from ependymal cells that line the ventricles and passageways in the brain and the spinal cord. Ependymal cells make cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

statement: The WHO groups ependymal tumors into five main subtypes: Subependymoma (Grade I), Myxopapillary ependymoma (Grade I), Ependymoma (Grade II), RELA fusion-positive ependymoma (Grade II or III), and Anaplastic ependymoma (Grade III).
source_span: The World Health Organization (WHO) groups ependymal tumors into five main subtypes:         - Subependymoma (WHO Grade I).    - Myxopapillary ependymoma (WHO Grade I).    - Ependymoma (WHO Grade II).    -  RELA fusionpositive ependymoma (WHO Grade II or Grade III with change in the RELA gene).    - Anaplastic ependymoma (WHO Grade III).

statement: Most ependymomas form in the fourth ventricle and affect the cerebellum and the brain stem.
source_span: Most ependymomas form in the fourth ventricle and affect the cerebellum and the brain stem.

statement: The cause of most childhood brain tumors is unknown.
source_span: The cause of most childhood brain tumors is unknown.

statement: Signs and symptoms of childhood ependymoma depend on the child's age and where the tumor has formed.
source_span: Signs and symptoms depend on the following:         - The child's age.    - Where the tumor has formed.

statement: A lumbar puncture collects cerebrospinal fluid that is checked for tumor cells, with higher than normal protein or lower than normal glucose potentially signaling a tumor.
source_span: A higher than normal amount of protein or lower than normal amount of glucose may be a sign of a tumor.

statement: Childhood ependymoma is diagnosed and removed in surgery.
source_span: Childhood ependymoma is diagnosed and removed in surgery.

statement: Adult primary liver cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the liver.
source_span: Adult primary liver cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the liver.

statement: The two types of adult primary liver cancer are hepatocellular carcinoma and cholangiocarcinoma (bile duct cancer).
source_span: The two types of adult primary liver cancer are: - Hepatocellular carcinoma. - Cholangiocarcinoma (bile duct cancer).

statement: Hepatocellular carcinoma, the most common type of adult primary liver cancer, is the third leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide.
source_span: The most common type of adult primary liver cancer is hepatocellular carcinoma. This type of liver cancer is the third leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide.

statement: The liver has four lobes and fills the upper right side of the abdomen inside the rib cage.
source_span: It has four lobes and fills the upper right side of the abdomen inside the rib cage.

statement: Having both hepatitis B and hepatitis C increases the risk of adult primary liver cancer even more than having just one.
source_span: Having both hepatitis B and hepatitis C increases the risk even more.

statement: Hemochromatosis causes the body to store more iron than it needs, with extra iron stored in the liver, heart, and pancreas.
source_span: Having hemochromatosis, a condition in which the body takes up and stores more iron than it needs. The extra iron is stored in the liver, heart, and pancreas

statement: Eating foods tainted with aflatoxin, a poison from a fungus that grows on improperly stored grains and nuts, is a risk factor for adult primary liver cancer.
source_span: Eating foods tainted with aflatoxin (poison from a fungus that can grow on foods, such as grains and nuts, that have not been stored properly).

statement: An increased level of alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) in the blood may indicate liver cancer, but AFP is sometimes normal even when liver cancer is present.
source_span: An increased level of alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) in the blood may be a sign of liver cancer...Sometimes the AFP level is normal even when there is liver cancer.

statement: Triple-phase CT takes images at three different times after dye injection to get the best picture of abnormal areas in the liver.
source_span: Images may be taken at three different times after the dye is injected, to get the best picture of abnormal areas in the liver. This is called triple-phase CT.

statement: Bile duct cancer is a rare disease in which malignant cells form in the bile ducts and is also called cholangiocarcinoma.
source_span: Bile duct cancer is a rare disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the bile ducts...Bile duct cancer is also called cholangiocarcinoma.

statement: There are two types of bile duct cancer: intrahepatic bile duct cancer and extrahepatic bile duct cancer.
source_span: There are two types of bile duct cancer: - Intrahepatic bile duct cancer...- Extrahepatic bile duct cancer

statement: Perihilar bile duct cancer, found in the hilum region, is also called a Klatskin tumor or perihilar cholangiocarcinoma.
source_span: Perihilar bile duct cancer is also called a Klatskin tumor or perihilar cholangiocarcinoma.

statement: The distal region is made up of the common bile duct, which passes through the pancreas and ends in the small intestine.
source_span: The distal region is made up of the common bile duct which passes through the pancreas and ends in the small intestine.

statement: Risk factors for bile duct cancer include primary sclerosing cholangitis, chronic ulcerative colitis, cysts in the bile ducts, and infection with a Chinese liver fluke parasite.
source_span: Risk factors for bile duct cancer include the following conditions: - Primary sclerosing cholangitis...- Chronic ulcerative colitis. - Cysts in the bile ducts...- Infection with a Chinese liver fluke parasite.

statement: Signs of bile duct cancer include jaundice, abdominal pain, dark urine, clay colored stool, fever, itchy skin, nausea and vomiting, and unexplained weight loss.
source_span: Signs of bile duct cancer include jaundice and pain in the abdomen...Dark urine. Clay colored stool...Itchy skin.

statement: Higher than normal levels of carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and CA 19-9 tumor markers may indicate bile duct cancer.
source_span: Higher than normal levels of carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and CA 19-9 may mean there is bile duct cancer.

statement: Liver function tests for bile duct cancer measure the amounts of bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase released into the blood by the liver.
source_span: A procedure in which a blood sample is checked to measure the amounts of bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase released into the blood by the liver.

statement: Childhood liver cancer is a disease in which malignant cells form in the tissues of the liver, and it is rare in children and adolescents.
source_span: Childhood liver cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the liver...Liver cancer is rare in children and adolescents.

statement: Hepatoblastoma is the most common type of childhood liver cancer and usually affects children younger than 3 years of age.
source_span: Hepatoblastoma is the most common type of childhood liver cancer. It usually affects children younger than 3 years of age.

statement: Hepatocellular carcinoma in children usually affects older children and adolescents and is more common in areas of Asia with high rates of hepatitis infection than in the U.S.
source_span: Hepatocellular carcinoma usually affects older children and adolescents. It is more common in areas of Asia that have high rates of hepatitis infection than in the U.S.

statement: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver usually occurs in children between 5 and 10 years of age and often spreads throughout the liver and/or to the lungs.
source_span: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver: This type of liver cancer usually occurs in children between 5 and 10 years of age. It often spreads all through the liver and/or to the lungs.

statement: Infantile choriocarcinoma of the liver is a very rare tumor that starts in the placenta and spreads to the fetus, usually found during the first few months of life.
source_span: Infantile choriocarcinoma of the liver is a very rare tumor that starts in the placenta and spreads to the fetus. The tumor is usually found during the first few months of life.

statement: Risk factors for hepatoblastoma include Aicardi syndrome, Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, familial adenomatous polyposis, glycogen storage disease, very low birth weight, Simpson-Golabi-Behmel syndrome, and Trisomy 18.
source_span: Risk factors for hepatoblastoma include the following syndromes or conditions: - Aicardi syndrome. - Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. - Familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP). - Glycogen storage disease. - A very low weight at birth. - Simpson-Golabi-Behmel syndrome. - Certain genetic changes, such as Trisomy 18.

statement: Risk factors for hepatocellular carcinoma in children include Alagille syndrome, glycogen storage disease, hepatitis B virus infection passed from mother to child at birth, progressive familial intrahepatic disease, and tyrosinemia.
source_span: Risk factors for hepatocellular carcinoma include the following syndromes or conditions: - Alagille syndrome. - Glycogen storage disease. - Hepatitis B virus infection that was passed from mother to child at birth. - Progressive familial intrahepatic disease. - Tyrosinemia.

statement: Some patients with tyrosinemia or progressive familial intrahepatic disease will have a liver transplant before there are signs or symptoms of cancer.
source_span: Some patients with tyrosinemia or progressive familial intrahepatic disease will have a liver transplant before there are signs or symptoms of cancer.

statement: The blood of children with liver cancer may have increased amounts of beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) or alpha-fetoprotein (AFP).
source_span: The blood of children who have liver cancer may have increased amounts of a hormone called beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (-hCG) or a protein called alpha-fetoprotein (AFP).
