statement: A pregnancy before age 20 or after age 35 is a risk factor for GTD.
source_span: Being pregnant when you are younger than 20 or older than 35 years of age.

statement: Choriocarcinoma is more likely to form in women who have had a molar pregnancy, especially with a complete hydatidiform mole, a normal pregnancy, a tubal pregnancy, or a miscarriage.
source_span: A choriocarcinoma is more likely to form in women who have had any of the following: Molar pregnancy, especially with a complete hydatidiform mole. Normal pregnancy. Tubal pregnancy... Miscarriage.

statement: A placental-site trophoblastic tumor (PSTT) grows very slowly, and signs or symptoms may appear months or years after a normal pregnancy.
source_span: A PSTT grows very slowly and signs or symptoms may appear months or years after a normal pregnancy.

statement: Signs of GTD include abnormal vaginal bleeding and a uterus that is larger than normal.
source_span: Signs of GTD include abnormal vaginal bleeding and a uterus that is larger than normal.

statement: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare cancer that begins in LCH cells, a type of dendritic cell which fights infection.
source_span: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare cancer that begins in LCH cells (a type of dendritic cell which fights infection).

statement: LCH may occur at any age but is most common in young children.
source_span: LCH may occur at any age, but is most common in young children.

statement: Mutations of the BRAF gene are among the mutations that occur in LCH cells and may make them grow and multiply quickly.
source_span: These include mutations of the BRAF gene. These changes may make the LCH cells grow and multiply quickly.

statement: Having a parent who was exposed to certain chemicals such as benzene is a risk factor for LCH.
source_span: Having a parent who was exposed to certain chemicals such as benzene.

statement: Having a parent who was exposed to metal, granite, or wood dust in the workplace is a risk factor for LCH.
source_span: Having a parent who was exposed to metal, granite, or wood dust in the workplace.

statement: Being Hispanic is listed as a risk factor for LCH.
source_span: Being Hispanic.

statement: Children with LCH lesions in bones around the ears or eyes have a high risk for diabetes insipidus and other central nervous system disease.
source_span: Children with LCH lesions in bones around the ears or eyes have a high risk for diabetes insipidus and other central nervous system disease.

statement: Diabetes insipidus, a symptom of LCH affecting the pituitary gland, can cause a strong thirst and frequent urination.
source_span: Diabetes insipidus. This can cause a strong thirst and frequent urination.

statement: Superior vena cava syndrome from LCH affecting the lymph nodes or thymus can cause coughing, trouble breathing, and swelling of the face, neck, and upper arms.
source_span: Superior vena cava syndrome. This can cause coughing, trouble breathing, and swelling of the face, neck, and upper arms.

statement: Hypopharyngeal cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the hypopharynx.
source_span: Hypopharyngeal cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the hypopharynx.

statement: The hypopharynx is the bottom part of the pharynx (throat).
source_span: The hypopharynx is the bottom part of the pharynx (throat).

statement: The pharynx is a hollow tube about 5 inches long that starts behind the nose, goes down the neck, and ends at the top of the trachea and esophagus.
source_span: The pharynx is a hollow tube about 5 inches long that starts behind the nose, goes down the neck, and ends at the top of the trachea (windpipe) and esophagus

statement: The hypopharynx has 3 different areas, and cancer may be found in 1 or more of these areas.
source_span: The hypopharynx has 3 different areas. Cancer may be found in 1 or more of these areas.

statement: Most hypopharyngeal cancers form in squamous cells, the thin, flat cells lining the inside of the hypopharynx.
source_span: Most hypopharyngeal cancers form in squamous cells, the thin, flat cells lining the inside of the hypopharynx.

statement: Hypopharyngeal cancer is a type of head and neck cancer.
source_span: Hypopharyngeal cancer is a type of head and neck cancer.

statement: Risk factors for hypopharyngeal cancer include smoking tobacco, chewing tobacco, heavy alcohol use, a diet without enough nutrients, and having Plummer-Vinson syndrome.
source_span: Risk factors include the following: - Smoking tobacco. - Chewing tobacco. - Heavy alcohol use. - Eating a diet without enough nutrients. - Having Plummer-Vinson syndrome.

statement: Signs and symptoms of hypopharyngeal cancer include a sore throat that does not go away, ear pain, a lump in the neck, painful or difficult swallowing, and a change in voice.
source_span: A sore throat that does not go away. - Ear pain. - A lump in the neck. - Painful or difficult swallowing. - A change in voice.

statement: Hypopharyngeal cancer is usually detected in later stages because early signs and symptoms rarely occur.
source_span: Hypopharyngeal cancer is usually detected in later stages because early signs and symptoms rarely occur.

statement: Patients who have had hypopharyngeal cancer are at an increased risk of developing a second cancer in the head or neck.
source_span: Patients who have had hypopharyngeal cancer are at an increased risk of developing a second cancer in the head or neck.

statement: Prognosis for hypopharyngeal cancer depends on the stage of the cancer, the patient's age, gender, and general health, the location of the cancer, and whether the patient smokes during radiation therapy.
source_span: The stage of the cancer... The patient's age, gender, and general health. The location of the cancer. Whether the patient smokes during radiation therapy.

statement: The stages of hypopharyngeal cancer are Stage 0 (Carcinoma in Situ), Stage I, Stage II, Stage III, and Stage IV.
source_span: Stage 0 (Carcinoma in Situ) - Stage I - Stage II - Stage III - Stage IV

statement: Oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer are diseases in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the mouth and throat.
source_span: Oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer are diseases in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the mouth and throat.

statement: Oral cavity cancer forms in the front two thirds of the tongue, the gingiva (gums), the buccal mucosa, the floor of the mouth, the hard palate, and the retromolar trigone.
source_span: Oral cavity cancer forms in any of these tissues of the oral cavity: The front two thirds of the tongue. The gingiva (gums). The buccal mucosa... The floor (bottom) of the mouth... The hard palate... The retromolar trigone

statement: Oropharyngeal cancer forms in the middle part of the pharynx behind the mouth, the back one third of the tongue, the soft palate, the side and back walls of the throat, and the tonsils.
source_span: Oropharyngeal cancer forms in any of these tissues of the oropharynx: The middle part of the pharynx (throat) behind the mouth. The back one third of the tongue. The soft palate... The side and back walls of the throat. The tonsils.

statement: Most oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancers start in squamous cells and are called squamous cell carcinoma.
source_span: Most oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancers start in squamous cells, the thin, flat cells that line the lips, oral cavity, and oropharynx. Cancer that forms in squamous cells is called squamous cell carcinoma.

statement: Over the past ten years, the number of new cases and deaths from oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer slightly increased in white men and women and slightly decreased among black men and women.
source_span: Over the past ten years, the number of new cases and deaths from oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer slightly increased in white men and women. The number slightly decreased among black men and women.

statement: Oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer is more common in men than in women.
source_span: Oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer is more common in men than in women.

statement: Oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer occurs most often in adults aged 55 to 64 years.
source_span: Although oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer may occur in adults of any age, it occurs most often in those aged 55 to 64 years.

statement: France, Brazil, and parts of Asia have much higher rates of oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer than most other countries.
source_span: France, Brazil, and parts of Asia have much higher rates of oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer than most other countries.

statement: The number of new cases of oropharyngeal cancer caused by certain HPV types has increased, and HPV 16 is often passed from person to person during sexual activity.
source_span: The number of new cases of oropharyngeal cancer caused by certain types of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection has increased. One kind of HPV, called HPV 16, is often passed from one person to another during sexual activity.

statement: Laryngeal cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the larynx.
source_span: Laryngeal cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the larynx.

statement: The larynx is a part of the throat located between the base of the tongue and the trachea, and contains the vocal cords.
source_span: The larynx is a part of the throat, between the base of the tongue and the trachea. The larynx contains the vocal cords, which vibrate and make sound when air is directed against them.

statement: The larynx has three main parts: the supraglottis, the glottis, and the subglottis.
source_span: There are three main parts of the larynx: Supraglottis... Glottis... Subglottis

statement: Most laryngeal cancers form in squamous cells, the thin, flat cells lining the inside of the larynx.
source_span: Most laryngeal cancers form in squamous cells, the thin, flat cells lining the inside of the larynx.

statement: Laryngeal cancer is a type of head and neck cancer.
source_span: Laryngeal cancer is a type of head and neck cancer.

statement: Use of tobacco products and drinking too much alcohol can affect the risk of laryngeal cancer.
source_span: Use of tobacco products and drinking too much alcohol can affect the risk of laryngeal cancer.

statement: Signs and symptoms of laryngeal cancer include a sore throat or cough that does not go away, trouble or pain when swallowing, ear pain, a lump in the neck or throat, and a change or hoarseness in the voice.
source_span: A sore throat or cough that does not go away. Trouble or pain when swallowing. Ear pain. A lump in the neck or throat. A change or hoarseness in the voice.

statement: Prognosis for laryngeal cancer depends on the stage of the disease, the location and size of the tumor, the grade of the tumor, and the patient's age, gender, and general health, including whether the patient is anemic.
source_span: The stage of the disease. The location and size of the tumor. The grade of the tumor. The patient's age, gender, and general health, including whether the patient is anemic.

statement: Smoking tobacco and drinking alcohol decrease the effectiveness of treatment for laryngeal cancer.
source_span: Smoking tobacco and drinking alcohol decrease the effectiveness of treatment for laryngeal cancer.

statement: Patients with laryngeal cancer who continue to smoke and drink are less likely to be cured and more likely to develop a second tumor.
source_span: Patients with laryngeal cancer who continue to smoke and drink are less likely to be cured and more likely to develop a second tumor.

statement: Lip and oral cavity cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the lips or mouth.
source_span: Lip and oral cavity cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the lips or mouth.

statement: The oral cavity includes the front two thirds of the tongue, the gingiva, the buccal mucosa, the floor of the mouth, the hard palate, and the retromolar trigone.
source_span: The oral cavity includes the following: - The front two thirds of the tongue. - The gingiva (gums). - The buccal mucosa (the lining of the inside of the cheeks). - The floor (bottom) of the mouth under the tongue. - The hard palate (the roof of the mouth). - The retromolar trigone (the small area behind the wisdom teeth).

statement: Most lip and oral cavity cancers start in squamous cells and are called squamous cell carcinomas.
source_span: Most lip and oral cavity cancers start in squamous cells, the thin, flat cells that line the lips and oral cavity. These are called squamous cell carcinomas.

statement: Squamous cell carcinoma usually develops in areas of leukoplakia, white patches of cells that do not rub off.
source_span: Squamous cell carcinoma usually develops in areas of leukoplakia (white patches of cells that do not rub off).

statement: Lip and oral cavity cancer is a type of head and neck cancer.
source_span: Lip and oral cavity cancer is a type of head and neck cancer.

statement: Risk factors for lip and oral cavity cancer include using tobacco products, heavy alcohol use, long-term exposure to natural or artificial sunlight, and being male.
source_span: Risk factors for lip and oral cavity cancer include the following: - Using tobacco products. - Heavy alcohol use. - Being exposed to natural sunlight or artificial sunlight (such as from tanning beds) over long periods of time. - Being male.

statement: Signs of lip and oral cavity cancer include a non-healing sore, a lump or thickening on the lips/gums/mouth, a white or red patch, bleeding, pain, numbness, voice change, loose teeth or ill-fitting dentures, trouble chewing/swallowing, jaw swelling, and sore throat.
source_span: Check with your doctor if you have any of the following: - A sore on the lip or in the mouth that does not heal. - A lump or thickening on the lips or gums or in the mouth. - A white or red patch on the gums, tongue, or lining of the mouth. - Bleeding, pain, or numbness in the lip or mouth. - Change in voice. - Loose teeth or dentures that no longer fit well. - Trouble chewing or swallowing or moving the tongue or jaw. - Swelling of jaw. - Sore throat or feeling that something is caught in the throat.

statement: Lip and oral cavity cancer may not have any symptoms and is sometimes found during a regular dental exam.
source_span: Lip and oral cavity cancer may not have any symptoms and is sometimes found during a regular dental exam.

statement: Tests used to diagnose lip and oral cavity cancer include physical exam, endoscopy, biopsy, exfoliative cytology, MRI, CT scan, barium swallow, PET scan, and bone scan.
source_span: The following tests and procedures may be used: - Physical exam of the lips and oral cavity ... - Endoscopy ... - Biopsy ... - Exfoliative cytology ... - MRI ... - CT scan ... - Barium swallow ... - PET scan ... - Bone scan

statement: A barium swallow, also called an upper GI series, involves the patient drinking a liquid containing barium that coats the esophagus before x-rays are taken.
source_span: This procedure is also called an upper GI series. ... The patient drinks a liquid that contains barium (a silver-white metallic compound). The liquid coats the esophagus and x-rays are taken.

statement: Prognosis for lip and oral cavity cancer depends on the stage of the cancer, where the tumor is located, and whether the cancer has spread to blood vessels.
source_span: Prognosis (chance of recovery) depends on the following: - The stage of the cancer. - Where the tumor is in the lip or oral cavity. - Whether the cancer has spread to blood vessels.

statement: For patients who smoke, the chance of recovery is better if they stop smoking before beginning radiation therapy.
source_span: For patients who smoke, the chance of recovery is better if they stop smoking before beginning radiation therapy.

statement: Metastatic squamous neck cancer with occult primary is a disease in which squamous cell cancer spreads to lymph nodes in the neck and the location where the cancer first formed is unknown.
source_span: Metastatic squamous neck cancer with occult primary is a disease in which squamous cell cancer spreads to lymph nodes in the neck and it is not known where the cancer first formed in the body.

statement: Some organs with squamous cells, where cancer can begin, are the esophagus, lungs, kidneys, and uterus.
source_span: Some organs with squamous cells are the esophagus, lungs, kidneys, and uterus.

statement: When squamous cell cancer spreads to lymph nodes in the neck or around the collarbone, it is called metastatic squamous neck cancer.
source_span: When squamous cell cancer spreads to lymph nodes in the neck or around the collarbone, it is called metastatic squamous neck cancer.

statement: Treatment for metastatic cancer is the same as treatment for the primary tumor.
source_span: treatment for metastatic cancer is the same as treatment for the primary tumor

statement: When tests cannot find a primary tumor, it is called an occult (hidden) primary tumor, and in many cases the primary tumor is never found.
source_span: When tests cannot find a primary tumor, it is called an occult (hidden) primary tumor. In many cases, the primary tumor is never found.

statement: Signs and symptoms of metastatic squamous neck cancer with occult primary include a lump or pain in the neck or throat that doesn't go away.
source_span: Check with your doctor if you have a lump or pain in your neck or throat that doesn't go away.

statement: Three types of biopsy that may be done are fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy, core needle biopsy, and excisional biopsy.
source_span: Three types of biopsy may be done: - Fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy : The removal of tissue or fluid using a thin needle. - Core needle biopsy : The removal of tissue using a wide needle. - Excisional biopsy : The removal of an entire lump of tissue.

statement: A tonsillectomy, surgery to remove both tonsils, is one procedure used to remove samples of cells or tissue for diagnosis.
source_span: Tonsillectomy: Surgery to remove both tonsils.

statement: A whole body PET scan and a CT scan are done at the same time to look for where the cancer first formed.
source_span: A whole body PET scan and a CT scan are done at the same time to look for where the cancer first formed.

statement: A diagnosis of occult primary tumor is made if the primary tumor is not found during testing or treatment.
source_span: A diagnosis of occult primary tumor is made if the primary tumor is not found during testing or treatment.

statement: Laboratory tests used to study tissue samples include immunohistochemistry, light and electron microscopy, and an Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and human papillomavirus (HPV) test.
source_span: One or more of the following laboratory tests may be done to study the tissue samples: - Immunohistochemistry ... - Light and electron microscopy ... - Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and human papillomavirus (HPV) test

statement: Nasopharyngeal cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the nasopharynx.
source_span: Nasopharyngeal cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the nasopharynx.

statement: The pharynx is a hollow tube about 5 inches long that starts behind the nose and ends at the top of the trachea and esophagus.
source_span: The pharynx is a hollow tube about 5 inches long that starts behind the nose and ends at the top of the trachea (windpipe) and esophagus (the tube that goes from the throat to the stomach).

statement: Nasopharyngeal cancer most commonly starts in the squamous cells that line the nasopharynx.
source_span: Nasopharyngeal cancer most commonly starts in the squamous cells that line the nasopharynx.

statement: Nasopharyngeal cancer is a type of head and neck cancer.
source_span: Nasopharyngeal cancer is a type of head and neck cancer.

statement: Risk factors for nasopharyngeal cancer include having Chinese or Asian ancestry, being exposed to the Epstein-Barr virus, and drinking large amounts of alcohol.
source_span: Risk factors for nasopharyngeal cancer include the following: - Having Chinese or Asian ancestry. - Being exposed to the Epstein-Barr virus... - Drinking large amounts of alcohol.

statement: The Epstein-Barr virus has been associated with certain cancers, including nasopharyngeal cancer and some lymphomas.
source_span: The Epstein-Barr virus has been associated with certain cancers, including nasopharyngeal cancer and some lymphomas.

statement: Signs of nasopharyngeal cancer include a lump in the nose or neck, sore throat, trouble breathing or speaking, nosebleeds, trouble hearing, pain or ringing in the ear, and headaches.
source_span: Check with your doctor if you have any of the following: - A lump in the nose or neck. - A sore throat. - Trouble breathing or speaking. - Nosebleeds. - Trouble hearing. - Pain or ringing in the ear. - Headaches.

statement: PET scans may be used to find nasopharyngeal cancers that have spread to the bone.
source_span: PET scans may be used to find nasopharyngeal cancers that have spread to the bone.

statement: An Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) test is a blood test that checks for antibodies to the Epstein-Barr virus and DNA markers of the virus.
source_span: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) test: A blood test to check for antibodies to the Epstein-Barr virus and DNA markers of the Epstein-Barr virus.

statement: A hearing test checks whether soft and loud sounds and low- and high-pitched sounds can be heard, with each ear checked separately.
source_span: Hearing test: A procedure to check whether soft and loud sounds and low- and high-pitched sounds can be heard. Each ear is checked separately.

statement: Oropharyngeal cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the oropharynx.
source_span: Oropharyngeal cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the oropharynx.

statement: The oropharynx is the middle part of the pharynx (throat), located behind the mouth.
source_span: The oropharynx is the middle part of the pharynx (throat), behind the mouth.

statement: The pharynx is a hollow tube about 5 inches long that starts behind the nose and ends where the trachea and esophagus begin.
source_span: The pharynx is a hollow tube about 5 inches long that starts behind the nose and ends where the trachea (windpipe) and esophagus (tube from the throat to the stomach) begin.

statement: The oropharynx includes the soft palate, the side and back walls of the throat, the tonsils, and the back one-third of the tongue.
source_span: The oropharynx includes the following: - Soft palate. - Side and back walls of the throat. - Tonsils. - Back one-third of the tongue.

statement: Most oropharyngeal cancers are squamous cell carcinomas.
source_span: Most oropharyngeal cancers are squamous cell carcinomas.

statement: A history of smoking cigarettes for more than 10 pack years and other tobacco use is a risk factor for oropharyngeal cancer.
source_span: A history of smoking cigarettes for more than 10 pack years and other tobacco use.

statement: Being infected with human papillomavirus (HPV), especially HPV type 16, is a risk factor for oropharyngeal cancer.
source_span: Being infected with human papillomavirus (HPV), especially HPV type 16.

statement: Heavy alcohol use is a risk factor for oropharyngeal cancer.
source_span: Heavy alcohol use.

statement: Chewing betel quid, a stimulant commonly used in parts of Asia, is a risk factor for oropharyngeal cancer.
source_span: Chewing betel quid, a stimulant commonly used in parts of Asia.

statement: Signs and symptoms of oropharyngeal cancer include a lump in the neck and a sore throat.
source_span: Signs and symptoms of oropharyngeal cancer include a lump in the neck and a sore throat.

statement: Other symptoms of oropharyngeal cancer include trouble swallowing, trouble opening the mouth fully, trouble moving the tongue, unexplained weight loss, ear pain, and coughing up blood.
source_span: Trouble swallowing.    - Trouble opening the mouth fully.    - Trouble moving the tongue.    - Weight loss for no known reason.    - Ear pain.  ... - Coughing up blood.

statement: A PET-CT scan combines pictures from a PET scan and a CT scan, both done at the same time with the same machine, to give more detailed pictures than either scan alone.
source_span: A procedure that combines the pictures from a positron emission tomography (PET) scan and a computed tomography (CT) scan. The PET and CT scans are done at the same time with the same machine.

statement: A fine-needle biopsy, using a thin needle, is usually done to remove a tissue sample for diagnosing oropharyngeal cancer.
source_span: A fine-needle biopsy is usually done to remove a sample of tissue using a thin needle.

statement: Paranasal sinus and nasal cavity cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the paranasal sinuses and nasal cavity.
source_span: Paranasal sinus and nasal cavity cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the paranasal sinuses and nasal cavity.

statement: The frontal sinuses are located in the lower forehead above the nose.
source_span: The frontal sinuses are in the lower forehead above the nose.

statement: The maxillary sinuses are located in the cheekbones on either side of the nose.
source_span: The maxillary sinuses are in the cheekbones on either side of the nose.

statement: The ethmoid sinuses are located beside the upper nose, between the eyes.
source_span: The ethmoid sinuses are beside the upper nose, between the eyes.

statement: The sphenoid sinuses are located behind the nose, in the center of the skull.
source_span: The sphenoid sinuses are behind the nose, in the center of the skull.

statement: The most common type of paranasal sinus and nasal cavity cancer is squamous cell carcinoma.
source_span: The most common type of paranasal sinus and nasal cavity cancer is squamous cell carcinoma.

statement: Being exposed to certain workplace chemicals or dust, such as in furniture-making, sawmill work, woodworking, shoemaking, metal-plating, or flour mill/bakery work, is a risk factor for paranasal sinus and nasal cavity cancer.
source_span: Being exposed to certain workplace chemicals or dust, such as those found in the following jobs: - Furniture-making.- Sawmill work.- Woodworking (carpentry).- Shoemaking.- Metal-plating.- Flour mill or bakery work.

statement: Being male and older than 40 years is a risk factor for paranasal sinus and nasal cavity cancer.
source_span: Being male and older than 40 years.

statement: Signs of paranasal sinus and nasal cavity cancer include sinus problems and nosebleeds.
source_span: Signs of paranasal sinus and nasal cavity cancer include sinus problems and nosebleeds.

statement: There are three types of biopsy used to diagnose paranasal sinus and nasal cavity cancer: fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy, incisional biopsy, and excisional biopsy.
source_span: There are three types of biopsy: - Fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy : The removal of tissue or fluid using a thin needle.- Incisional biopsy... - Excisional biopsy

statement: Inverting papilloma is a benign tumor that forms inside the nose, and a small number of these change into cancer.
source_span: Inverting papilloma: Benign tumors that form inside the nose. A small number of these change into cancer.

statement: Salivary gland cancer is a rare disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the salivary glands.
source_span: Salivary gland cancer is a rare disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the salivary glands.

statement: There are 3 pairs of major salivary glands: parotid glands, sublingual glands, and submandibular glands.
source_span: There are 3 pairs of major salivary glands: - Parotid glands... - Sublingual glands... - Submandibular glands

statement: The parotid glands are the largest salivary glands, found in front of and just below each ear, and most major salivary gland tumors begin in this gland.
source_span: Parotid glands: These are the largest salivary glands and are found in front of and just below each ear. Most major salivary gland tumors begin in this gland.

statement: More than half of all salivary gland tumors are benign (not cancerous) and do not spread to other tissues.
source_span: More than half of all salivary gland tumors are benign (not cancerous) and do not spread to other tissues.

statement: Risk factors for salivary gland cancer include older age, treatment with radiation therapy to the head and neck, and being exposed to certain substances at work.
source_span: risk factors include the following: - Older age.    - Treatment with radiation therapy to the head and neck.    - Being exposed to certain substances at work.

statement: Signs of salivary gland cancer include a lump or trouble swallowing.
source_span: Signs of salivary gland cancer include a lump or trouble swallowing.

statement: Fine needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy is the most common type of biopsy used for salivary gland cancer.
source_span: An FNA is the most common type of biopsy used for salivary gland cancer.

statement: The stages used for major salivary gland cancers are Stage I, Stage II, Stage III, and Stage IV.
source_span: The following stages are used for major salivary gland cancers: - Stage I - Stage II - Stage III - Stage IV

statement: Most small (minor) salivary gland tumors begin in the palate (roof of the mouth).
source_span: Most small salivary gland tumors begin in the palate (roof of the mouth).

Using tobacco is the most common cause of oral cavity cancer and oropharyngeal cancer.
source_span: Using tobacco is the most common cause of oral cavity cancer and oropharyngeal cancer.

statement: The risk of oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer is about 5 to 10 times higher for current smokers than for people who have never smoked.
source_span: The risk of these cancers is about 5 to 10 times higher for current smokers than for people who have never smoked.

statement: For cigarette smokers, the risk of oral cavity cancer and oropharyngeal cancer increases with the number of cigarettes smoked per day.
source_span: the risk of oral cavity cancer and oropharyngeal cancer increases with the number of cigarettes smoked per day

statement: The risk of oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer is about twice as high in people who have 3 to 4 alcoholic drinks per day compared with people who don't drink.
source_span: about twice as high in people who have 3 to 4 alcoholic drinks per day...compared with those who don't drink alcohol

statement: The risk of oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer is 5 times higher in people who have 5 or more alcoholic drinks per day compared with people who don't drink.
source_span: 5 times higher in people who have 5 or more alcoholic drinks per day compared with those who don't drink alcohol

statement: The risk of oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer is 2 to 3 times higher in people who use both tobacco and alcohol than in people who use only tobacco or only alcohol.
source_span: The risk of oral cavity cancer and oropharyngeal cancer is 2 to 3 times higher in people who use both tobacco and alcohol than it is in people who use only tobacco or only alcohol.

statement: The risk of oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer is about 35 times higher in people who smoke 2 or more packs of cigarettes per day and have more than 4 alcoholic drinks per day than in people who have never smoked or consumed alcohol.
source_span: about 35 times higher in people who smoke 2 or more packs of cigarettes per day and have more than 4 alcoholic drinks per day than it is in people who have never smoked cigarettes or consumed alcohol

statement: Betel quid contains areca nut, which is a cancer-causing substance.
source_span: Betel quid contains areca nut, which is a cancer-causing substance.

statement: The risk for oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer is higher when chewing gutka than when chewing betel quid alone.
source_span: The risk for oral cavity cancer and oropharyngeal cancer is higher when chewing gutka than when chewing betel quid alone.

statement: Betel quid and gutka chewing is common in many countries in South Asia and Southeast Asia, including China and India.
source_span: Betel quid and gutka chewing is common in many countries in South Asia and Southeast Asia, including China and India.

statement: Being infected with certain types of HPV, especially HPV type 16, increases the risk of oropharyngeal cancer.
source_span: Being infected with certain types of HPV, especially HPV type 16, increases the risk of oropharyngeal cancer.

statement: The risk of oropharyngeal cancer is about 15 times higher in people who have oral HPV 16 infection compared with people who do not have it.
source_span: The risk of oropharyngeal cancer is about 15 times higher in people who have oral HPV 16 infection compared with people who do not have oral HPV 16 infection.

statement: When people stop smoking cigarettes, their risk of oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer decreases by one half (50%) within 5 years.
source_span: their risk of oral cavity cancer and oropharyngeal cancer decreases by one half (50%) within 5 years

statement: Within 20 years of quitting smoking, a person's risk of oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancer is the same as for a person who never smoked cigarettes.
source_span: Within 20 years of quitting, their risk of oral cavity cancer and oropharyngeal cancer is the same as for a person who never smoked cigarettes.

statement: A personal history of head and neck cancer increases the risk of oral cavity cancer and oropharyngeal cancer.
source_span: A personal history of head and neck cancer increases the risk of oral cavity cancer and oropharyngeal cancer.

statement: It has not been proven that stopping alcohol use will decrease the risk of oral cavity or oropharyngeal cancer.
source_span: It has not been proven that stopping alcohol use will decrease the risk of oral cavity cancer or oropharyngeal cancer.

statement: The pancreas is a gland about 6 inches long that is shaped like a thin pear lying on its side.
source_span: The pancreas is a gland about 6 inches long that is shaped like a thin pear lying on its side.

statement: About 95% of pancreatic cancers begin in exocrine cells.
source_span: About 95% of pancreatic cancers begin in exocrine cells.

statement: Risk factors for pancreatic cancer include smoking, being very overweight, having a personal history of diabetes or chronic pancreatitis, and having a family history of pancreatic cancer or pancreatitis.
source_span: Smoking.    - Being very overweight.    - Having a personal history of diabetes or chronic pancreatitis.    - Having a family history of pancreatic cancer or pancreatitis.

statement: Hereditary conditions linked to pancreatic cancer risk include MEN1 syndrome, hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer (Lynch syndrome), von Hippel-Lindau syndrome, Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome, and FAMMM syndrome.
source_span: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) syndrome...Hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer (HNPCC; Lynch syndrome)...von Hippel-Lindau syndrome...Peutz-Jeghers syndrome...Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome...Familial atypical multiple mole melanoma (FAMMM) syndrome

statement: Signs and symptoms of pancreatic cancer include jaundice, light-colored stools, dark urine, pain in the upper or middle abdomen and back, weight loss for no known reason, loss of appetite, and feeling very tired.
source_span: Jaundice...Light-colored stools.    - Dark urine.    - Pain in the upper or middle abdomen and back.     - Weight loss for no known reason.     - Loss of appetite.    - Feeling very tired.

statement: Pancreatic cancer is difficult to detect and diagnose early because there aren't noticeable signs or symptoms in the early stages, its symptoms resemble those of many other illnesses, and the pancreas is hidden behind other organs.
source_span: There arent any noticeable signs or symptoms in the early stages of pancreatic cancer...like the signs and symptoms of many other illnesses...The pancreas is hidden behind other organs such as the stomach, small intestine, liver, gallbladder, spleen, and bile ducts.

statement: A tumor marker test for pancreatic cancer measures substances such as CA 19-9 and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA).
source_span: A procedure in which a sample of blood, urine, or tissue is checked to measure the amounts of certain substances, such as CA 19-9, and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA)

statement: In a PET scan, a small amount of radioactive glucose is injected into a vein, and malignant tumor cells show up brighter because they take up more glucose than normal cells.
source_span: A small amount of radioactive glucose (sugar) is injected into a vein...Malignant tumor cells show up brighter in the picture because they are more active and take up more glucose than normal cells do.

statement: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors form in hormone-making cells (islet cells) of the pancreas.
source_span: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors form in hormone-making cells (islet cells) of the pancreas.

statement: Endocrine pancreas cells are also called islet cells or islets of Langerhans.
source_span: Endocrine pancreas cells are also called islet cells or islets of Langerhans.

statement: Pancreatic NETs are much less common than pancreatic exocrine tumors and have a better prognosis.
source_span: Pancreatic NETs are much less common than pancreatic exocrine tumors and have a better prognosis.

statement: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) syndrome is a risk factor for pancreatic NETs.
source_span: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) syndrome is a risk factor for pancreatic NETs.

statement: A gastrinoma forms in cells that make gastrin, usually in the head of the pancreas and sometimes in the small intestine, and most gastrinomas are malignant.
source_span: A gastrinoma usually forms in the head of the pancreas and sometimes forms in the small intestine. Most gastrinomas are malignant (cancer).

statement: When increased stomach acid, stomach ulcers, and diarrhea are caused by a gastrin-making tumor, it is called Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
source_span: When increased stomach acid, stomach ulcers, and diarrhea are caused by a tumor that makes gastrin, it is called Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.

statement: An insulinoma forms in cells that make insulin, forms in the head, body, or tail of the pancreas, and is usually benign and slow-growing.
source_span: Insulinomas are usually slow-growing tumors that rarely spread. An insulinoma forms in the head, body, or tail of the pancreas. Insulinomas are usually benign (not cancer).

statement: A glucagonoma forms in cells that make glucagon, usually forms in the tail of the pancreas, and most glucagonomas are malignant; too much glucagon causes hyperglycemia.
source_span: A glucagonoma usually forms in the tail of the pancreas. Most glucagonomas are malignant (cancer)...Too much glucagon causes hyperglycemia (high blood sugar).

statement: VIPomas make vasoactive intestinal peptide and may also be called Verner-Morrison syndrome.
source_span: VIPomas, which make vasoactive intestinal peptide. VIPoma may also be called Verner-Morrison syndrome.

statement: Somatostatinomas are tumors that make somatostatin.
source_span: Somatostatinomas, which make somatostatin.

statement: A higher than normal amount of chromogranin A together with normal amounts of hormones such as gastrin, insulin, and glucagon can be a sign of a non-functional pancreatic NET.
source_span: A higher than normal amount of chromogranin A and normal amounts of hormones such as gastrin, insulin, and glucagon can be a sign of a non-functional pancreatic NET.

statement: Renal cell cancer (also called kidney cancer or renal adenocarcinoma) is a disease in which malignant cancer cells are found in the lining of tubules in the kidney.
source_span: Renal cell cancer (also called kidney cancer or renal adenocarcinoma) is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells are found in the lining of tubules (very small tubes) in the kidney.

statement: There are 2 kidneys, one on each side of the backbone, above the waist.
source_span: There are 2 kidneys, one on each side of the backbone, above the waist.

statement: Smoking and misuse of certain pain medicines can affect the risk of renal cell cancer.
source_span: Smoking and misuse of certain pain medicines can affect the risk of renal cell cancer.

statement: Signs of renal cell cancer include blood in the urine and a lump in the abdomen.
source_span: Signs of renal cell cancer include blood in the urine and a lump in the abdomen.

statement: In stage I, the tumor is 7 centimeters or smaller and is found only in the kidney.
source_span: In stage I, the tumor is 7 centimeters or smaller and is found only in the kidney.

statement: In stage II, the tumor is larger than 7 centimeters and is found only in the kidney.
source_span: In stage II, the tumor is larger than 7 centimeters and is found only in the kidney.

statement: In stage III, the tumor is any size with cancer in the kidney and 1 or more nearby lymph nodes, or cancer is found in the main blood vessels of the kidney or the fatty tissue around it.
source_span: the tumor is any size and cancer is found only in the kidney and in 1 or more nearby lymph nodes; or cancer is found in the main blood vessels of the kidney or in the layer of fatty tissue around the kidney

statement: In stage IV, cancer has spread beyond the fatty tissue layer around the kidney, possibly to the adrenal gland or nearby lymph nodes, or to other organs such as the lungs, liver, bones, or brain.
source_span: beyond the layer of fatty tissue around the kidney and may be found in the adrenal gland above the kidney with cancer, or in nearby lymph nodes; or to other organs, such as the lungs, liver, bones, or brain

statement: Five types of standard treatment are used for renal cell cancer: surgery, radiation therapy, chemotherapy, biologic therapy, and targeted therapy.
source_span: Five types of standard treatment are used:         - Surgery     - Radiation therapy     - Chemotherapy     - Biologic therapy     - Targeted therapy

statement: If renal cell cancer spreads to the bone, the disease is called metastatic renal cell cancer, not bone cancer.
source_span: if renal cell cancer spreads to the bone, the cancer cells in the bone are actually cancerous renal cells. The disease is metastatic renal cell cancer, not bone cancer.

statement: Cancer can spread through tissue, the lymph system, and the blood.
source_span: Cancer can spread through tissue, the lymph system, and the blood

statement: Transitional cell cancer of the renal pelvis and ureter is a disease in which malignant cells form in the renal pelvis and ureter.
source_span: Transitional cell cancer of the renal pelvis and ureter is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the renal pelvis and ureter.

statement: Misuse of certain pain medicines can affect the risk of transitional cell cancer of the renal pelvis and ureter.
source_span: Misuse of certain pain medicines can affect the risk of transitional cell cancer of the renal pelvis and ureter.

statement: The kidneys of an adult are about 5 inches long and 3 inches wide and are shaped like a kidney bean.
source_span: The kidneys of an adult are about 5 inches long and 3 inches wide and are shaped like a kidney bean.

statement: Symptoms of transitional cell cancer of the renal pelvis and ureter may include blood in the urine, back pain that doesn't go away, extreme tiredness, unexplained weight loss, and painful or frequent urination.
source_span: Blood in the urine.    - A pain in the back that doesn't go away.    - Extreme tiredness.    -  Weight loss with no known reason.     - Painful or frequent urination.

statement: Diagnostic tests for transitional cell cancer of the renal pelvis and ureter include physical exam and history, urinalysis, ureteroscopy, urine cytology, intravenous pyelogram (IVP), CT scan, ultrasound, MRI, and biopsy.

statement: The prognosis for transitional cell cancer of the renal pelvis and ureter depends on the stage and grade of the tumor.
source_span: The prognosis (chance of recovery) depends on the stage and grade of the tumor.

statement: Treatment options for transitional cell cancer of the renal pelvis and ureter depend on the stage and grade of the tumor, its location, whether the other kidney is healthy, and whether the cancer has recurred.
source_span: The stage and grade of the tumor.    -  Where the tumor is.    - Whether the patient's other kidney is healthy.    - Whether the cancer has recurred.

statement: Most transitional cell cancer of the renal pelvis and ureter can be cured if found early.
source_span: Most transitional cell cancer of the renal pelvis and ureter can be cured if found early.

statement: Ureteroscopy uses a thin, tube-like instrument called a ureteroscope, inserted through the urethra into the bladder, ureter, and renal pelvis, to check for abnormal areas.
source_span: A ureteroscope is a thin, tube-like instrument with a light and a lens for viewing. The ureteroscope is inserted through the urethra into the bladder, ureter, and renal pelvis.

statement: In children and adolescents younger than 15 years old, most kidney cancers are Wilms tumors.
source_span: In children and adolescents younger than 15 years old, most kidney cancers are Wilms tumors.

statement: Renal cell cancer is rare in children and adolescents younger than 15 but is much more common in adolescents between 15 and 19 years old.
source_span: Renal cell cancer is rare in children and adolescents younger than 15 years old. It is much more common in adolescents between 15 and 19 years old.

statement: Rhabdoid tumor of the kidney occurs mostly in infants and young children and grows and spreads quickly, often to the lungs or brain.
source_span: Rhabdoid tumor of the kidney is a type of kidney cancer that occurs mostly in infants and young children ... Rhabdoid tumor of the kidney grows and spreads quickly, often to the lungs or brain.

statement: Children younger than one year old with a SMARCB1 gene change have an ultrasound of the abdomen every two to three months and an ultrasound of the head every month to check for rhabdoid tumor.
source_span: Children younger than one year old have an ultrasound of the abdomen every two to three months and an ultrasound of the head every month.

statement: Children one to four years old with a SMARCB1 gene change have an ultrasound of the abdomen and an MRI of the brain and spine every three months.
source_span: Children one to four years old have an ultrasound of the abdomen and an MRI of the brain and spine every three months.

statement: When clear cell sarcoma of the kidney recurs after treatment, it often recurs in the brain or lung.
source_span: When it recurs (comes back) after treatment, it often recurs in the brain or lung.

statement: Congenital mesoblastic nephroma is often diagnosed during the first year of life and can usually be cured.
source_span: Congenital mesoblastic nephroma is a tumor of the kidney that is often diagnosed during the first year of life. It can usually be cured.

statement: Multilocular cystic nephromas are benign tumors made up of cysts and are most common in infants, young children, and adult women.
source_span: Multilocular cystic nephromas are benign tumors made up of cysts and are most common in infants, young children, and adult women.

statement: Anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney is most common in children or adolescents younger than 15 years of age and often spreads to the lungs, liver, or bones.
source_span: Anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney is a rare tumor that is most common in children or adolescents younger than 15 years of age. Anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney often spreads to the lungs, liver, or bones.

statement: After nephroblastomatosis is found in a kidney removed for Wilms tumor, frequent follow-up testing is important at least every 3 months for at least 7 years after treatment.

statement: Nonmelanoma skin cancers rarely spread to other parts of the body, while melanoma is more likely to invade nearby tissues and spread.
source_span: Nonmelanoma skin cancers rarely spread to other parts of the body. Melanoma is a much rarer type of skin cancer. It is more likely to invade nearby tissues and spread to other parts of the body.

statement: Actinic keratosis is a skin condition that sometimes becomes squamous cell carcinoma.
source_span: Actinic keratosis is a skin condition that sometimes becomes squamous cell carcinoma.

statement: The skin's two main layers are the epidermis (upper/outer layer) and the dermis (lower/inner layer).

statement: Melanocytes are cells found in the lower part of the epidermis that make melanin, the pigment that gives skin its natural color.
source_span: Melanocytes: Cells that make melanin and are found in the lower part of the epidermis. Melanin is the pigment that gives skin its natural color.

statement: Skin cancer is most common in skin that is often exposed to sunlight, such as the face, neck, hands, and arms.

Plasma cell neoplasms are diseases in which the body makes too many plasma cells.
source_span: Plasma cell neoplasms are diseases in which the body makes too many plasma cells.

statement: Plasma cells develop from B lymphocytes (B cells), a type of white blood cell that is made in the bone marrow.
source_span: Plasma cells develop from B lymphocytes (B cells), a type of white blood cell that is made in the bone marrow.

statement: Plasma cells in plasma cell neoplasms make an unneeded antibody protein called M protein.
source_span: The plasma cells also make an antibody protein, called M protein, that is not needed by the body

statement: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) is not cancer but can become cancer.
source_span: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) is not cancer but can become cancer.

statement: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, plasmacytoma, and multiple myeloma are types of plasma cell neoplasms that are cancer.
source_span: The following types of plasma cell neoplasms are cancer: - Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma... - Plasmacytoma. - Multiple myeloma.

statement: In MGUS, less than 10% of the bone marrow is made up of abnormal plasma cells and there is no cancer.
source_span: less than 10% of the bone marrow is made up of abnormal plasma cells and there is no cancer

statement: There are two types of plasmacytoma: isolated plasmacytoma of bone and extramedullary plasmacytoma.
source_span: There are two types of plasmacytoma.

statement: In isolated plasmacytoma of bone, one plasma cell tumor is found in the bone, less than 10% of the bone marrow is plasma cells, and there are no other signs of cancer.
source_span: In isolated plasmacytoma of bone, one plasma cell tumor is found in the bone, less than 10% of the bone marrow is made up of plasma cells, and there are no other signs of cancer.

statement: Plasmacytoma of the bone often becomes multiple myeloma.
source_span: Plasmacytoma of the bone often becomes multiple myeloma.

statement: Extramedullary plasmacytomas commonly form in tissues of the throat, tonsil, and paranasal sinuses.
source_span: Extramedullary plasmacytomas commonly form in tissues of the throat, tonsil, and paranasal sinuses.

statement: In multiple myeloma, abnormal plasma cells (myeloma cells) build up in the bone marrow and form tumors in many bones of the body.
source_span: abnormal plasma cells (myeloma cells) build up in the bone marrow and form tumors in many bones of the body

statement: Smoldering multiple myeloma is multiple myeloma that does not cause any signs or symptoms.
source_span: Sometimes multiple myeloma does not cause any signs or symptoms. This is called smoldering multiple myeloma.

statement: A multiple myeloma tumor can damage bone and cause hypercalcemia (too much calcium in the blood).
source_span: A tumor can damage the bone and cause hypercalcemia (too much calcium in the blood).

statement: Multiple myeloma and other plasma cell neoplasms may cause a condition called amyloidosis.
source_span: Multiple myeloma and other plasma cell neoplasms may cause a condition called amyloidosis.

statement: Signs of amyloidosis include purple spots on the skin, an enlarged tongue, diarrhea, and tingling or numbness in the legs and feet.
source_span: Purple spots on the skin. - Enlarged tongue. - Diarrhea. - Swelling caused by fluid in your body's tissues. - Tingling or numbness in your legs and feet.

statement: Neuroblastoma is a disease in which malignant cells form in neuroblasts (immature nerve tissue) in the adrenal gland, neck, chest, or spinal cord.
source_span: Neuroblastoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in neuroblasts (immature nerve tissue) in the adrenal gland, neck, chest, or spinal cord.

statement: Neuroblastoma often begins in the nerve tissue of the adrenal glands.
source_span: Neuroblastoma often begins in the nerve tissue of the adrenal glands.

statement: There are two adrenal glands, one on top of each kidney in the back of the upper abdomen.
source_span: There are two adrenal glands, one on top of each kidney in the back of the upper abdomen.

statement: Neuroblastoma most often begins in infancy and may be diagnosed in the first month of life.
source_span: Neuroblastoma most often begins in infancy and may be diagnosed in the first month of life.

statement: By the time neuroblastoma is diagnosed, the cancer has usually already metastasized (spread).
source_span: By the time neuroblastoma is diagnosed, the cancer has usually metastasized (spread).

statement: Neuroblastoma spreads most often to the lymph nodes, bones, bone marrow, and liver, and in infants also to the skin.
source_span: Neuroblastoma spreads most often to the lymph nodes, bones, bone marrow, and liver. In infants, it also spreads to the skin.

statement: Gene mutations that increase the risk of neuroblastoma are sometimes inherited from a parent to a child.
source_span: Gene mutations that increase the risk of neuroblastoma are sometimes inherited (passed from the parent to the child).

statement: In children with an inherited gene mutation, neuroblastoma usually occurs at a younger age and more than one tumor may form in the adrenal glands.
source_span: In children with a gene mutation, neuroblastoma usually occurs at a younger age and more than one tumor may form in the adrenal glands.

statement: Common signs of neuroblastoma include a lump in the abdomen, neck, or chest, bulging eyes, dark circles around the eyes, and bone pain.
source_span: Lump in the abdomen, neck, or chest. - Bulging eyes. - Dark circles around the eyes ("black eyes"). - Bone pain.

statement: A higher than normal amount of VMA or HVA in urine catecholamine studies can be a sign of neuroblastoma.
source_span: A higher than normal amount of VMA or HVA can be a sign of neuroblastoma.

statement: In an mIBG scan, radioactive mIBG is injected into a vein and scans may be taken over 1-3 days.
source_span: Scans may be taken over 1-3 days.

statement: mIBG is used in high doses to treat neuroblastoma.
source_span: mIBG is used in high doses to treat neuroblastoma.

statement: Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy involves inserting a hollow needle into the hipbone or breastbone to remove bone marrow, blood, and a small piece of bone.
source_span: The removal of bone marrow, blood, and a small piece of bone by inserting a hollow needle into the hipbone or breastbone.

statement: Neuroblastoma most often begins during early childhood, usually in children younger than 5 years of age.
source_span: Neuroblastoma most often begins during early childhood, usually in children younger than 5 years of age.

statement: Neuroblastoma is the most common type of cancer in infants.
source_span: Neuroblastoma is the most common type of cancer in infants.

statement: The number of new cases of neuroblastoma is greatest among children under 1 year of age.
source_span: The number of new cases of neuroblastoma is greatest among children under 1 year of age.

statement: Neuroblastoma is slightly more common in males than in females.
source_span: Neuroblastoma is slightly more common in males than females.

statement: The risk factors for neuroblastoma are not known.
source_span: The risk factors for neuroblastoma are not known.

statement: In rare cases, neuroblastoma may be found before birth by fetal ultrasound.
source_span: In rare cases, neuroblastoma may be found before birth, by fetal ultrasound.

statement: Neuroblastoma screening carries a risk of overdiagnosis.
source_span: Neuroblastoma may be overdiagnosed.

statement: A false-negative neuroblastoma screening result may cause a person to delay seeking medical care even if symptoms are present.
source_span: A person who receives a false-negative test result (one that shows there is no cancer when there really is) may delay seeking medical care even if there are symptoms.

statement: A false-positive neuroblastoma screening result can cause anxiety and is usually followed by more tests and procedures.
source_span: A false-positive test result (one that shows there is cancer when there really isn't) can cause anxiety and is usually followed by more tests and procedures, which also have risks.

statement: A urine test showing a higher than normal amount of HVA or VMA can lead to tests and treatments for neuroblastoma that may not be needed.
source_span: when a urine test result shows a higher than normal amount of homovanillic acid (HMA) or vanillyl mandelic acid (VMA), tests and treatments for neuroblastoma are likely to be done, but may not be needed

statement: Melanoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in melanocytes, the cells that color the skin.
source_span: Melanoma is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in melanocytes (cells that color the skin).

statement: The number of new cases of melanoma has been increasing over the last 40 years.
source_span: The number of new cases of melanoma has been increasing over the last 40 years.

statement: When melanoma starts in the skin it is called cutaneous melanoma.
source_span: When melanoma starts in the skin, it is called cutaneous melanoma.

statement: When melanoma occurs in the eye it is called intraocular or ocular melanoma.
source_span: When melanoma occurs in the eye, it is called intraocular or ocular melanoma.

statement: In men, melanoma is often found on the trunk or the head and neck; in women, it forms most often on the arms and legs.
source_span: In men, melanoma is often found on the trunk (the area from the shoulders to the hips) or the head and neck. In women, melanoma forms most often on the arms and legs.

statement: Nonmelanoma skin cancers, the most common types of skin cancer, rarely spread to other parts of the body.
source_span: Nonmelanoma skin cancers rarely spread to other parts of the body.

statement: Risk factors for melanoma include fair complexion, long-term natural or artificial sunlight exposure, environmental exposures such as radiation, solvents, vinyl chloride and PCBs, a history of many blistering sunburns, having several large or many small moles, a family history of atypical nevus syndrome, a family or personal history of melanoma, being white, a weakened immune system, and certain gene changes.
source_span: Risk factors for melanoma include the following:...Having a fair complexion...Being exposed to natural sunlight or artificial sunlight...Being exposed to certain factors in the environment...radiation, solvents, vinyl chloride, and PCBs.

statement: Signs of possible melanoma include a mole that changes in size, shape, or color, has irregular edges, is more than one color, is asymmetrical, itches, oozes/bleeds/ulcerates, or new satellite moles growing near an existing mole.
source_span: A mole that: - changes in size, shape, or color. - has irregular edges or borders. - is more than one color. - is asymmetrical...Satellite moles (new moles that grow near an existing mole).

statement: Melanoma is detected and diagnosed using a skin exam and biopsy, in which a pathologist examines removed tissue under a microscope.
source_span: Skin exam: A doctor or nurse checks the skin for moles...Biopsy: A procedure to remove the abnormal tissue and a small amount of normal tissue around it. A pathologist looks at the tissue under a microscope to check for cancer cells.

statement: Abnormal areas of skin should not be shaved off or cauterized because cancer cells that remain may spread.
source_span: It is important that abnormal areas of the skin not be shaved off or cauterized (destroyed with a hot instrument, an electric current, or a caustic substance) because cancer cells that remain may

statement: Merkel cell carcinoma is a very rare disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the skin.
source_span: Merkel cell carcinoma is a very rare disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the skin.

statement: Merkel cell carcinoma is also called neuroendocrine carcinoma of the skin or trabecular cancer.
source_span: Merkel cell carcinoma, also called neuroendocrine carcinoma of the skin or trabecular cancer

statement: Merkel cell carcinoma starts most often in areas of skin exposed to the sun, especially the head and neck, as well as the arms, legs, and trunk.
source_span: Merkel cell carcinoma starts most often in areas of skin exposed to the sun, especially the head and neck, as well as the arms, legs, and trunk.

statement: Merkel cell carcinoma tends to grow quickly and metastasize at an early stage, usually spreading first to nearby lymph nodes and then to distant lymph nodes, skin, lungs, brain, bones, or other organs.
source_span: Merkel cell carcinoma tends to grow quickly and to metastasize (spread) at an early stage. It usually spreads first to nearby lymph nodes and then may spread to lymph nodes or skin in distant parts of the body, lungs, brain, bones, or other organs.

statement: Risk factors for Merkel cell carcinoma include heavy natural sunlight exposure, artificial sunlight such as tanning beds or PUVA therapy for psoriasis, a weakened immune system (e.g. chronic lymphocytic leukemia or HIV infection), immunosuppressive drugs such as after an organ transplant, a history of other cancers, and being older than 50, male, or white.
source_span: Risk factors for Merkel cell carcinoma include the following: - Being exposed to a lot of natural sunlight. - Being exposed to artificial sunlight, such as from tanning beds or psoralen and ultraviolet A (PUVA) therapy for psoriasis. - Having an immune system weakened by disease...- Taking drugs that make the immune system less active...- Having a history of other types of cancer. - Being older than 50 years, male, or white.

statement: Merkel cell carcinoma usually appears as a single lump that is fast-growing, painless, firm and dome-shaped or raised, and red or violet in color.
source_span: Merkel cell carcinoma usually appears on sun-exposed skin as a single lump that is: - Fast-growing. - Painless. - Firm and dome-shaped or raised. - Red or violet in color.

statement: Merkel cell carcinoma is diagnosed using physical exam and history, a full-body skin exam, and a skin biopsy.
source_span: Physical exam and history...Full-body skin exam...Skin biopsy: The removal of skin cells or tissues so they can be viewed under a microscope

statement: Prognosis for Merkel cell carcinoma depends on the stage of cancer, its location in the body, whether it is newly diagnosed or recurred, the patient's age and general health, and how deeply the tumor has grown into the skin.
source_span: The prognosis (chance of recovery) and treatment options depend on the following: - The stage of the cancer...- Where the cancer is in the body. - Whether the cancer has just been diagnosed or has recurred...Prognosis also depends on how deeply the tumor has grown into the skin.

statement: The stages used for Merkel cell carcinoma are Stage 0 (carcinoma in situ), IA, IB, IIA, IIB, IIC, IIIA, IIIB, and IV.
source_span: Stage 0 (carcinoma in situ) Stage IA Stage IB Stage IIA Stage IIB Stage IIC Stage IIIA Stage IIIB Stage IV

statement: Staging tests for Merkel cell carcinoma may include CT scan, MRI, PET scan, and lymph node biopsy including sentinel lymph node biopsy.
source_span: CT scan (CAT scan)...MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)...PET scan (positron emission tomography scan)...Lymph node biopsy: There are two main types of lymph node biopsy used to stage Merkel cell carcinoma...Sentinel lymph node biopsy

statement: Melanoma forms in the melanocytes and is a less common type of skin cancer that grows and spreads quickly.

statement: Parathyroid cancer is a rare disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of a parathyroid gland.
source_span: Parathyroid cancer is a rare disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of a parathyroid gland.

statement: The parathyroid glands are four pea-sized organs found in the neck near the thyroid gland.
source_span: The parathyroid glands are four pea-sized organs found in the neck near the thyroid gland.

statement: The parathyroid glands make parathyroid hormone (PTH), which helps the body use and store calcium to keep blood calcium at normal levels.
source_span: The parathyroid glands make parathyroid hormone (PTH or parathormone). PTH helps the body use and store calcium to keep the calcium in the blood at normal levels.

statement: Hyperparathyroidism is most often caused by a benign tumor called an adenoma, and only very rarely by parathyroid cancer.
source_span: Hyperparathyroidism can occur when a benign tumor (noncancer), called an adenoma, forms on one of the parathyroid glands, and causes it to grow and become overactive. Sometimes hyperparathyroidism can be caused by parathyroid cancer, but this is very rare.

statement: Extra PTH causes hypercalcemia by moving calcium from bones into the blood and increasing intestinal absorption of calcium.
source_span: The extra PTH causes: - The calcium stored in the bones to move into the blood. - The intestines to absorb more calcium from the food we eat... This condition is called hypercalcemia

statement: The hypercalcemia caused by hyperparathyroidism is more serious and life-threatening than parathyroid cancer itself.
source_span: The hypercalcemia caused by hyperparathyroidism is more serious and life-threatening than parathyroid cancer itself and treating hypercalcemia is as important as treating the cancer.

statement: Risk factors for parathyroid cancer include the inherited disorders familial isolated hyperparathyroidism (FIHP) and multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) syndrome.
source_span: Risk factors for parathyroid cancer include the following rare disorders that are inherited (passed down from parent to child): - Familial isolated hyperparathyroidism (FIHP). - Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) syndrome.

statement: Treatment with radiation therapy may increase the risk of developing a parathyroid adenoma.
source_span: Treatment with radiation therapy may increase the risk of developing a parathyroid adenoma.

statement: Signs and symptoms of parathyroid cancer include weakness, feeling tired, and a lump in the neck.
source_span: Signs and symptoms of parathyroid cancer include weakness, feeling tired, and a lump in the neck.

statement: Other signs and symptoms of parathyroid cancer include pain in the abdomen/side/back, bone pain, a broken bone, change in voice such as hoarseness, and trouble swallowing.
source_span: Other signs and symptoms of parathyroid cancer include the following: - Pain in the abdomen, side, or back that doesn't go away. - Pain in the bones. - A broken bone. - A lump in the neck. - Change in voice such as hoarseness. - Trouble swallowing.

statement: A sestamibi scan injects a small amount of the radioactive substance technetium 99 into a vein to find an overactive parathyroid gland.
source_span: A very small amount of a radioactive substance called technetium 99 is injected into a vein and travels through the bloodstream to the parathyroid gland.

statement: Diagnostic procedures for parathyroid cancer include physical exam and history, blood chemistry studies, parathyroid hormone test, sestamibi scan, CT scan, SPECT scan, ultrasound exam, angiogram, and venous sampling.
source_span: Blood chemistry studies... Parathyroid hormone test... Sestamibi scan... CT scan... SPECT scan... Ultrasound exam... Angiogram... Venous sampling

statement: Penile cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the penis.
source_span: Penile cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the penis.

statement: The penis contains two types of erectile tissue: the corpora cavernosa (two columns forming most of the penis) and the corpus spongiosum (single column).
source_span: Corpora cavernosa: The two columns of erectile tissue that form most of the penis. - Corpus spongiosum: The single column of erectile tissue that forms a small portion of the penis.

statement: The corpus spongiosum surrounds the urethra, the tube through which urine and sperm pass from the body.
source_span: The corpus spongiosum surrounds the urethra (the tube through which urine and sperm pass from the body).

statement: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection may increase the risk of developing penile cancer.
source_span: Human papillomavirus infection may increase the risk of developing penile cancer.

statement: Circumcision may help prevent HPV infection, and men who were not circumcised at birth may have a higher risk of developing penile cancer.
source_span: Circumcision may help prevent infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV)... Men who were not circumcised at birth may have a higher risk of developing penile cancer.

statement: Other risk factors for penile cancer include being age 60 or older, having phimosis, poor personal hygiene, having many sexual partners, and using tobacco products.
source_span: Being age 60 or older. - Having phimosis (a condition in which the foreskin of the penis cannot be pulled back over the glans). - Having poor personal hygiene. - Having many sexual partners. - Using tobacco products.

statement: Signs of penile cancer include sores, discharge, and bleeding, as well as redness, irritation on the penis, or a lump on the penis.
source_span: Signs of penile cancer include sores, discharge, and bleeding... Redness, irritation, or a sore on the penis. - A lump on the penis.

statement: Biopsy methods used to diagnose penile cancer include fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy, incisional biopsy, and excisional biopsy.
source_span: Fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy: The removal of tissue or fluid using a thin needle. - Incisional biopsy... - Excisional biopsy

statement: Prognosis and treatment options for penile cancer depend on the stage of the cancer, the location and size of the tumor, and whether the cancer is newly diagnosed or has recurred.
source_span: The prognosis (chance of recovery) and treatment options depend on the following: - The stage of the cancer. - The location and size of the tumor. - Whether the cancer has just been diagnosed or has recurred (come back).

statement: Penile cancer staging uses five stages: Stage 0 (Carcinoma in Situ), Stage I, Stage II, Stage III, and Stage IV.
source_span: The following stages are used for penile cancer: - Stage 0 (Carcinoma in Situ) - Stage I - Stage II - Stage III - Stage IV

statement: A sentinel lymph node biopsy removes the first lymph node likely to receive cancer spread from a tumor, located using a radioactive substance and/or blue dye injected near the tumor.
source_span: The sentinel lymph node is the first lymph node to receive lymphatic drainage from a tumor. It is the first lymph node the cancer is likely to spread to from the tumor. A radioactive substance and/or blue dye is injected near the tumor.

statement: A pituitary tumor is a growth of abnormal cells in the tissues of the pituitary gland.
source_span: A pituitary tumor is a growth of abnormal cells in the tissues of the pituitary gland.

statement: The pituitary gland is a pea-sized organ in the center of the brain, just above the back of the nose, sometimes called the "master endocrine gland."
source_span: Pituitary tumors form in the pituitary gland, a pea-sized organ in the center of the brain, just above the back of the nose. The pituitary gland is sometimes called the "master endocrine gland"

statement: Pituitary tumors are divided into three groups: benign pituitary adenomas, invasive pituitary adenomas, and pituitary carcinomas.
source_span: Pituitary tumors are divided into three groups: - Benign pituitary adenomas... - Invasive pituitary adenomas... - Pituitary carcinomas

statement: Very few pituitary tumors are malignant (pituitary carcinomas).
source_span: Very few pituitary tumors are malignant.

statement: Most pituitary tumors are functioning tumors, which make more than the normal amount of one or more hormones.
source_span: Functioning pituitary tumors make more than the normal amount of one or more hormones. Most pituitary tumors are functioning tumors.

statement: Hormones made by the pituitary gland include prolactin, adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), growth hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone, and luteinizing hormone (LH)/follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).
source_span: Hormones made by the pituitary gland include: - Prolactin... - Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)... - Growth hormone... - Thyroid-stimulating hormone... - Luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)

statement: Risk factors for pituitary tumors include the hereditary diseases multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) syndrome, Carney complex, and isolated familial acromegaly.
source_span: Risk factors for pituitary tumors include having the following hereditary diseases: - Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) syndrome. - Carney complex. - Isolated familial acromegaly.

statement: In adults, too much growth hormone from a pituitary tumor may cause acromegaly, the growth of bones in the face, hands, and feet; in children it may cause excessive overall body growth.
source_span: Too much growth hormone may cause... In adults, acromegaly (growth of the bones in the face, hands, and feet). In children, the whole body may grow much taller and larger than normal.

statement: Signs of a pituitary tumor include problems with vision and certain physical changes.
source_span: Signs of a pituitary tumor include problems with vision and certain physical changes.

statement: Too much ACTH from a pituitary tumor may cause weight gain in the face, neck, and trunk with thin arms and legs, a fat lump on the back of the neck, thin skin with stretch marks, and easy bruising.
source_span: Too much ACTH may cause: - Headache. - Some loss of vision. - Weight gain in the face, neck, and trunk of the body, and thin arms and legs. - A lump of fat on the back of the neck. - Thin skin that may have purple or pink stretch marks on the chest or abdomen. - Easy bruising.
