statement: Small intestine cancer is a rare disease in which malignant cells form in the tissues of the small intestine.
source_span: Small intestine cancer is a rare disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the small intestine.

statement: There are five types of small intestine cancer: adenocarcinoma, sarcoma, carcinoid tumors, gastrointestinal stromal tumor, and lymphoma.
source_span: The types of cancer found in the small intestine are adenocarcinoma, sarcoma, carcinoid tumors, gastrointestinal stromal tumor, and lymphoma.

statement: Adenocarcinoma starts in glandular cells in the lining of the small intestine and is the most common type of small intestine cancer.
source_span: Adenocarcinoma starts in glandular cells in the lining of the small intestine and is the most common type of small intestine cancer.

statement: Most adenocarcinoma tumors of the small intestine occur in the part near the stomach.
source_span: Most of these tumors occur in the part of the small intestine near the stomach.

statement: Leiomyosarcoma starts in the smooth muscle cells of the small intestine.
source_span: Leiomyosarcoma starts in the smooth muscle cells of the small intestine.

statement: Most leiomyosarcoma tumors occur in the part of the small intestine near the large intestine.
source_span: Most of these tumors occur in the part of the small intestine near the large intestine.

statement: Risk factors for small intestine cancer include eating a high-fat diet, having Crohn disease, having celiac disease, and having familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP).
source_span: Risk factors for small intestine cancer include the following: - Eating a high-fat diet. - Having Crohn disease. - Having celiac disease. - Having familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP).

statement: Signs and symptoms of small intestine cancer include pain or cramps in the middle of the abdomen, unexplained weight loss, a lump in the abdomen, and blood in the stool.
source_span: Pain or cramps in the middle of the abdomen. - Weight loss with no known reason. - A lump in the abdomen. - Blood in the stool.

statement: Capsule endoscopy involves swallowing a pill-sized capsule with a light and tiny wireless camera that sends pictures to a recorder worn around the waist or shoulder, and the capsule passes out of the body during a bowel movement.
source_span: A capsule that is about the size of a large pill and contains a light and a tiny wireless camera is swallowed by the patient...sends many pictures of the inside of the digestive tract to a recorder that is worn around the waist or over the shoulder...The capsule passes out of the body during a bowel movement.

statement: Double balloon endoscopy uses a special instrument made of two tubes, one inside the other, inserted through the mouth or rectum into the small intestine.
source_span: A special instrument made up of two tubes (one inside the other) is inserted through the mouth or rectum and into the small intestine.

statement: Thymoma and thymic carcinoma are diseases in which malignant cells form on the outside surface of the thymus.
source_span: Thymoma and thymic carcinoma are diseases in which malignant (cancer) cells form on the outside surface of the thymus.

statement: The thymus is a small organ in the upper chest under the breastbone, is part of the lymph system, and makes lymphocytes that protect the body against infections.
source_span: The thymus, a small organ that lies in the upper chest under the breastbone, is part of the lymph system. It makes white blood cells, called lymphocytes, that protect the body against infections.

statement: Thymoma tumor cells grow slowly and rarely spread beyond the thymus, whereas thymic carcinoma cells grow more quickly and have usually spread to other parts of the body by the time the cancer is found.
source_span: The tumor cells in a thymoma look similar to the normal cells of the thymus, grow slowly, and rarely spread beyond the thymus...the tumor cells in a thymic carcinoma...grow more quickly, and have usually spread to other parts of the body when the cancer is found.

statement: Autoimmune diseases linked with thymoma include myasthenia gravis, acquired pure red cell aplasia, hypogammaglobulinemia, polymyositis, lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, thyroiditis, and Sjögren syndrome.
source_span: They include: - Myasthenia gravis. - Acquired pure red cell aplasia. - Hypogammaglobulinemia. - Polymyositis. - Lupus erythematosus. - Rheumatoid arthritis. - Thyroiditis. - Sjgren syndrome.

statement: Signs and symptoms of thymoma and thymic carcinoma include a cough that doesn't go away, chest pain, and trouble breathing.
source_span: Check with your doctor if you have any of the following: - A cough that doesn't go away. - Chest pain. - Trouble breathing.

statement: A fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy uses a thin needle to remove a sample of cells, while a core biopsy uses a wide needle.
source_span: using a thin needle to remove a sample of cells. This is called a fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy. Sometimes a wide needle is used to remove a sample of cells and this is called a core biopsy.

statement: Prognosis and treatment options for thymoma and thymic carcinoma depend on the stage of the cancer, the type of cancer cell, whether the tumor can be removed completely by surgery, the patient's general health, and whether the cancer is newly diagnosed or recurred.
source_span: The prognosis (chance of recovery) and treatment options depend on the following: - The stage of the cancer. - The type of cancer cell. - Whether the tumor can be removed completely by surgery. - The patient's general health. - Whether the cancer has just been diagnosed or has recurred (come back).

statement: Thymoma is staged using four stages: Stage I, Stage II, Stage III, and Stage IV.
source_span: The following stages are used for thymoma: - Stage I - Stage II - Stage III - Stage IV

statement: Cancer can spread through tissue, the lymph system, and the blood.
source_span: Cancer can spread through tissue, the lymph system, and the blood

statement: Urethral cancer is a disease in which malignant cells form in the tissues of the urethra.
source_span: Urethral cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the urethra.

statement: In women the urethra is about 1½ inches long and lies just above the vagina; in men it is about 8 inches long and goes through the prostate gland and the penis.
source_span: In women, the urethra is about 1 inches long and is just above the vagina. In men, the urethra is about 8 inches long, and goes through the prostate gland and the penis to the outside of the body.

statement: Urethral cancer is a rare cancer that occurs more often in men than in women.
source_span: Urethral cancer is a rare cancer that occurs more often in men than in women.

statement: Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common type of urethral cancer.
source_span: Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common type of urethral cancer.

statement: Transitional cell carcinoma of the urethra forms in the area near the urethral opening in women, and in the part of the urethra that goes through the prostate gland in men.
source_span: Transitional cell carcinoma forms in the area near the urethral opening in women, and in the part of the urethra that goes through the prostate gland in men.

statement: Risk factors for urethral cancer include a history of bladder cancer and conditions causing chronic urethral inflammation, including sexually transmitted diseases such as HPV (especially HPV type 16) and frequent urinary tract infections.
source_span: Risk factors for urethral cancer include the following: - Having a history of bladder cancer. - Having conditions that cause chronic inflammation in the urethra, including: - Sexually transmitted diseases (STDs), including human papillomavirus (HPV), especially HPV type 16. - Frequent urinary tract infections (UTIs).

statement: Signs of urethral cancer include bleeding or trouble with urination, and there may be no signs or symptoms in the early stages.
source_span: Signs of urethral cancer include bleeding or trouble with urination...There may be no signs or symptoms in the early stages.

statement: Urethral cancer can metastasize quickly to tissues around the urethra and is often found in nearby lymph nodes by the time it is diagnosed.
source_span: Urethral cancer can metastasize (spread) quickly to tissues around the urethra and is often found in nearby lymph nodes by the time it is diagnosed.

statement: A ureteroscope is a thin, tube-like instrument with a light and lens that is inserted through the urethra into the bladder, ureter, and renal pelvis to check for abnormal areas.
source_span: A ureteroscope is a thin, tube-like instrument with a light and a lens for viewing. The ureteroscope is inserted through the urethra into the bladder, ureter, and renal pelvis.

statement: An accessory navicular bone is a small bone located in the middle of the foot, near the navicular bone.
source_span: An accessory navicular bone is a small bone located in the middle of the foot. It is near the navicular bone

statement: Accessory navicular bone is estimated to occur in approximately 2 to 12% of the general population.
source_span: estimated to be in approximately 2 to 12% of the general population

statement: Accessory navicular bone occurs in up to 14% of children.
source_span: up to 14% of children

statement: This bone may develop a bump that can cause irritation, swelling, and pain.
source_span: This bone may develop a bump that can cause irritation, swelling, and pain.

statement: Symptoms of accessory navicular bone may worsen with increased activity or tight shoes.
source_span: Symptoms may worsen with increased activity or tight shoes.

statement: The cause of accessory navicular bone is unknown, but may be related to flatfoot (pes planus) or repeated foot and ankle sprains.
source_span: the condition may be related to the development of flatfoot also known as pes planus, in other cases it may be related to repeated foot and ankle sprains

statement: In children, accessory navicular bone symptoms usually resolve once the child stops growing.
source_span: In children the condition usually resolves once the child stops growing.

statement: For people with severe symptoms, surgery may be considered to remove the bony growth.
source_span: For people with accessory navicular bone who experience severe symptoms surgery may be considered to remove the bony growth.

statement: Treatments for accessory navicular bone may include NSAIDs such as ibuprofen, moleskin padding, or immobilizing the area with a cast for six weeks.
source_span: non-steroidal anti-inflammatories (NSAIDs) such as ibuprofen, placing a doughnut-shaped piece of moleskin around the affected area to relieve pain and tenderness, or immobilizing the area with a cast for six weeks

statement: Aceruloplasminemia is a disorder of iron metabolism that causes iron to build up in the body.
source_span: Aceruloplasminemia is a disorder of iron metabolism. This disorder causes iron to build-up in the body.

statement: People with aceruloplasminemia tend to develop anemia and diabetes in their 20's.
source_span: People with this disorder tend to develop anemia and diabetes in their 20's.

statement: As aceruloplasminemia progresses, movement problems such as tremors, chorea, ataxia, eyelid twitching, and grimacing are common.
source_span: movement problems are common, such as tremors, chorea, ataxia, eyelid twitching, and grimacing

statement: Some people with aceruloplasminemia experience psychiatric problems and dementia in their 40's and 50's.
source_span: Some experience psychiatric problems and dementia in their 40's and 50's.

statement: Aceruloplasminemia is caused by mutations in the CP gene and is inherited in an autosomal recessive fashion.
source_span: Aceruloplasminemia is caused by mutations in the CP gene and are inherited in an autosomal recessive fashion.

statement: Abnormal renal physiology, abnormality of iron homeostasis, anemia, chorea, diabetes mellitus, retinopathy, and tremor each occur in about 90% of people with aceruloplasminemia.
source_span: Abnormal renal physiology 90% Abnormality of iron homeostasis 90% Anemia 90% Chorea 90% Diabetes mellitus 90% Retinopathy 90% Tremor 90%

statement: People with aceruloplasminemia tend to have low serum copper (<10 ug/dL), low serum iron (<45 ug/dL), high serum ferritin (850-4000 ng/mL), and absent serum ceruloplasmin concentration.
source_span: People with aceruloplasminemia tend to have low serum copper (<10 ug/dL), low serum iron (< 45 ug/dL), high serum ferritin (850-4000 ng/mL) and absent serum ceruloplasmin concentration.

statement: Aceruloplasminemia should be suspected when a person has more than one of: diabetes mellitus, retinal degeneration, anemia, and movement disorder.
source_span: When a person has more than one of the following symptoms, aceruloplasminemia should be suspected: Diabetes mellitus Retinal degeneration Anemia Movement disorder

statement: Diagnosis of aceruloplasminemia can be further supported by MRI and pathology results demonstrating iron deposition in the body.
source_span: Diagnosis can be further supported by MRI and pathology results demonstrating iron deposition in the body.

statement: Achalasia is typically diagnosed in individuals between 25 and 60 years of age.
source_span: Achalasia is typically diagnosed in individuals between 25 and 60 years of age.

statement: Achalasia symptoms are caused by damage to the nerves of the esophagus, though the exact etiology is unknown.
source_span: The exact etiology is unknown, however, symptoms are caused by damage to the nerves of the esophagus.

statement: When a genetic influence is suspected, achalasia is called familial esophageal achalasia.
source_span: When a genetic influence is suspected, achalasia is called familial esophageal achalasia.

statement: Most people with achalasia experience difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) and heartburn.
source_span: Most people with achalasia experience difficulty swallowing, also known as dysphagia and heartburn.

statement: Other achalasia symptoms include regurgitation/vomiting, noncardiac chest pain, odynophagia, upper abdominal pain, coughing/asthma, chronic aspiration, hoarseness/sore throat, and unintentional weight loss.
source_span: regurgitation or vomiting, noncardiac chest pain, odynophagia (painful swallowing), and pain in the upper central region of the abdomen. Non esophageal symptoms might include: coughing or asthma, chronic aspiration ... hoarseness or sore throat, and unintentional weight loss

statement: The diagnosis of achalasia is confirmed by manometry, though upper endoscopy and upper GI X-ray can also be useful.
source_span: The diagnosis of achalasia is confirmed by manometry (test that measures how well the esophagus is working); however, other tests such as upper endoscopy and upper GI X-ray can additionally be useful.

statement: Achalasia treatment includes Botox injection (temporary), medications like isosorbide dinitrate or nifedipine, Heller myotomy surgery, and pneumatic balloon dilation.
source_span: Injection with botulinum toxin (Botox) ... Medications, such as long-acting nitrates (i.e. isosorbide dinitrate) or calcium channel blockers (i.e. nifedipine) ... Surgery (Heller myotomy) ... Pneumatic balloon dilation of the esophagus

statement: Vulvar cancer is a rare disease in which malignant cells form in the tissues of the vulva.
source_span: Vulvar cancer is a rare disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the vulva.

statement: Vulvar cancer most often affects the outer vaginal lips; less often it affects the inner vaginal lips, clitoris, or vaginal glands.
source_span: Vulvar cancer most often affects the outer vaginal lips. Less often, cancer affects the inner vaginal lips, clitoris, or vaginal glands.

statement: Vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN) is a condition where abnormal cells grow on the surface of the vulvar skin and can become vulvar cancer.
source_span: This condition is called vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN). Because it is possible for VIN to become vulvar cancer, it is very important to get treatment.

statement: Risk factors for vulvar cancer include having vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN), HPV infection, and a history of genital warts.
source_span: Risk factors for vulvar cancer include the following: - Having vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN). - Having human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. - Having a history of genital warts.

statement: Other possible risk factors for vulvar cancer include having many sexual partners, first sexual intercourse at a young age, and a history of abnormal Pap tests.
source_span: Having many sexual partners. - Having first sexual intercourse at a young age. - Having a history of abnormal Pap tests (Pap smears).

statement: Signs of vulvar cancer include bleeding or itching.
source_span: Signs of vulvar cancer include bleeding or itching.

statement: Symptoms checked by a doctor include a lump or growth on the vulva, skin color/texture changes, persistent itching, bleeding not related to menstruation, and tenderness in the vulvar area.
source_span: A lump or growth on the vulva. - Changes in the vulvar skin... Bleeding not related to menstruation (periods). - Tenderness in the vulvar area.

statement: Vulvar cancer is diagnosed using a physical exam and history, and a biopsy of vulvar tissue.
source_span: Physical exam and history... Biopsy : The removal of samples of cells or tissues from the vulva so they can be viewed under a microscope...

statement: Prognosis and treatment options for vulvar cancer depend on the stage of the cancer, the patient's age and general health, and whether the cancer is newly diagnosed or recurrent.
source_span: The prognosis (chance of recovery) and treatment options depend on the following: - The stage of the cancer. - The patient's age and general health. - Whether the cancer has just been diagnosed or has recurred (come back).

statement: Vulvar cancer is classified into four stages: Stage I, Stage II, Stage III, and Stage IV.
source_span: The following stages are used for vulvar cancer: - Stage I - Stage II - Stage III - Stage IV

statement: Staging tests for vulvar cancer may include pelvic exam, colposcopy, cystoscopy, proctoscopy, and X-rays.
source_span: Pelvic exam... Colposcopy... Cystoscopy... Proctoscopy... X-rays

statement: Recurrent vulvar cancer is cancer that has come back after treatment, either in the vulva or in other parts of the body.
source_span: Recurrent vulvar cancer is cancer that has recurred (come back) after it has been treated. The cancer may come back in the vulva or in other parts of the body.

statement: Abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) occur in the part of the aorta that passes through the abdomen and are most common in men between 50 and 80 years of age.
source_span: Abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) are aneurysms that occur in the part of the aorta that passes through the abdomen... are most common in men between 50 and 80 years of age.

statement: About 20% of AAAs eventually rupture and are often fatal.
source_span: About 20% of AAAs eventually rupture and are often fatal.

statement: Some people with an AAA experience a pulsing sensation in the abdomen and/or pain in the back.
source_span: some people have a pulsing sensation in the abdomen and/or pain in the back.

statement: If an AAA ruptures it may cause deep, severe pain, nausea, vomiting, fast heart rate, clammy skin, and/or shock.
source_span: If the aneurysm ruptures, it may cause deep, severe pain; nausea; vomiting; fast heart rate; clammy skin; and/or shock.

statement: Treatment for AAA depends on the size of the aneurysm and may include blood pressure medications or surgery to repair it.
source_span: Treatment depends on the size of the aneurysm and may include blood pressure medications, or surgery to repair the aneurysm.

statement: When more than one family member is affected by AAA, it may be considered 'familial abdominal aortic aneurysm.'
source_span: When more than one family member is affected, it may be considered "familial abdominal aortic aneurysm."

statement: AAA is thought to be a multifactorial condition where one or more genes interact with environmental factors.
source_span: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is thought to be a multifactorial condition, meaning that one or more genes likely interact with environmental factors to cause the condition.

statement: A Swedish survey found the relative risk of developing AAA for a first-degree relative of an affected person was approximately double that of someone with no family history.
source_span: A Swedish survey reported that the relative risk of developing AAA for a first-degree relative of a person with AAA was approximately double that of a person with no family history of AAA.

statement: In another study, having a family history of AAA increased the risk of having an aneurysm 4.3-fold.
source_span: In another study, having a family history increased the risk of having an aneurysm 4.3-fold.

statement: The highest AAA risk was among brothers older than age 60, where the prevalence was 18%.
source_span: The highest risk was among brothers older than age 60, in whom the prevalence was 18%.

statement: AAA can occur with inherited single-gene disorders such as Marfan syndrome and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, vascular type, though these more typically involve the thoracoabdominal aorta.
source_span: It can occur with some inherited disorders that are caused by mutations in a single gene, such as Marfan syndrome and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, vascular type. However, these more typically involve the thoracoabdominal aorta.

statement: Abetalipoproteinemia is characterized by the inability to fully absorb dietary fats, cholesterol, and fat-soluble vitamins.
source_span: Abetalipoproteinemia is a condition characterized by the inability to fully absorb dietary fats, cholesterol and fat-soluble vitamins.

statement: Signs and symptoms of abetalipoproteinemia appear in the first few months of life and include failure to thrive, diarrhea, acanthocytosis, and stool abnormalities.
source_span: Signs and symptoms appear in the first few months of life and can include failure to thrive; diarrhea; acanthocytosis; and stool abnormalities.

statement: Later childhood features of abetalipoproteinemia include slower intellectual development, poor muscle coordination, progressive ataxia, and retinitis pigmentosa.
source_span: Other features develop later in childhood and often impair the function of the nervous system, potentially causing slower intellectual development; poor muscle coordination; progressive ataxia; and an eye disorder called retinitis pigmentosa.

statement: Most symptoms of abetalipoproteinemia are due to defects in the absorption and transport of vitamin E.
source_span: Most of the symptoms are due to defects in the absorption and transport of vitamin E.

statement: Abetalipoproteinemia is caused by mutations in the MTTP gene and is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner.
source_span: Abetalipoproteinemia is caused by mutations in the MTTP gene and is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner.

statement: Early diagnosis, high-dose vitamin E therapy, and medium-chain fatty acid supplements may slow the progression of the nervous system abnormalities in abetalipoproteinemia.
source_span: Early diagnosis, high-dose vitamin E therapy, and medium-chain fatty acid supplements may slow the progression of the nervous system abnormalities.

statement: If left untreated, abetalipoproteinemia can result in early death.
source_span: If left untreated, the condition can result in early death.

statement: Vision deterioration in abetalipoproteinemia is gradual and often leads to blindness by the fourth decade of life.
source_span: gradual deterioration of vision, often leading to blindness in the fourth decade of life

statement: Malabsorption occurs in approximately 90% of people with abetalipoproteinemia.
source_span: Malabsorption 90%

statement: When two carriers of abetalipoproteinemia have children, each child has a 25% chance of being affected, a 50% chance of being an unaffected carrier, and a 25% chance of being unaffected and not a carrier.
source_span: each child has a: 25% (1 in 4) chance to be affected 50% (1 in 2) chance to be an unaffected carrier like each parent 25% chance to be unaffected and not be a carrier

statement: The MTTP gene provides instructions to make a protein needed for creating beta-lipoproteins, which are necessary for absorbing and transporting fats, cholesterol, and fat-soluble vitamins.
source_span: The MTTP gene gives the body instructions to make a protein needed for creating beta-lipoproteins. These lipoproteins are necessary for the body to absorb fats, cholesterol, and fat-soluble vitamins.

statement: Treatment for abetalipoproteinemia involves very large doses of vitamin E, additional fat-soluble vitamin supplements (A, D, K), and linoleic acid supplements.
source_span: Treatment involves very large doses of vitamin E, as well as large doses of vitamin supplements containing other fat-soluble vitamins (vitamin A, vitamin D, and vitamin K). Linoleic acid supplements are also recommended.

statement: Achondrogenesis is a group of severe disorders, present from birth, that affect the development of cartilage and bone.
source_span: Achondrogenesis is a group of severe disorders that are present from birth and affect the development of cartilage and bone.

statement: There are at least three forms of achondrogenesis: type 1A, type 1B, and type 2.
source_span: There are at least three forms of achondrogenesis, type 1A, type 1B and type 2

statement: Type 1A and type 1B achondrogenesis are both inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
source_span: Type 1A and 1B achondrogenesis are both inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.

statement: Type 1B achondrogenesis may be caused by mutations in the SLC26A2 gene.
source_span: Type 1B may be caused by mutations in the SLC26A2 gene.

statement: Type 2 achondrogenesis is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern and is caused by new (de novo) mutations in the COL2A1 gene.
source_span: Type 2 achondrogenesis is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern and is caused by new (de novo) mutations in the COL2A1 gene.

statement: The genetic cause of achondrogenesis type 1A remains unknown.
source_span: The genetic cause of achondrogenesis type 1A remains unknown.

statement: The SLC26A2 gene provides instructions for a protein important for normal cartilage development and for converting cartilage to bone.
source_span: The SLC26A2 gene provides instructions for making a protein that is important for the normal development of cartilage and for the conversion of cartilage to bone.

statement: The COL2A1 gene provides instructions for a protein that forms a type of collagen found mostly in cartilage and in the vitreous of the eyeball.
source_span: The COL2A1 gene provides instructions for making a protein that forms a type of collagen found mostly in cartilage and in the clear gel that fills the eyeball (vitreous).

statement: Achondrogenesis type 2 is almost always caused by new (de novo) mutations and typically occurs in people with no family history of the disorder.
source_span: It is almost always caused by new (de novo) mutations and typically occurs in people with no history of the disorder in their family.

statement: Achondroplasia is caused by mutations in the FGFR3 gene.
source_span: Achondroplasia is caused by mutations in the FGFR3 gene.

statement: Achondroplasia is inherited in an autosomal dominant fashion.
source_span: It is inherited in an autosomal dominant fashion.

statement: About 80% of individuals with achondroplasia have parents of normal stature and are born with the condition as a result of a new (de novo) gene mutation.
source_span: About 80% of individuals who have achondroplasia have parents with normal stature and are born with the condition as a result of a new (de novo) gene alteration (mutation).

statement: Each individual with achondroplasia has a 50% chance, with each pregnancy, of passing on the mutated gene.
source_span: Each individual with achondroplasia has a 50% chance, with each pregnancy, to pass on the mutated gene.

statement: Two specific mutations in the FGFR3 gene are responsible for almost all cases of achondroplasia.
source_span: Two specific mutations in the FGFR3 gene are responsible for almost all cases of achondroplasia.

statement: In babies, apnea occurs when breathing stops for more than 15 seconds.
source_span: In babies, apnea occurs when breathing stops for more than 15 seconds.

statement: A speech evaluation is recommended by age two years for children with achondroplasia.
source_span: Speech evaluation by age two years

statement: Recommendations for managing children with achondroplasia were outlined by the American Academy of Pediatrics Committee on Genetics.
source_span: Recommendations for management of children with achondroplasia were outlined by the American Academy of Pediatrics Committee on Genetics.

statement: Acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis is also known as Sweet syndrome.
source_span: Acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis - also known as Sweet syndrome

statement: It is a skin condition marked by fever, arthritis, and painful skin lesions that appear mainly on the face, neck, back and arms.
source_span: a skin condition marked by fever, inflammation of the joints (arthritis), and painful skin lesions that appear mainly on the face, neck, back and arms

statement: Middle-aged women are most likely to develop the condition, though it may also affect men, older adults, and infants.
source_span: Although middle-aged women are most likely to develop this condition, it may also affect men, older adults and even infants.

statement: Most often the condition is not serious and will clear on its own within a few months.
source_span: Most often, it isn't serious and will clear on its own in a few months.

statement: Doctors usually prescribe systemic corticosteroids, such as prednisone or prednisolone, to treat this condition.
source_span: Doctors usually prescribe systemic corticosteroids (prednisone or prednisolone) to treat this condition.

statement: With medication, skin lesions can improve within two or three days, with the worst lesions disappearing within one to four weeks.
source_span: Medications can improve skin lesions and associated symptoms in just two or three days, with the worst of the lesions disappearing within one to four weeks.

statement: Left untreated, the condition (when not associated with a more serious disease) may disappear on its own within one to three months.
source_span: Left untreated, acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis not associated with a more serious condition may disappear on its own within one to three months.

statement: The condition can be a sign of an immune response linked to acute myelogenous leukemia, inflammatory bowel disease, bowel or breast cancer, pregnancy, or rheumatoid arthritis, among others.
source_span: Blood disorders, especially acute myelogenous leukemia, a cancer of the blood and bone marrow Inflammatory bowel disease, such as ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease Bowel or breast cancer Pregnancy Rheumatoid arthritis

statement: Certain medications, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), can trigger the condition.
source_span: Certain medications, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)

statement: Acute intermittent porphyria (AIP) is one of the liver (hepatic) porphyrias, caused by low levels of porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD), an enzyme also called hydroxymethylbilane synthase.
source_span: Acute intermittent porphyria (AIP) is one of the liver (hepatic) porphyrias. AIP is caused by low levels of porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD), an enzyme also often called hydroxymethylbilane synthase.

statement: Activating factors such as hormones, drugs, and dietary changes may trigger AIP symptoms.
source_span: activating factors such as hormones, drugs, and dietary changes may trigger symptoms

statement: Symptomatic AIP individuals typically present with abdominal pain with nausea.
source_span: symptomatic individuals typically present with abdominal pain with nausea

statement: AIP symptoms usually appear after puberty, and activating factors include alcohol, drugs (e.g., barbiturates, steroids, sulfa-containing antibiotics), chemicals, smoking, reduced caloric intake, stress, and travel.
source_span: Those individuals that present with symptoms usually do so after puberty, probably because of hormonal influences, although other activating factors include: alcohol, drugs (e.g., barbiturates, steroids, sulfa-containing antibiotics), chemicals, smoking, reduced caloric intake, stress, and travel.

statement: AIP symptoms usually last several days, but attacks that are not treated promptly may last weeks or months.
source_span: Symptoms usually last several days, but attacks for which treatment is not received promptly may last weeks or months.

statement: Individuals with AIP have an increased risk of developing hepatocellular carcinoma, and some develop kidney failure.
source_span: Individuals with AIP have an increased risk of developing hepatocellular carcinoma; some develop kidney failure.

statement: Abdominal pain occurs in about 90% of AIP patients according to HPO data.
source_span: Abdominal pain 90%

statement: AIP is caused by deficiency of PBGD due to a mutation in the HMBS gene, which is the only gene known to be associated with AIP.
source_span: The deficiency of PBGD is caused by a mutation in the HMBS gene. The HMBS gene is the only gene known to be associated with AIP.

statement: AIP is inherited in an autosomal dominant fashion, meaning only one of the two HMBS genes needs a disease-causing mutation to decrease enzyme activity and cause symptoms.
source_span: AIP is inherited in an autosomal dominant fashion, which means only one of the two HMBS genes needs to have a disease-causing mutation to decrease enzyme activity and cause symptoms.

statement: Diagnosis of an acute porphyria such as AIP is established by finding increased levels of delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG) in urine.
source_span: The finding of increased levels of delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG) in urine establishes that one of the acute porphyrias is present.

statement: Molecular genetic testing of the HMBS gene detects more than 98% of affected individuals and is available in clinical laboratories.
source_span: Molecular genetic testing of the HMBS gene detects more than 98% of affected individuals and is available in clinical laboratories.

statement: Panhematin, an intravenous medication used to correct heme deficiency, may be prescribed to treat AIP.
source_span: Panhematin, an intravenous medication used to correct heme deficiency, may also be prescribed.

statement: Cancer of the appendix is very rare and is typically found incidentally during appendectomies, in about 1% of cases.
source_span: Cancer of the appendix is very rare and is typically found incidentally during appendectomies, in about 1% of the cases.

statement: According to a National Cancer Institute report using the SEER database, appendix cancers account for about 0.4% of gastrointestinal tumors.
source_span: According to a report published by the National Cancer Institute, using the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, appendix cancer account for about 0.4% of gastrointestinal tumors.

statement: The carcinoid type is the most common subtype of appendix cancer, accounting for 66% of the total.
source_span: The most common is the carcinoid type (66% of the total)

statement: Cyst-adenocarcinoma accounts for 20% and adenocarcinoma accounts for 10% of appendix cancer subtypes.
source_span: with cyst-adenocarcinoma accounting for 20% and adenocarcinoma accounting for 10%

statement: Signet cell carcinoma of the appendix is the rarer subtype, involving only 4% of all appendix cancer subtypes.
source_span: signet cell carcinoma of appendix (which is the rarer involving only 4% of all the subtypes of appendix cancer)

statement: Rare forms of appendix cancer include adenocarcinoid, signet ring, non-Hodgkins lymphoma, ganglioneuroma, and pheochromocytoma.
source_span: rare forms of cancers which include adenocarcinoid, signet ring, non-Hodgkins lymphoma, ganglioneuroma, and pheochromocytoma

statement: The most common clinical symptom of adenocarcinoma of the appendix is acute appendicitis.
source_span: The most common clinical symptom is acute appendicitis.

statement: Other symptoms of adenocarcinoma of the appendix include a palpable abdominal mass, ascites, peritonitis due to a perforated appendix, bloating, vague abdominal pain, and tenderness.
source_span: Other symptoms include a palpable abdominal mass, ascites (fluid buildup), peritonitis (inflammation of the membrane lining the abdominal cavity) due to a perforated appendix, and non-specific gastrointestinal or genitourinary symptoms such as bloating, vague abdominal pain, and tenderness.

statement: Mucinous adenocarcinomas of the appendix may be found incidentally as a right sided cystic mass on an imaging study.
source_span: Mucinous adenocarcinomas may also be found incidentally as a right sided cystic mass on an imaging study.

statement: Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) is a rare form of adenocarcinoma, which is cancer that begins in glandular tissues.
source_span: Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) is a rare form of adenocarcinoma, which is cancer that begins in gladular tissues.

statement: ACC most commonly arises in the head and neck, in the major and minor salivary glands including the palate, nasopharynx, lining of the mouth, larynx, or trachea.
source_span: ACC most commonly arises in the head and neck, in various parts of the major and minor salivary glands including the palate, nasopharynx, lining of the mouth, voice box (larynx) or windpipe (trachea).

statement: ACC can also occur in the breast, uterus, or other locations in the body.
source_span: It can also occur in the breast, uterus, or other locations in the body.

statement: Early symptoms of ACC may include lumps under the lining of the mouth or facial skin, numbness in the mouth or face, difficulty swallowing, hoarseness, pain, or paralysis of a facial nerve.
source_span: Early symptoms depend on the tumor's location and may include lumps under the lining of the mouth or facial skin; numbness in the mouth or face; difficulty swallowing; hoarseness; pain; or paralysis of a facial nerve.

statement: ACC spreads along nerves or through the bloodstream, and only spreads to the lymph nodes in about 5-10% of cases.
source_span: ACC spreads along nerves or through the bloodstream, and only spreads to the lymph nodes in about 5-10% of cases.

statement: The cause of ACC is currently unknown, and no strong genetic or environmental risk factors specific to ACC have been identified.
source_span: The cause of ACC is currently unknown. ... no strong genetic or environmental risk factors specific to ACC have been identified.

statement: Treatment of ACC depends on many factors and may include surgery, radiation, and/or chemotherapy.
source_span: Treatment depends on many factors and may include surgery, radiation, and/or chemotherapy.

statement: Only one case of apparent familial ACC has been reported worldwide, involving a father and daughter both affected with ACC of the sublingual salivary gland.
source_span: only one case of apparent familial ACC has been reported worldwide. In this case, a father and daughter were both affected with ACC of the sublingual salivary gland.

statement: There has been one reported case of ACC of the salivary gland occurring in a person with basal cell nevus syndrome, a hereditary tumor-predisposition syndrome.
source_span: There has also been one report of a case of ACC of the salivary gland occurring in a person with basal cell nevus syndrome, a hereditary syndrome known to predispose affected people to a very wide range of tumors.

statement: Adult-onset Still's disease is an inflammatory condition characterized by high fevers, rash, sore throat, and joint pain.
source_span: an inflammatory condition characterized by high fevers, rash, sore throat, and joint pain

statement: Still's disease was named after English doctor George Still, who described the condition in children in 1896.
source_span: named after an English doctor named George Still, who described the condition in children in 1896

statement: Still's disease occurring in children under age 16 is now known as systemic onset juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (JRA).
source_span: Still's disease which occurs in children (those under the age of 16) is now known as systemic onset juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (JRA)

statement: In 1971, the term "adult Still's disease" was used to describe adults with a condition similar to systemic onset JRA.
source_span: In 1971, the term "adult Still's disease" was used to describe adults who had a condition similar to systemic onset JRA

statement: The cause of adult-onset Still's disease is unknown and no risk factors for the disease have been identified.
source_span: The cause of adult-onset Still's disease is unknown. No risk factors for the disease have been identified

statement: There is no cure for adult-onset Still's disease, though treatment may offer symptom relief and help prevent complications.
source_span: There's no cure for adult-onset Still's disease; however, treatment may offer symptom relief and help prevent complications

statement: Some hypothesize adult-onset Still's disease results from or is triggered by a virus or other infectious agent, while others believe it is a hypersensitive or autoimmune disorder, with no conclusive evidence for either.
source_span: Some hypothesize that the condition results from or is triggered by a virus or other infectious agent. Others believe that it is a hypersensitive or autoimmune disorder. To date, no conclusive evidence has been found

statement: Adult-onset vitelliform macular dystrophy (AVMD) is an eye disorder affecting the macula that can cause progressive vision loss.
source_span: AVMD affects an area of the retina called the macula, which is responsible for sharp central vision

statement: Signs and symptoms of AVMD usually begin between ages 30 and 50 and include blurred and/or distorted vision that can progress to central vision loss.
source_span: Signs and symptoms usually begin between ages 30 and 50 and include blurred and/or distorted vision, which can progress to central vision loss over time

statement: AVMD has historically been characterized as caused by mutations in the PRPH2, BEST1, IMPG1, and IMPG2 genes.
source_span: AVMD has been characterized as a genetic disorder caused by mutations in the PRPH2, BEST1, IMPG1, and IMPG2 genes

statement: AVMD is additionally suspected to be associated with a single-nucleotide polymorphism in the HTRA1 gene, which is also associated with age-related macular degeneration.
source_span: it is additionally suspected that AVMD might be associated with a single-nucleotide polymorphism (variant DNA sequence) in the HTRA1 gene. Single-nucleotide polymorphisms in the HTRA1 gene are additionally associated with age-related macular degeneration

statement: When AVMD is caused by a known mutation inherited in an autosomal dominant manner, a person has a 50% chance with each pregnancy of passing along the altered gene to their child.
source_span: a person with adult-onset macular dystrophy (AVMD) has a 50% chance with each pregnancy of passing along the altered gene to his or her child

statement: Management of AVMD includes a comprehensive eye examination, including dilation, once or twice a year.
source_span: Management for this condition should include a comprehensive eye examination, including dilation, once or twice a year

statement: Intravitreal injections of either Ranibizumab or Bevacizumab may be effective in the short-term for AVMD, and transcorneal electrical stimulation has been found to improve visual acuity.
source_span: Intravitreal injections of either Ranibizumab or Bevacizumab may be effective in the short-term. Transcorneal electrical stimulation has also been found to improve visual acuity

statement: Afibrinogenemia is an inherited blood disorder in which the blood does not clot normally due to a deficiency of fibrinogen (factor I).
source_span: an inherited blood disorder in which the blood does not clot normally. It occurs when there is a lack (deficiency) of a protein called fibrinogen (or factor I)

statement: Afibrinogenemia is thought to be transmitted as an autosomal recessive trait.
source_span: Afibrinogenemia is thought to be transmitted as an autosomal recessive trait

statement: In afibrinogenemia, fibrinogen levels are less than 0.1 g/L, with bleeding manifestations ranging from mild to severe.
source_span: with fibrinogen levels less than 0.1 g/L, bleeding manifestations range from mild to severe

statement: Umbilical cord hemorrhage frequently provides an early alert to afibrinogenemia.
source_span: Umbilical cord hemorrhage frequently provides an early alert to the abnormality

statement: Afibrinogenemia can result from mutations in one of the fibrinogen genes alpha (FGA), beta (FGB), or gamma (FGG).
source_span: This defect in fibrinogen synthesis can result from mutations in one or another of the fibrinogen genes alpha (FGA), beta (FGB) or gamma (FGG)

statement: Afibrinogenemia is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner, requiring inheritance of two abnormal genes, one from each parent.
source_span: Afibrinogenemia is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner, meaning that in order to be affected, an individual must have inherited two abnormal genes, one from each parent

statement: Treatment for bleeding episodes in afibrinogenemia may include plasma or a blood product containing concentrated fibrinogen (cryoprecipitate) given via transfusion.
source_span: patients may receive: The liquid portion of the blood (plasma) A blood product containing concentrated fibrinogen (cryoprecipitate) through a vein (transfusion)

statement: Individuals with afibrinogenemia should be vaccinated with the hepatitis B vaccine because transfusion increases the risk of hepatitis.
source_span: Vaccination with the hepatitis B vaccine because transfusion increases the risk of hepatitis

statement: Adenylosuccinase deficiency is caused by mutations in the ADSL gene and is inherited in an autosomal recessive fashion.
source_span: Adenylosuccinase deficiency is caused by mutations in the ADSL gene and is inherited in an autosomal recessive fashion.

statement: Adenylosuccinase deficiency results from a lack of the enzyme adenylosuccinate lyase.
source_span: results from a lack of the enzyme adenylosuccinate lyase

statement: Seizures are observed in 60 percent of affected individuals and may begin within the first month of life.
source_span: Seizures are observed in 60 percent of affected individuals.

statement: Growth delay has been observed in 30 percent of affected individuals in the first years of life, mainly related to feeding problems.
source_span: growth delay has been observed in 30 percent of affected individuals, mainly related to feeding problems

statement: Autism has been found to be present in one-third of cases of adenylosuccinase deficiency.
source_span: Autism has been found to be present in one-third of cases.

statement: There are currently no effective therapies for adenylosuccinase deficiency; treatment is supportive based on specific features.
source_span: At the current time, there are no effective therapies for the treatment of adenylosuccinase deficiency. Treatment is supportive based on the specific features.

statement: Almost all affected individuals experience delayed motor milestones ranging from mild to severe.
source_span: Almost all affected individuals experience delayed motor milestones ranging from mild to severe.

statement: Adiposis dolorosa is characterized by the growth of multiple, painful lipomas (benign, fatty tumors).
source_span: growth of multiple, painful, lipomas (benign, fatty tumors)

statement: Adiposis dolorosa usually occurs in obese, post-menopausal women, but it can also occur in men.
source_span: It usually occurs in obese, post-menopausal women, but it can also occur in men.

statement: Most cases of adiposis dolorosa are sporadic (not inherited), but a few familial cases with autosomal dominant inheritance have been reported.
source_span: Most cases are sporadic (not inherited) but a few familial cases with autosomal dominant inheritance have been reported.

statement: Arthralgia (joint pain) occurs in approximately 90% of adiposis dolorosa patients.
source_span: Arthralgia 90%

statement: Obesity occurs in approximately 90% of adiposis dolorosa patients.
source_span: Obesity 90%

statement: In familial autosomal dominant cases of adiposis dolorosa, each child of an affected person has a 50% (1 in 2) risk of inheriting the gene causing the condition.
source_span: each child has a 50% (1 in 2) risk to inherit the gene causing the condition

statement: Clinical genetic testing for adiposis dolorosa is currently not available because no specific associated gene has been identified.
source_span: Clinical genetic testing for adiposis dolorosa is currently not available.

statement: Treatments for adiposis dolorosa pain may include prednisone or intravenous lidocaine, and no drug is known to change the course of the disease.
source_span: prednisone or intravenous lidocaine for pain traditional pain medicines ... There is currently no drug known to change the course of the disease.

statement: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis is an abnormal curvature of the spine that appears in late childhood or adolescence, usually in an elongated 's' or 'C' shape with twisted/rotated spinal bones.
source_span: an abnormal curvature of the spine that appears in late childhood or adolescence

statement: Severe and progressive spinal curves occur more frequently in girls than in boys, for unknown reasons.
source_span: severe and progressive curves occur more frequently in girls than in boys

statement: The cause of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis is unknown, but it likely involves both genetic and environmental factors.
source_span: The cause of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis is unknown. It is likely that there are both genetic and environmental factors involved.

statement: Treatment of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis may include observation, bracing, and/or surgery.
source_span: Treatment may include observation, bracing and/or surgery.

statement: Common signs of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis include a tilt or unevenness in the shoulders, hips, or waist, or one leg appearing longer than the other.
source_span: the most common signs of the condition include a tilt or unevenness (asymmetry) in the shoulders, hips, or waist, or having one leg that appears longer than the other

statement: Having a close relative, such as a parent or sibling, with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis increases a child's risk of developing it.
source_span: having a close relative (such as a parent or sibling) with the condition increases a child's risk of developing it

statement: Scoliosis curves progress most during the patient's rapid growth period, i.e., the adolescent or pre-adolescent growth spurt.
source_span: Curves progress most during the rapid growth period of the patient (adolescent or pre-adolescent growth spurt).

statement: Agenesis of the dorsal pancreas is a congenital malformation in which either the entire dorsal pancreas or part of it fails to develop (complete or partial agenesis).
source_span: a congenital malformation of the pancreas in which either the entire dorsal pancreas or part of the dorsal pancreas fails to develop (complete agenesis or partial agenesis, respectively)

statement: Hyperglycemia has been shown to be present in approximately 50% of individuals with agenesis of the dorsal pancreas.
source_span: Hyperglycemia has been shown to be present in approximately 50% of affected individuals.

statement: Symptoms of agenesis of the dorsal pancreas can include hyperglycemia, diabetes mellitus, bile duct obstruction, abdominal pain, and pancreatitis.
source_span: others may develop hyperglycemia, diabetes mellitus, bile duct obstruction, abdominal pain, pancreatitis, or other conditions

statement: Agenesis of the dorsal pancreas may occur sporadically, or in some cases with suggested autosomal dominant or X-linked dominant inheritance.
source_span: It may occur in individuals with no history of the condition in the family (sporadically) and in some cases, autosomal dominant or X-linked dominant inheritance has been suggested.

statement: Agenesis of the dorsal pancreas has been reported to occur with the very rare conditions polysplenia and polysplenia/heterotaxy syndrome.
source_span: It has also been reported to occur with very rare conditions including polysplenia and polysplenia/heterotaxy syndrome.

statement: Agenesis of the dorsal pancreas results from failure of the dorsal pancreatic bud to form the body and tail of the pancreas during fetal development.
source_span: Partial or complete agenesis of the dorsal pancreas results from the failure of the dorsal pancreatic bud to form the body and tail of the pancreas in the developing fetus.

statement: When associated with polysplenia/heterotaxy syndrome, agenesis of the dorsal pancreas may be linked with benign to severe congenital cardiac malformations.
source_span: it may occur due to errors in development of the asymmetric organs and may be associated with benign to severe congenital cardiac (heart) malformations

statement: During pancreatitis attacks, individuals should avoid pain medications such as acetaminophen that can affect the liver.
source_span: avoiding pain medications that can affect the liver (such as acetaminophen)

statement: Albright's hereditary osteodystrophy is caused by mutations in the GNAS gene and is transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait.
source_span: This autosomal dominantly inherited condition is caused by mutations in the GNAS gene.

statement: Albright's hereditary osteodystrophy features include short stature, obesity, round face, subcutaneous ossifications, and brachydactyly (shortening and widening of the bones in the hands and feet).
source_span: a syndrome with a wide range of manifestations including short stature, obesity, round face, subcutaneous (under the skin) ossifications (gradual replacement of cartilage by bone), and characteristic shortening and widening of the bones in the hands and feet (brachydactyly)

statement: Albright's hereditary osteodystrophy is associated with resistance to parathyroid hormone (pseudohypoparathyroidism) and to other hormones, particularly thyroid-stimulating hormone.
source_span: The features of Albright's hereditary osteodystrophy are associated with resistance to parathyroid hormone (pseudohypoparathyroidism) and to other hormones (thyroid-stimulation hormone, in particular).

statement: Treatment of Albright's hereditary osteodystrophy consists of calcium and vitamin D supplements.
source_span: Treatment consists of calcium and vitamin D supplements.

statement: Phosphate binders such as calcium carbonate, calcium acetate, and sevelamer HCl may be used to lower high blood phosphate levels in Albright's hereditary osteodystrophy.
source_span: medications called phosphate binders to help lower the levels of phosphate. Examples of phosphate binders include calcium carbonate, calcium acetate, and sevelamer HCl.

statement: Alopecia universalis is characterized by complete loss of hair on the scalp and body and is an advanced form of alopecia areata.
source_span: Alopecia universalis (AU) is a condition characterized by the complete loss of hair on the scalp and body. It is an advanced form of alopecia areata

statement: Alopecia universalis is thought to be an autoimmune condition in which the immune system mistakenly attacks the hair follicles.
source_span: it is thought to be an autoimmune condition in which an affected person's immune system mistakenly attacks the hair follicles

statement: Roughly 20% of people with alopecia universalis have a family member with alopecia, suggesting genetic factors may contribute.
source_span: Roughly 20% of affected people have a family member with alopecia, suggesting that genetic factors may contribute to the development of AU.

statement: There is currently no cure for alopecia universalis, but hair regrowth sometimes occurs on its own, even after many years.
source_span: There is currently no cure for AU, but sometimes hair regrowth occurs on it's own, even after many years.

statement: About 40% of people treated with topical immunotherapy will regrow scalp hair after about six months of treatment.
source_span: About 40% of people treated with topical immunotherapy will regrow scalp hair after about six months of treatment.

statement: Diagnosis of alopecia universalis is usually based on signs and symptoms; a scalp biopsy is rarely needed to confirm it.
source_span: A diagnosis of alopecia universalis is usually based on the signs and symptoms present in each person. In rare cases, a scalp biopsy may be needed to confirm the diagnosis.

statement: Regrown hair from corticosteroid treatment is likely to fall out again when the corticosteroids are stopped.
source_span: regrown hair is likely to fall out when the corticosteriods are stopped

statement: Alport syndrome is a genetic condition characterized by kidney disease, hearing loss, and eye abnormalities.
source_span: Alport syndrome is a genetic condition characterized by kidney disease, hearing loss, and eye abnormalities.

statement: Most affected individuals experience progressive loss of kidney function, usually resulting in end-stage kidney disease.
source_span: Most affected individuals experience progressive loss of kidney function, usually resulting in end-stage kidney disease.

statement: People with Alport syndrome frequently develop sensorineural hearing loss in late childhood or early adolescence.
source_span: People with Alport syndrome also frequently develop sensorineural hearing loss in late childhood or early adolescence.

statement: The eye abnormalities seen in Alport syndrome seldom lead to vision loss.
source_span: The eye abnormalities seen in this condition seldom lead to vision loss.

statement: About 80% of Alport syndrome cases are inherited in an X-linked manner and caused by mutations in the COL4A5 gene.
source_span: In 80% of cases, Alport syndrome is inherited in an X-linked manner and is caused by mutations in the COL4A5 gene.

statement: The remaining Alport syndrome cases may be inherited in an autosomal recessive or autosomal dominant manner and are caused by mutations in the COL4A3 or COL4A4 genes.
source_span: In the remaining cases, it may be inherited in either an autosomal recessive or autosomal dominant manner and caused by mutations in the COL4A3 or COL4A4 genes.

statement: Treatment for Alport syndrome may include use of a hearing aid, hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis for end-stage renal failure, and kidney transplantation.
source_span: Treatment may include use of a hearing aid; hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis to treat those with end-stage renal failure; and kidney transplantation.

statement: In males, one altered copy of the COL4A5 gene in each cell is sufficient to cause kidney failure and other severe symptoms of Alport syndrome.
source_span: In males (who have only one X chromosome), one altered copy of the COL4A5 gene in each cell is sufficient to cause kidney failure and other severe symptoms of the disorder.

statement: In females, a mutation in only one copy of the COL4A5 gene usually only results in hematuria, though some women experience more severe symptoms.
source_span: In females (who have two X chromosomes), a mutation in only one copy of the COL4A5 gene usually only results in hematuria, but some women experience more severe symptoms.

statement: Fathers cannot pass X-linked traits, such as the X-linked form of Alport syndrome, to their sons.
source_span: A characteristic of X-linked inheritance is that fathers cannot pass X-linked traits to their sons.

statement: Type IV collagen is an important component of the organ of Corti, an inner ear structure that transforms sound waves into nerve impulses for the brain.
source_span: Type IV collagen is also an important component of the organ of Corti, an inner ear structure that transforms sound waves into nerve impulses for the brain.

statement: ACE inhibitors can help reduce proteinuria and the progression of kidney disease in Alport syndrome.
source_span: Research suggests that ACE inhibitors can help reduce proteinuira and the progression of kidney disease.

statement: About 10% of Alport syndrome patients who receive a kidney transplant develop nephritis in the graft.
source_span: some studies have reported that about 10% of transplanted patients develop nephritis in the graft

statement: Hearing loss in Alport syndrome is likely to be permanent.
source_span: Loss of hearing is likely to be permanent.

statement: Young men with Alport syndrome should use hearing protection in noisy environments.
source_span: Young men with Alport syndrome should use hearing protection in noisy environments.

statement: Glomerulopathy, retinopathy, and sensorineural hearing impairment each occur in approximately 90% of people with Alport syndrome.
source_span: Glomerulopathy 90% Retinopathy 90% Sensorineural hearing impairment 90%

statement: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) causes a deficiency or absence of the alpha-1 antitrypsin (AAT) protein in the blood.
source_span: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) is a disorder that causes a deficiency or absence of the alpha-1 antitrypsin (AAT) protein in the blood.

statement: AAT is made in the liver and sent through the bloodstream to the lungs to protect them from damage.
source_span: AAT is made in the liver and sent through the bloodstream to the lungs, to protect the lungs from damage.

statement: AATD is caused by mutations in the SERPINA1 gene.
source_span: AATD is caused by mutations in the SERPINA1 gene

statement: AATD is inherited in a codominant manner.
source_span: is inherited in a codominant manner

statement: In adults, AATD symptoms may include shortness of breath, reduced ability to exercise, wheezing, respiratory infections, fatigue, vision problems, and weight loss.
source_span: In adults, symptoms may include shortness of breath; reduced ability to exercise; wheezing; respiratory infections; fatigue; vision problems; and weight loss.

statement: Rarely, AATD can cause a skin condition called panniculitis.
source_span: Rarely, AATD can cause a skin condition called panniculitis.

statement: Emphysema occurs in approximately 90% of people with AATD.
source_span: Emphysema 90%

statement: Hepatic failure occurs in approximately 90% of people with AATD.
source_span: Hepatic failure 90%

statement: Cirrhosis occurs in approximately 5% of people with AATD.
source_span: Cirrhosis 5%

statement: The severity of AATD may be worsened by environmental factors such as exposure to tobacco smoke, dust, and chemicals.
source_span: The severity of AATD may also be worsened by environmental factors such as exposure to tobacco smoke, dust, and chemicals.

statement: Diagnosis of AATD is confirmed by a blood test showing a low serum concentration of AAT, plus either isoelectric focusing or SERPINA1 gene mutation testing on both gene copies.
source_span: Confirming the diagnosis involves a blood test showing a low serum concentration of the alpha-1 antitrypsin (AAT) protein, and either: detecting a functionally deficient AAT protein variant by isoelectric focusing (a method for detecting mutations); or detecting SERPINA1 gene mutations on both copies of the gene

statement: Intravenous augmentation therapy has been recommended for people with established fixed airflow obstruction, determined by a specific lung function test.
source_span: Intravenous augmentation therapy...has been recommended for people with established fixed airflow obstruction (determined by a specific lung function test).

statement: Liver transplantation is the definitive treatment for advanced liver disease in AATD.
source_span: Liver transplantation is the definitive treatment for advanced liver disease.

statement: All people with severe AATD should have pulmonary function tests every 6 to 12 months.
source_span: All people with severe AATD should have pulmonary function tests every 6 to 12 months.

statement: Yearly vaccinations against influenza and pneumococcus are recommended, along with vaccination against hepatitis A and B, for people with AATD.
source_span: Yearly vaccinations against influenza and pneumococcus are recommended to lessen the progression of lung disease. Vaccination against hepatitis A and B is recommended to lessen the risk of liver disease.

statement: Alpha-thalassemia is a blood disorder that reduces the body's production of hemoglobin.
source_span: Alpha-thalassemia is a blood disorder that reduces the body's production of hemoglobin.

statement: Hb Bart syndrome is the more severe type of alpha-thalassemia, while HbH disease is the milder form.
source_span: the more severe type is known as Hb Bart syndrome; the milder form is called HbH disease.

statement: Hb Bart syndrome may be characterized by hydrops fetalis, severe anemia, hepatosplenomegaly, heart defects, and abnormalities of the urinary system or genitalia.
source_span: Hb Bart syndrome may be characterized by hydrops fetalis; severe anemia; hepatosplenomegaly; heart defects; and abnormalities of the urinary system or genitalia.

statement: Most babies with Hb Bart syndrome are stillborn or die soon after birth.
source_span: Most babies with this condition are stillborn or die soon after birth.

statement: HbH disease may cause mild to moderate anemia, hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, or bone changes.
source_span: HbH disease may cause mild to moderate anemia; hepatosplenomegaly; jaundice; or bone changes.

statement: Alpha-thalassemia typically results from deletions involving the HBA1 and HBA2 genes.
source_span: Alpha-thalassemia typically results from deletions involving the HBA1 and HBA2 genes.

statement: No treatment is effective for Hb Bart syndrome, but for HbH disease occasional red blood cell transfusions may be needed.
source_span: No treatment is effective for Hb Bart syndrome. For HbH disease, occasional red blood cell transfusions may be needed.

statement: There are 4 alleles total (2 from the HBA1 gene and 2 from the HBA2 gene) that produce alpha-globin.
source_span: there are 4 alleles that produce alpha-globin

statement: A person with 1 mutated alpha-globin allele is a carrier and has no signs or symptoms.

statement: One principle for structuring state is to group related state, merging two state variables into one if they always change together.
source_span: **Group related state.** If you always update two or more state variables at the same time, consider merging them into a single state variable.

statement: A second principle is to avoid contradictions in state, since state that can disagree with itself leaves room for mistakes.
source_span: **Avoid contradictions in state.** When the state is structured in a way that several pieces of state may contradict and "disagree" with each other, you leave room for mistakes.

statement: A third principle is to avoid redundant state — information calculable from props or existing state during rendering shouldn't be stored in state.
source_span: **Avoid redundant state.** If you can calculate some information from the component's props or its existing state variables during rendering, you should not put that information into that component's state.

statement: A fourth principle is to avoid duplication in state, since duplicated data across state variables is hard to keep in sync.
source_span: **Avoid duplication in state.** When the same data is duplicated between multiple state variables, or within nested objects, it is difficult to keep them in sync.

statement: A fifth principle is to avoid deeply nested state, preferring a flat structure since deeply hierarchical state is inconvenient to update.
source_span: **Avoid deeply nested state.** Deeply hierarchical state is not very convenient to update. When possible, prefer to structure state in a flat way.

statement: In the feedback form example, the isSending and isSent boolean state variables are replaced with a single status variable that can be 'typing', 'sending', or 'sent'.
source_span: it is better to replace them with one `status` state variable that may take one of *three* valid states:** `'typing'` (initial), `'sending'`, and `'sent'`

statement: The reason for replacing isSending/isSent with status is that isSending and isSent should never be true at the same time.
source_span: Since `isSending` and `isSent` should never be `true` at the same time, it is better to replace them with one `status` state variable

statement: If a state variable is an object, you cannot update only one field in it without explicitly copying the other fields; e.g., calling setPosition({x: 100}) would lose the y property entirely.
source_span: you can't do `setPosition({ x: 100 })` in the above example because it would not have the `y` property at all!

statement: To update only x in an object state, you should either do setPosition({...position, x: 100}) or split into two state variables and call setX(100).
source_span: you would either do `setPosition({ ...position, x: 100 })`, or split them into two state variables and do `setX(100)`

2. **Opt-in with "use memo"** - Only compile components that explicitly opt in
3. **Runtime gating** - Control compilation with feature flags

statement: React event handlers are functions triggered in response to interactions like clicking, hovering, and focusing form inputs.
source_span: Event handlers are your own functions that will be triggered in response to interactions like clicking, hovering, focusing form inputs, and so on.

statement: To add an event handler, you define a function and pass it as a prop to the JSX tag, e.g. onClick={handleClick}.
source_span: Add `onClick={handleClick}` to the `<button>` JSX.

statement: By convention, event handler functions are named 'handle' followed by the event name, such as handleClick or handleMouseEnter.
source_span: it is common to name event handlers as `handle` followed by the event name. You'll often see `onClick={handleClick}`, `onMouseEnter={handleMouseEnter}`

statement: Writing onClick={handleClick()} (with parentheses) is incorrect because it calls the function immediately during rendering rather than passing it to fire on click.
source_span: the `()` at the end of `handleClick()` fires the function *immediately* during [rendering], without any clicks.

statement: Writing <button onClick={alert('You clicked me!')}> causes the alert to fire on every component render, not on click.
source_span: This alert fires when the component renders, not when clicked!

statement: Because event handlers are declared inside components, they have access to the component's props, as shown by AlertButton calling alert(message) using its message prop.
source_span: Because event handlers are declared inside of a component, they have access to the component's props. Here is a button that, when clicked, shows an alert with its `message` prop

statement: In the example, PlayButton passes handlePlayClick as the onClick prop to its child Button, and UploadButton passes () => alert('Uploading!') as the onClick prop to its child Button.
source_span:
`PlayButton` passes `handlePlayClick` as the `onClick` prop to the `Button` inside.
- `UploadButton` passes `() => alert('Uploading!')` as the `onClick` prop to the `Button` inside.

statement: React comes with several built-in Hooks including useState, useContext, and useEffect.

statement: You add a ref to a component by importing the useRef Hook from React.
source_span: import { useRef } from 'react';

statement: useRef takes the initial value you want to reference as its only argument, e.g. useRef(0).
source_span: const ref = useRef(0);

statement: useRef returns an object like { current: 0 } holding the value passed to it.
source_span: current: 0 // The value you passed to useRef

statement: A ref's current value is accessed via ref.current and is intentionally mutable, meaning you can both read and write to it.
source_span: You can access the current value of that ref through the `ref.current` property. This value is intentionally mutable, meaning you can both read and write to it.

statement: Changing a ref does not cause the component to re-render, unlike setting state.
source_span: Changing a ref does not!

statement: useState(initialValue) returns the current value of a state variable and a state setter function, unlike useRef which returns only an object with a current property.
source_span: `useState(initialValue)` returns the current value of a state variable and a state setter function ( `[value, setValue]`)

statement: You shouldn't read or write a ref's current value during rendering, whereas you can read state at any time.
source_span: You shouldn't read (or write) the `current` value during rendering.

statement: The React linter verifies that every reactive value (like props and state) read by an Effect is included in that Effect's dependency list.

statement: Unnecessary dependencies may cause an Effect to run too often, or even create an infinite loop.

statement: Reactive values include props and all variables and functions declared directly inside the component body.

statement: Displaying UI in React involves three steps: triggering a render, rendering the component, and committing changes to the DOM.
source_span:
1. **Triggering** a render (delivering the guest's order to the kitchen)
2. **Rendering** the component (preparing the order in the kitchen)
3. **Committing** to the DOM (placing the order on the table)

statement: There are two reasons a component renders: it's the component's initial render, or the component's (or an ancestor's) state has been updated.
source_span: It's the component's **initial render.**... The component's (or one of its ancestors') **state has been updated.**

statement: The initial render is triggered by calling createRoot with the target DOM node and then calling its render method with the component.
source_span: it's done by calling [`createRoot`](/reference/react-dom/client/createRoot) with the target DOM node, and then calling its `render` method with your component

statement: Updating a component's state with the set function automatically queues a render.
source_span: Updating your component's state automatically queues a render.

statement: "Rendering" means React calling your components.
source_span: **"Rendering" is React calling your components.**

statement: On the initial render React calls the root component; for subsequent renders React calls the function component whose state update triggered the render.
source_span:
On initial render, React will call the root component.
* **For subsequent renders,** React will call the function component whose state update triggered the render.

statement: Rendering must always be a pure calculation: given the same inputs a component must return the same JSX, and it must not change objects or variables that existed before rendering.
source_span: Rendering must always be a [pure calculation]... * **Same inputs, same output.**... * **It minds its own business.**

statement: In Strict Mode, React calls each component's function twice to help surface mistakes caused by impure functions.
source_span: When developing in "Strict Mode", React calls each component's function twice, which can help surface mistakes caused by impure functions.

statement: During a re-render, React calculates which properties have changed since the previous render but doesn't act on that information until the commit phase.
source_span: During a re-render, React will calculate which of their properties, if any, have changed since the previous render. It won't do anything with that information until the next step, the commit phase.

statement: Event handlers only re-run when the same interaction is performed again, while Effects re-synchronize whenever a value they read (like a prop or state variable) differs from the last render.
source_span: Event handlers only re-run when you perform the same interaction again. Unlike event handlers, Effects re-synchronize if some value they read, like a prop or a state variable, is different from what it was during the last render.
